News.title: Storm Boelo leaves 90,000 without power as Met Office issues new wind warning
News.content:
A clean-up operation is under way in parts of the UK after Storm Boelo caused flooding and property damage, leaving thousands without power.

The Energy Networks Association (ENA) said around 90,000 properties are still without power as of Monday.

Two men were killed by falling trees during the storm on Sunday - a man in his 20s in north London and a 60-year-old in Dumfries and Galloway.

The Met Office has issued a yellow warning for strong winds from 18:00 on Monday to 03:00 on Tuesday across the west coast of England, Wales and Scotland and eastern parts of Northern Ireland.

Another yellow warning kicks in from 03:00 across northern parts of Scotland.

The Met Office has warned that further power cuts in areas covered by the warning are likely and people should make sure they have essentials prepared, including torches and batteries.

Coastal communities could also be affected by spray or large waves, while travel delays are expected.

Boelo is the second storm to have hit parts of the UK in recent days, following Storm Austen which brought similar levels of disruption.

Leo Slade, CEO of the ENA said it had been "a tough weekend" and that efforts to reconnect some properties were being hampered by the weather, with sustained winds of 50-85mph across parts of Scotland and northern England.

"Until that weather system passes, we can't safely get engineers out to replace poles, to get wires back up, so today is going to be a hive of activity in getting engineers out into the field," Slade told BBC Radio 4's Today programme.

He stressed that the UK's power network was very resilient money was spent to prepare for these sorts of scenarios, but said a debate was needed over how much more investment was required to mitigate for further storms brought by climate change.

News.title: Healey to shield low-income pensioners from income tax in the Budget
News.content:
The chancellor's allies argue his plans for pensioners will mean they do not need to face an administrative burden just to pay a small amount of tax.

More specific details, including how many pensioners this will affect, have yet to be confirmed by the Treasury.

The Budget is due to be printed this evening, with Healey's speech likely to be fine-tuned right up until it is delivered on Wednesday lunchtime.

Treasury sources concede it will not involve the scale of tax and spending announcements seen from Labour and Conservative governments in recent years.

The Tories are calling on the chancellor to cut green taxes, red tape and benefits to bring down energy bills.

Reform is recommending the chancellor adopts 60 policies which they claim will create jobs - including approving the controversial Rosebank oil field - a project Healey is understood to back.

Liberal Democrat Treasury spokeswoman Daisy Cooper has called on the government to agree a new growth and defence partnership with the EU, including joining the single market. She argued this would help "ease the huge tax burden weighing people down".

The Green Party has urged Healey to use his first Budget to "make the UK affordable", including by funding energy bill support by ending a tax relief for data centres.

Senior Green politicians, including leader Zack Polanski, MPs and peers, made clear their suggestions in a letter to Healey.

News.title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month
News.content:
Consultant doctors in England are to stage a two-day strike next month in a dispute over pay and working conditions.

The walkout will begin on 25 November at 06:59 GMT, with consultants staffing emergency care only.

This is known as Christmas Day cover and is likely to have a major impact on most routine and elective or planned services.

The announcement comes after talks had been taking place with the government over the past month, following the vote in favour of strike action by British Medical Association members in July.

Consultants â the most senior doctors in the NHS â were given a 3.5% pay increase this year.

But the BMA argues pay has fallen by a quarter over the past 17 years, once inflation is taken into account.

The union also wants a reduction in the standard working week, from 40 to 35 hours, and higher pay for out-of-hours work, alongside changes to pensions, including greater flexibility over when they can be taken.

News.title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home
News.content:
A woman has described her "phenomenal" relief after she won a legal case that means she is entitled to be paid for caring for her elderly mother in her final years.

Bern Rogers, from Bristol, told the BBC of the "harrowing and deeply sad" family dispute since her elderly mother Sheila died in 2020, which even led to her facing criminal charges.

Legal experts said the "hugely significant" High Court ruling would lead to other claims.

The executor of Sheila's estate, Bern's brother Andrew, said it had "always been willing to pay" her "genuine expenses" and an extra amount for her efforts. But the estate intends to appeal against the judgment that awarded Bern Â£127,500 for care she provided.

News.title: Knighting Sinfield 'easiest decision anyone's had to make,' says Prince William
News.content:
The Prince of Wales has said awarding a knighthood to rugby league star Sir Kevin Sinfield "was probably the easiest decision anyone's ever had to make".

Speaking to BBC Breakfast, Prince William spoke about his personal admiration for Sir Kevin, who recently completed seven ultra marathons in seven days.

It was his latest endurance challenge to raise money for Motor Neurone Disease (MND) charities following the death of his friend and former team-mate, Rob Burrow, from the condition in 2024.

"I think frankly he should have been Sir Kevin years ago," said Prince William.

"What Kevin does, is he can bind and glue communities together by being that leader. The more Kevs we have in this country the better."

The Prince and Princess of Wales were in Wakefield in West Yorkshire last month to see for themselves just how gruelling the seven ultramarathon challenge was.

William and Catherine surprised Sir Kevin as he completed the third of the marathons.

"I don't know how he keeps going, I'm worried about his knees, I'm worried about his hips. The guy is just a machine," Prince William told the BBC.

News.title: Funding set to double for plan to get rough sleepers off streets by Christmas
News.content:
Funding is set to double to support a pledge by the prime minister to give every rough sleeper in England a route off the streets by Christmas.

Ending rough sleeping was one of Andy Burnham's first promises when he entered Downing Street, announcing a Â£442m package to provide emergency accommodation and practical support.

Ahead of the first Rough Sleeping Summit at Downing Street on Monday, No 10 has indicated a further Â£432m will be added to the initiative in Wednesday's Budget.

Shadow housing secretary Katie Lam said rough sleeping had hit "record highs under Labour" and criticised Burnham for failing to end rough sleeping when he was the Mayor of Greater Manchester.

The most recent official figures estimated there were 4,793 people sleeping rough, external on a single night in autumn 2025 in England.

The government's commitment is that every rough sleeper will either be able to physically move into accommodation by Christmas or will have been offered support as a way to prevent them sleeping rough.

Money being added to the pot this week will extend support beyond March 2027 to the end of this Parliament, taking total investment to Â£874m.

Burnham told ITV's Good Morning Britain he was confident it could be done, saying: "I have this strong feeling about putting the right standards at the heart of the country again and we can't get to a position where we just become used to walking past people sleeping rough: it's about care for people."

He added: "In the end, actually, it's cheaper to do that than to leave people sleeping rough going in and out of A&E, that's not good for anybody."

News.title: Israelis prepare to vote in one of the most pivotal elections in the country's history
News.content:
Israeli voters are preparing to head to the polls in an election some have described as the most consequential in the country's history.

It's the first general election since the Hamas-led attacks of 7 October 2023. Tuesday's vote could see Benjamin Netanyahu's almost two-decade-long period of right-wing rule replaced by a more left-leaning government.

Emerging as Netanyahu's main challenger is Gadi Eisenkot, a former military chief of staff, who says the election is about Israel's identity as a liberal and tolerant democracy.

Netanyahu has made security central to his campaign, warning that electing his rivals would risk making Israel less safe.

Middle East correspondent Lucy Williamson reports.

News.title: Healey's Budget needs to sustain the stronger economy through gathering clouds
News.content:
There have been almost no Budget leaks.

The chancellor's aides are using intelligence-style security measures to guard its secrets: the Budget has been split into "compartments" with very few given access to all of them. There are codenames. The IT has been locked down and ministers viewing the plans have to sign a digital promise not to brief media.

Such security is a response to the feeling that speculation around the last Budget, sometimes informed by insiders, was economically destabilising.

As a recent former defence secretary, Chancellor John Healey has embraced such strict procedures, and has approached most of his public engagements and interviews with a sturdy refusal to break the Budget omertÃ , akin to his fellow Yorkshireman Geoffrey Boycott's at times ultra-defensive stance on a cricket pitch.

The economic news has been good - growth has been better than expected and the International Monetary Fund has endorsed the UK for "standing out" among the G7 countries for at least planning to cut borrowing.

News.title: Dead whale found washed up on beach in storm
News.content:
People have been warned to keep away from a dead whale which has washed up on a shoreline.

Maryport Coastguard Rescue Team said it was called to Flimby beach where a juvenile northern bottlenose whale was found on Saturday, after Storm Austen and Storm Boelo battered the UK.

Northern bottlenose whales are most commonly found in the North Atlantic Ocean, where they can dive to more than 1,400m (4,593ft) deep and stay submerged for up to two hours, according to the charity Whale and Dolphin Conservation.

The Coastguard urged people to not touch the carcass as it "may have toxins that can pass to humans" and advised people to take care as Storm Boelo was "still going strong".

The Coastguard asked people to report any sightings of stranded whales as soon as possible, even if they might be dead, to keep clear from the mammal and to wait for help.

"Gathering round the animal will intensify their distress, and it is possible for disease to be passed to humans," it added.

News.title: Letter making claims about Meghan's father written by his first wife, BBC understands
News.content:
A letter sent to the Metropolitan Police making a number of claims relating to the Duchess of Sussex's father was written by his ex-wife Roslyn Loveless, the BBC understands.

Meghan confirmed on Friday she had previously been informed about "disturbing allegations" about her estranged father, Thomas Markle.

On Saturday, the Met confirmed it received a letter relating to Markle in 2019, and it was shared with the Duke and Duchess of Sussex at the time.

It has been reported that images of child sexual abuse allegedly belonging to Markle, 82, had been found in his former home in the Philippines. Markle, who is based in the US, denies all such allegations.

Loveless, who has since died, is the mother of Meghan's half-siblings Samantha Markle and Thomas Markle Jr. Loveless divorced Markle in 1975 before he married the Duchess' mother Doria Ragland in 1979.

Meghan was born in 1981 and is the only daughter of Markle and Ragland.

In a statement shared on Friday, Meghan confirmed the existence of the letter and wrote: "I am deeply distressed... my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed."

She said she hoped it could be understood why she had largely cut off contact from her father and did "not allow him to have contact with our children".

Meghan has been estranged from her father since 2018. The BBC understands she broke contact with him last year, telling him she and the authorities knew he had abused young girls.

Sources close to the duchess said Meghan warned Markle in a letter - sent while he was in hospital in the Philippines after having his leg amputated - that he would never meet his grandchildren.

News.title: Body found in search for man who fell overboard from ferry
News.content:
The body of a missing ferry passenger who fell overboard has been found on a beach in North Ayrshire.

HM Coastguard responded to a report of a man going overboard from the MV Caledonian Isles near Arran about 20:30 on Sunday 18 October.

The man was later named as 82-year-old Jim Wither, who was reported missing from Johnstone, Renfrewshire.

Police Scotland earlier received a report that the body of a man had been found in the Largs beach area on Sunday. Formal identification has yet to take place, but the family of Jim Wither has been informed.

Two helicopters, a coastguard aircraft, Royal National Lifeboat Institution (RNLI) lifeboats and rescue teams from the surrounding area were sent to find the passenger, but the search was called off at 16:55 on Monday.

Officers said the death was not being treated as suspicious and a report would be submitted to the procurator fiscal in due course.

News.title: Couple were celebrating anniversary before Bahamas tragedy
News.content:
He said both boys had been so excited and been snorkelling in shallow water as they sorted out their towels and bags on the beach when the boys got into difficulties.

Both parents went into the sea and tried to save them as they were swept out by the current, he added, and the whole ordeal happened in less than 10 minutes.

Nathan said the loss of his 36-year-old "childhood sweetheart" was "unimaginable", but she was a "hero... in life and in death" as she helped to rescue the two boys.

"I've known her since infant school," he told the BBC. "We first got together when we were 14... so 22 years."

"There are no words I can use to describe Leanne, same as anyone she has ever known.

"She was the purest of people, the most generous kind and beautiful person who ever walked the Earth.

"Our relationship was perfect. She was the perfect mother, the perfect wife, the foundation of our entire family."

Nathan added: "Royal Caribbean and Virgin Airlines were absolutely incredible to us and made an impossible journey home so much easier."

Now, as he "keeps strong for his boys", a fundraising page has generated nearly Â£9,000 in donations to support the family.

News.title: Photos show potholes days before fatal crash
News.content:
Newly released photographs show a road riddled with potholes just days before a speeding car struck one and plunged into a river, killing two teenagers.

A VW Polo driven by Declan Berry was travelling at about 90mph (145km/h) moments before it entered the River Nene on North Brink, near Wisbech, Cambridgeshire, on 17 March, killing him and one of his passengers.

Four days earlier, Cambridgeshire County Council had ordered repairs to 98 potholes along the road, with the work scheduled to start on 3 April.

The authority said repairs to that section of North Brink had been "scheduled in line with our normal maintenance processes and response times".

News.title: Board of Deputies of British Jews declares Greens to be racist party
News.content:
The Green Party of England and Wales has been declared a racist organisation by the Board of Deputies of British Jews.

The Jewish body, which is the largest in the UK, was responding to the "Zionism is racism" policy motion passed at the Green Party's conference earlier this month.

Board of Deputies president Phil Rosenberg said a vote passed by 118 votes to one to declare that the Greens had, "by adopting an antisemitic platform, become a racist party".

A spokesman for the Greens insisted the party does not discriminate against people who hold Zionist views and said it rejected the Board of Deputies' "characterisation of this motion and our party".

They added the decision "will not stop us from speaking out against the genocide in Gaza and pushing for stronger sanctions against the Israeli government and its leaders". Israel has repeatedly denied its actions in Gaza amount to genocide.

The motion passed by the Board of Deputies urged other parties not to do deals with the Greens unless they rejected the policy.

Forming coalition deals with Greens at local or national level would be "failing to take antisemitism with the requisite seriousness", it said, unless the party's local leadership have rejected the policy and committed to overturn it.

Labour has already issued an ultimatum to local Green groups it is currently in coalition with, telling them to disown the motion or lose the party's support.

Rosenberg said: "By adopting an antisemitic platform, the Green Party of England and Wales has become a racist party. We will treat it accordingly.

"No political party has the right to tell Jews that a central part of our identity, rooted in thousands of years of history, faith and peoplehood, is racist.

"The Green Party's policy brands much of our community, including our synagogues and communal organisations, with that slur. It gives prejudice against Jews a political licence.

"The Green Party's leadership must now take responsibility for reversing this policy and confronting the antisemitism it has legitimised."

The motion backed by Green members at its party conference earlier this month said Zionism was an ideology supporting "an ethnonationalist Jewish state in historic Palestine to the exclusion and/ or domination of the non-Jewish population".

It was criticised by Jewish groups, as well as four Green MPs and two former leaders, and opposition political parties.

Responding when the Green motion was passed, the Board of Deputies and Jewish Leadership Council said in a joint statement that "Zionism is anti-racism, creating a refuge for Jews in their ancient homeland after millennia of persecution outside it".

Green Party leader Zack Polanski, who is Jewish, did not take part in the vote on the motion as he left the conference early to campaign in the Holborn and St Pancras by-election which was held days later.

He has since told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg that, while he would like to make amendments, he would not overturn the motion, which would be party policy until 2028.

News.title: Four-year-old girl dies after fall from tower block
News.content:
A four-year-old girl has died after falling from a tower block in east London.

The Metropolitan Police said officers were called to the scene at an address in St Paul's Road, Barking, at about 11:00 BST on Saturday morning, following reports that a child had fallen from height.

Paramedics from the London Ambulance Service gave first aid and the child was taken to hospital, but later died from her injuries.

A Met spokesperson said the incident was not believed to be suspicious.

"Our thoughts and deepest sympathies are with the child's family and loved ones at this incredibly difficult time," they said.

"An investigation into the circumstances surrounding this tragic incident is ongoing. However, at this time, the incident is not believed to be suspicious.

"We urge anyone with information about the incident to contact police on 101, quoting CAD 2424/24OCT."

News.title: 10 best armchairs to sink into, reviewed by an interiors expert
News.content:
Your questions about armchairs answered

What is the best armchair?

I rate Habitat Dawson fabric swivel chair as the best overall. Excellent value, it's a comfy swivel design that is neutral enough to suit a living area, kitchen, office or bedroom space. It comes with a matching footstool for an extra £60, so you can put your feet up and relax.

My best budget buy is the Nyla accent chair from Dusk. At 81.5cm high, it’s a relatively compact armchair that can be easily transported around the home and it’s neutral enough to work with most colours and finishes. You could use it to add extra seating around a sofa, as a space to sit in an open-plan kitchen and living room or in a corner of your bedroom.

Also worth a mention is Loaf’s slow riser, which is simply dreamy and its design works well in both classic and more contemporary set ups. While it comes with a premium price tag, I think it’s a design that will age gracefully through the years, so well worth the spend.

What is the best armchair for back pain?

Look for armchairs that have a high backrest that can provide support for the full length of the spine, and ideally one with somewhere to support your head and neck. Equally, it can be helpful if the armchair’s cushions are firm enough that you don’t find yourself sinking into them and hunching over.

In my tests, I found Next’s armchair to offer good support for my back and shoulders, thanks to its high back, and the firm cushions helped me to stay sitting in a good posture.

How I tested armchairs

To find the best armchair, I called in a selection of attractive designs from well-known brands. I placed the armchairs up around my house – carrying out the odd bit of DIY to set them up when necessary – and have taken time out to try them out personally. I’ve rated them on the following criteria:

Design: I’ve rated each armchair on its aesthetics and how attractive it looks. I’ve honed in on its materials – be it wood or metal – and fabric options – be it faux leather, velvet or linen. I’ve assessed how durable I think each chair is and whether I think its craftsmanship has the quality to stand the test of time.

I’ve assessed how durable I think each chair is and whether I think its craftsmanship has the quality to stand the test of time. Comfort: I tested out each armchair personally, and asked family members and guests to give their opinion too. I took into consideration firmness and support – softer cushions feel comfy at first, but firmer ones can offer more support over time, for example. While style is important, comfort is undeniably what will ensure the chair becomes a permanent fixture in your home, after all.

I took into consideration firmness and support – softer cushions feel comfy at first, but firmer ones can offer more support over time, for example. While style is important, comfort is undeniably what will ensure the chair becomes a permanent fixture in your home, after all. Ease of cleaning and durability: An armchair will get a lot of wear and tear, so choosing a design that is practical and easy to keep looking box fresh is important. I’ve rated each design on how easy the materials are to care for and how easy the design is to clean.

What should you look for in a good armchair?

“Think about how you intend to use the armchair as this will dictate what kind of style you choose,” says interior designer Andrew Dunning of London Contemporary. “Is it for reading? Then you’ll probably want something with a higher backrest for supporting your head and neck. Or if you intend to use it while watching TV, perhaps you’ll want to opt for a design with a matching footstool. If it’s to furnish an empty stretch of wall or corner of your living space, a bold, colourful design or one with a unique shape will add the wow-factor to your design scheme. But no matter what design you choose, comfort is key as the best armchair should be cherished, used daily and just get better with age.”

How do I clean a wood and leather armchair?

“When cleaning an armchair with a leather seat and wooden frame, it's important to treat each material separately to avoid damaging the finish,” says Emma Mannion, cleaning expert at Astonish.

Wipe down the leather seat with a dry microfibre cloth to remove any dust and surface dirt. For a deeper clean, use a slightly damp cloth with a small amount of diluted mild soap, wiping gently over the surface before drying it straight away with a clean cloth. For the wooden arms and legs, use a soft cloth to remove dust, then wipe with a barely damp cloth and a mild cleaning solution, always following the direction of the wood grain. Finish by drying the wood thoroughly to prevent moisture from affecting the finish.

How do I clean a fabric armchair?

“Your vacuum's upholstery attachment is your best friend for this,’ says Catherine Green, sustainable cleaning expert at Smol.

Clean away loose crumbs, dust, or pet hair with a good vacuum. Pop any removable cushion covers in a cool wash. For fixed upholstery or a general refresh (this method works wonderfully for velvet sofas and chairs too), mix half a litre of warm water with half a teaspoon of washing-up liquid to create some suds. With a microfibre cloth, apply a small amount of the suds, and gently rub the fabric in circular motions. Once the dirt has lifted, wiping the area with another clean, slightly damp cloth. The golden rule here is to make sure cloths aren't too wet; soaking the fabric can lead to water-logging and nasty, musty smells building up. If you just have a few isolated marks, spot cleaning with a bleach-free stain gel is a fantastic alternative. To tackle any lingering odours, a sprinkle of bicarbonate of soda left on the fabric for at least 30 minutes before vacuuming acts as a brilliant natural deodoriser.

News.title: Burnham: Brexit is to blame for Britain’s small boats crisis
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Andy Burnham has blamed Britain’s migrant crisis on Brexit, arguing that leaving the EU had left the UK with “weaker control”.

The prime minister said on Monday that he wants to see Britain rejoin the European Union in his lifetime, after he reopened the Brexit debate earlier this year.

Mr Burnham ruled out a return for the UK to EU freedom of movement rules without a referendum, after he signalled he could include the move in Labour’s next election manifesto.

But the prime minister said he did not think “things have worked out as people said they would at the time”, highlighting immigration and the small boats crisis.

“I don't think things have worked out as people said they would at the time, particularly when it comes to immigration,” Mr Burnham said.

“I think we've got weaker control now. The reason the small boats crisis has arisen is because we can't return people, and people know we can't do that in the same way that we used to be able to do.”

open image in gallery Burnham ruled out a return of the UK to EU freedom of movement rules without a referendum, after he signalled he could include the move in Labour’s next election manifesto ( PA )

More than 200,000 migrants have arrived in the UK after crossing the Channel since data began on January 1 2018.

The record for the largest number of migrants to arrive in the UK in a calendar year is 45,774, which was set in 2022.

The number rapidly increased over the Covid-19 pandemic, but in the first six months of 2026, the number of people arriving in the UK by small boat fell 41 per cent and the number of boats 47 per cent compared to the previous year.

The prime minister admitted on Saturday he is open to reintroducing freedom of movement in an intervention that has boosted hopes that the UK could look to rejoin the bloc after the next general election.

It comes just weeks after Mr Burnham said the UK could go “all the way” and rejoin the bloc, but insisted the British public will “be the boss” of its own future.

But he added on Monday: “I’m not proposing any changes in this parliament. I’m not going to move away from the red lines that were in the Labour manifesto.”

open image in gallery More than 200,000 migrants have arrived in the UK after crossing the Channel since data began on 1 January 2018 ( Reuters )

Asked whether he would allow the UK to join the EU freedom of movement scheme without a referendum, he said: “No, I mean I wasn’t saying that yesterday. I was asked about how things have changed in the 10 years since Brexit, and the truth of the matter is we’ve lost immigration control in the way that we once had.”

And asked whether he would like to see the UK rejoin the EU, he said: “In my lifetime I would like to see that happen but I am not going to move ahead of the public, I am not going to dictate.

The Independent has led the campaign for Britain to rebuild its relationship with Brussels on the basis of clear evidence that it has damaged the economy and failed to deliver promised benefits on a wide range of issues including immigration.

News.title: The £66.50 holiday fee EasyJet will now cover for free
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Parents booking an easyJet holiday can soon have the cost of their baby's passport covered, the operator has announced.

In a survey of 2,000 parents for easyJet, one in 10 admitted they did not know their baby needed their own passport until they started planning a holiday.

And one in four said when they did get around to applying for one, it took up to six attempts to get a passport photo approved.

Stuart Wright, customer director at easyJet Holidays, said: “Travel has a unique way of bringing families together, and a baby’s very first holiday is often one of those moments parents remember for years to come.

“By covering the cost of a baby’s first passport, we’re helping more families start making those memories that little bit sooner.”

open image in gallery Nine-month-old Emelia on board an easyJet aircraft ( PA )

During the promotional period, the £66.50 fee will be covered for a child up to the age of 18 months when parents book an easyJet holiday.

easyJet holidays reported a 10 per cent increase in infants travelling this year compared to 2025.

In the UK, a parent or guardian can apply for a first child passport for any child under the age of 16. It costs £66.50 to apply online and £80 to apply with a paper form from the Post Office, and is then valid for five years. Current processing times estimate a three-week wait.

Details on how to claim the offer will be available at easyJet.com/firstpassport.

The promotion ends 26 November at 11pm.

open image in gallery Access to e-gates at UK airports was expanded to include younger children ( PA )

Earlier this year, the Home Office announced that e-gates at UK airports would be made available to younger children.

Since 8 July, children aged eight and nine returning to the UK have been eligible to use the automated gates.

The gates use facial recognition technology for identity verification, which is generally quicker than manual inspections.

Children must be at least 120cm tall so they can be seen by biometric scanners and accompanied by an adult.

Previously, passengers under the age of 10 were prohibited from using the gates, often leading to longer queues for families at traditional passport booths.

News.title: Nicolas Cage makes candid confession about ‘problem’ that led to awkward Chris Rock encounter
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Nicolas Cage has confessed to having "a problem" with interrupting people, while offering an apology for gatecrashing Chris Rock’s interview on the Howard Stern Show back in 2022.

The 62-year-old actor made headlines after making an unannounced appearance on the radio programme while Stern and Rock were in mid-conversation.

Addressing a panel during New York Comic Con earlier this month, Nicolas told attendees: "I don’t interrupt people anymore. I had a problem with that in the past. I feel very bad about it. And I’ve actually apologised."

Reflecting on the moment in question, Nicolas said: "Chris Rock was on the Howard Stern Show and I just crashed the show. I felt terrible. I didn’t know it was Chris. I just showed up. I didn’t want to give Howard time to think about questions to ask."

Cage later ran into Rock in public, describing the stand-up as "the coolest human in all of Hollywood", and noted that Chris accepted his apology with grace.

He said: "I love Chris and he was nice about it. But yeah, I probably shouldn’t have interrupted."

Nicolas Cage at the New York Comic Con ( Getty )

During the radio studio interruption, Stern and Rock were halfway through their interview when Cage walked in, surprising both of them in the process.

He explained he could only stay briefly, leading Rock to joke that Cage was the more famous of the two.

After Cage disputed this, Rock retorted: "He’s got an Academy Award. I’ve got a Source Award."

The Face/Off actor also reflected on his relationship with Sean Connery, specifically remembering the late star’s love for playing golf.

He told Stern and Rock: "I was all about fishing [at the time], and I like being on my boat. And Sean wanted to get me on the golf course."

Cage shared that he enjoyed a "great relationship" with Connery, though he added: "I never went on the golf course because I just didn’t have time for that."

News.title: US Marine indicted for ‘strangling woman with telephone wire and robbing her’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A US marine has been indicted in Okinawa prefecture in Japan on charges of robbing and murdering a Japanese woman.

Lance corporal Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, was accused of killing Anna Yagi, 39, in a hotel in the prefecture’s capital Naha and taking her wallet and backpack earlier this month. Ballard denied the allegations.

Ballard, who was stationed at Futenma Air Base, was found walking alone in Okinawa city later that day and was arrested the following day on suspicion of robbery and murder.

He was indicted on Sunday amid growing anger among Okinawa residents over the incident and the presence of US military installations.

He allegedly strangled the woman with the cord of a telephone in a hotel room between 2.10 and 4.15am on 3 October and stole her backpack that contained her wallet and other belongings, according to the indictment.

The woman had checked into the hotel with a man around 2.10am that day. Hotel employees entered the room at 4.15am after she did not check out on time. The staff found her body and alerted the police, investigative sources told the Japan Times.

open image in gallery Ballard, pictured leaving a police station, denies the allegations ( Reuters )

Investigators later checked the security footage that showed a man with tattoos on both arms and a backpack leading the hotel, the report said. The backpack was found near the hotel.

Under Japanese law, conviction can carry the death penalty or life imprisonment.

The incident involving a foreign national prompted Okinawa governor Genta Koja to step up calls for the central government to take preventive measures.

Local residents have long voiced anger over crimes committed by US military personnel, including offences against women and girls, as well as noise and pollution associated with American military installations.

Following his arrest, the US military in Okinawa imposed a 30-day curfew on 9 October, restricting personnel from leaving their bases between midnight and 5 am.

It was after the Japanese government lodged a strong protest with the US government over the incident.

Prime minister Sanae Takaichi condemned the incident as a “brutal and heinous” crime and called for stricter discipline of American personnel.

open image in gallery People watch the flight line near a poster showing the different kinds of aircraft next to Kadena Air Base in Kadena, Okinawa prefecture ( AFP/Getty )

The incident renewed long-standing local tensions over the heavy US military presence on Okinawa, which hosts a large share of US bases in Japan.

Crimes involving US military personnel stationed in Japan, including murder, rape, and robbery, have long been a source of public concern.

In Okinawa, local police handled over 100 criminal cases involving US personnel in 2025 alone, according to an official from the prefecture.

In 2016, a former Marine and Kadena base civilian worker Kenneth Gadson was sentenced to life in prison for raping and murdering a 20-year-old woman.

The rape of a ​12-year-old Okinawan ⁠girl by three US servicemen in 1995 sparked widespread protests.

News.title: Royal Mail delays full rollout of postal overhaul until after Christmas
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Royal Mail has revealed it will halt the full rollout of its second-class post overhaul until after Christmas amid calls for the service to urgently improve its performance.

The group said it had agreed with the postal workers’ union to delay expanding the reforms to the remaining 107 delivery offices until January to allow staff to focus on the peak festive season.

Royal Mail, whose owner International Distribution Services was bought last year by Czech billionaire Daniel Kretinsky, is rolling out major reforms that will result in second-class post only being delivered on alternate weekdays with Saturday second-class deliveries scrapped.

The business had expected to expand the new model across all its 1,200 delivery offices by Christmas, after initial delays because of disagreements with the trade union.

open image in gallery The reforms are being delayed at around 100 delivery offices (PA) ( PA Archive )

Royal Mail has so far completed the changes in just under 1,100 delivery offices, with another 15 included by November 2, but will wait until January 11 for the reforms to be applied in the final 107 offices across the UK.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham last week told Royal Mail to improve its performance and warned the Government would take “further measures” after repeatedly missing delivery targets.

The Communication Workers Union also earlier this month called for an emergency summit on Royal Mail’s future, claiming the organisation was “on the brink of collapse”.

Royal Mail insisted its reforms were starting to bear fruit, but said the latest delay was a “pragmatic approach” to allow it to “maintain the momentum behind one of the biggest operational changes in its history, while keeping focus firmly on delivering a successful Christmas for customers”.

Alistair Cochrane, chief executive of Royal Mail, said: “We have now deployed our new delivery model in around 90% of delivery offices and are starting to see the benefits for customers.

“First-class quality of service has improved by 9%, and offices operating under the new delivery model are delivering to around 95% of addresses each day on average, compared with 88% before rollout began.

“There is still more to do, but the progress we are seeing gives us confidence that the new delivery model will continue to ensure more reliable, efficient and sustainable deliveries for our customers,” he added.

News.title: Drone ‘the size of four toasters’ seen hovering over British Airways plane after Heathrow take-off
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A British Airways plane encountered a drone “the size of four toasters” after taking-off from Heathrow Airport, air safety officials have revealed.

The New York City-bound flight had only recently departed London Heathrow Airport on June 24 when it encountered the drone.

The pilot told Air Traffic Control that a drone had flown in the opposite direction about 50 feet above the plane’s right wing at 12.08pm.

The plane didn’t have to take any action to avoid the drone, a British Airways spokesman said.

The drone flew straight past the aircraft and the Boeing 777 arrived at its destination as planned.

A drone flew past a British Airways plane the “size of four toasters”, air safety officials revealed ( PA Wire )

The UK Aiprox Board said in its monthly report of close encounters that the plane was 6,000ft in the air when the “shiny, silver object” whizzed past.

“They said it was moving very fast, was probably of silver colour, metallic and reflective,” the report said.

“After an enquiry as to its size, the [pilot] reported to them that it was about the ‘size of four toasters’.”

A spokesperson for British Airways said: “We take matters such as these extremely seriously, and our pilots report these incidents so authorities can investigate them and take appropriate action.”

News.title: Wolff puts ‘tequila on ice’ with Antonelli two points away from title
News.content:
Mercedes had chosen the medium tyres for the start, while Ferrari’s Leclerc and the Red Bulls of Verstappen and Isack Hadjar started on new softs. Antonelli was able to convert that choice into a one-stop race while almost everyone else did two, emphasising his superiority as he finished 16 seconds clear of Leclerc.

A late virtual safety car after Valtteri Bottas’s Cadillac ground to a halt by the side of the track made the final laps rather processional, denying the huge crowds at COTA the opportunity of seeing the fast-closing Hamilton take on Verstappen for the final podium spot.

That might have been fun, with Verstappen having lost his cool with his team midway through the race, furious that they didn’t order team-mate Hadjar out of the way when he came up behind him after stopping: “Thanks guys. Really good strategy there. Stuck in the dirty air.”

Incredibly, his third place finish in Austin means is the first time since the final race of 2020 that Verstappen has been out of title contention.

But it hardly mattered. The day belonged once again to Antonelli who should be champion by the end of next week. Not that he was getting carried away. “It was the result we needed,” he said. “The whole team deserved it so much, bringing this [upgrade] package. It was also the perfect execution with the strategy to do the one stop.”

Asked about the title, he added: “We’re very close, we try to finish on a high and hopefully we can finish it very soon. I mean, the perfect way will be to finish in style and then just enjoy the rest of the season. I’m very aware that it’s very close, but the mindset doesn’t change. I want to finish on a high to go into 2027 with momentum.”

“Yeah, what a boy, no?” Wolff said, admiringly. “I was just saying before, I got a question about whether he was nervous before the race, and I said, ‘Oh, he just sneaked into my office before getting ready and said, ‘I’m just going to enjoy this right now, and it’s weird, I’m not thinking about the championship at all. Isn’t that funny?’”

Wolff added that there would “definitely be a lot of tequila on ice” in Mexico. In hindsight it was always going to be a more appropriate venue to crown the sport’s youngest ever champion. Antonelli is not, after all, old enough to drink yet in the state of Texas.

News.title: Hapless and hopeless Man Utd bring curtain down on out-of-depth Carrick
News.content:
Hapless, hopeless and utterly humiliated. And that has to be that for Michael Carrick. It is surely inconceivable that he will continue any longer as Manchester United’s head coach. A proud club on its knees and a favoured son on his way out.

The former midfielder will carry the can. As managers always do. Even if the fault lines run so deep at United that it feels like they are almost irreparable. Owners – the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe – executives, players. A collective failing of monumental proportions. Although, again, it will be the manager who goes. Carrick knows it and it looked like it at the end. He knows the score, especially after this score.

More than four years ago Ralf Rangnick, the then interim manager, declared that United needed “open heart surgery”. Now there is barely a pulse.

An announcement must be imminent, with United turning to someone else in the fight against Premier League relegation. A joke? No, this abject performance against Bournemouth leaves United in 16th place, just a point above the bottom three, so the priority for the new man will be clear. Save them from the drop. They are 14 points off the top already, but forget that. It is irrelevant given their plight.

News.title: Trafford shows he has credentials to dislodge Pickford as England No 1
News.content:
Goalkeeping is defined by athleticism, physical strength and reflexes, but it is also about decision-making and mental fortitude. The two saves Trafford made to deny Sunderland’s Brian Brobbey in the first half were very different, but equally impressive.

The first was deceptively hard. Although the connection on Brobbey’s shot – back in the Sunderland side and causing chaos as usual – from the edge of the area was not the cleanest and that almost made it harder, as the flight of the ball was difficult to pick up. The bounce just in front of the goalkeeper meant he had to watch it closely, judge the trajectory in the air and spin off the grass and still keep a strong hand, at full stretch, to push it away from danger.

The second was, arguably, even better. Trafford had come off his line as Brobbey ran into the box. He was in a really vulnerable position, well outside his six-yard box in a one-on-one with the Netherlands international. The way he kept calm, stood up and timed when to move for the ball was superb, especially as an error could have led to a penalty.

Trafford may have saved with his feet, but he had cramped Brobbey for room, waited for the centre forward to make a move and timed the moment to dive at his feet perfectly. It was elite-level goalkeeping in a really tricky situation that favoured the striker.

Trafford made two more fine stops in the second half too, both from Nilson Angulo. The first was getting down low to tip another bouncing ball wide, which had flicked off a defender too. The second punching another deflected effort away after a block had taken some of the venom out of the shot.

Sunderland will feel like they shaded the battle, but Robin Roefs also made two decent stops from long-range shots in the second half while substitute Sean Longstaff saw an injury-time effort cleared off the line.

News.title: England pay price for toothless bowling in astonishing defeat by Pakistan
News.content:
Hello and welcome to live, over-by-over coverage of Pakistan v England in Lahore. In the UK, the clocks went back an hour overnight; England would love to wind them back 72 hours and have another go at defending 429 against Sri Lanka. That unfathomable defeat in Rawalpindi has left them on the brink in this tri-series.

England won’t be mathematically eliminated if they lose to Pakistan today, but it would leave them needing snookers if they are to reach Saturday’s final. Realistically, they need to win the last two group games, and there’s a chance even that might not be enough.

“It’s my first tri-series and it replicates World Cup styles and pressures,” said the England all-rounder Will Jacks. “You can’t replicate that in training or a bilateral series. In World Cups you have to bounce back. I remember in 2019 when England lost a couple of games in the group and they had to win their last two and they were able to do that to take the momentum forward.

“I’m not saying it’s the same thing but it’s a mini version of that and hopefully we can win on Sunday and move on. We have the opportunity to play in two must-win fixtures. Sometimes you learn more in losses than you do in wins.”

Jacks’ Surrey team-mate Sam Curran suffered the most against Sri Lanka, conceding an eye-watering 103 from his nine overs.

“They were incredibly hard conditions to bowl in and he bowls a lot of pressure overs – that’s his role in the team,” said Jacks. “He’s been so successful with that for England over a number of years. There are some days where it doesn’t quite work.”

Curran has kept his place in the side – but Josh Tongue is replaced by Henry Crocombe, who makes his international debut. And there’s no recall for Adil Rashid. We’ll have the toss and full team news in a moment.

News.title: Most expensive goal in Liverpool history gives Iraola era lift-off
News.content:
This was an important afternoon for Liverpool’s head coach, a difficult assignment against high-flying, well-respected opponents in Brighton, who arrived on Merseyside having won their last four Premier League fixtures with a combined aggregate of 15-0, including a 3-0 thumping of reigning champions Arsenal.

But Liverpool rose impressively to the challenge and there are grounds for saying this was the most significant success to date for Iraola, whose team defended relentlessly to preserve a clean sheet. They are up to fourth now after this 2-0 success and deserve their position.

“I’m very happy,” Iraola said. “We faced a very good opponent, similar to Villarreal [in the Champions League]. It’s difficult to defend them a lot of times and it was key how we started. We needed to be aggressive, recover balls, win our duels, be dangerous in transitions: I think we’ve done it.”

And how. Iraola was able to march towards the Kop at the end, to clap the supporters and acknowledge only Liverpool’s fifth (and his first) Premier League win at Anfield in 2026, and it was evident he had a spring in his step from what he had seen.

Whether the game would have flowed in the direction it did had Brighton taken the lead can only be speculated but what a glorious chance they wasted for us to find out: in the 13th minute, five swift, one-touch passes bamboozled Liverpool’s defence and created space for Yasin Ayari.

With the goal at his mercy, Ayari could have made things exceptionally uncomfortable but he leant back and blazed over. He clasped his face and grimaced, knowing what had gone begging in front of the Kop; four minutes later, his misery was exacerbated.

News.title: Antonelli takes another step closer to F1 title with US GP pole position
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for qualifying for the 2026 United States Grand Prix at the Circuit of the Americas, just outside of Austin. This is one of the finest tracks that we have on the Formula One calendar and is a fitting place for the US Grand Prix. The races are usually entertaining, the drivers love the track (though have complained about the bumps this year) and it comfortably the best on-track action of the three races in the US.

What might we see this weekend? Well, Kimi Antonelli could be crowned world champion if results go his way. The way the results need to go make that fairly unlikely, but stranger things have happened in F1 and they often do. In any case, it would take a catastrophic implosion for Antonelli to lose the championship from here, so it is a case of when rather than if.

Who looks in good form? Well, Ferrari do. They have brought an updated car here this weekend it, so far, is paying off. Charles Leclerc had good pace yesterday and Lewis Hamilton, his team-mate, was fastest earlier today in final practice. Hamilton’s time of 1min34.893sec was a tenth or two quicker than the Red Bull of Max Verstappen, with Leclerc not too far behind. Then it was Antonelli, George Russell in the second Mercedes and Oscar Piastri making up the top six, though the Australian was nearly half a second off the ultimate pace of Hamilton.

Qualifying begins in about 50 minutes and we will be here with all the updates from that.

News.title: Sensational Spurs storm Stamford Bridge as Palmer loses his head
News.content:
Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has told Cole Palmer he must learn from his red card that contributed to his team’s London derby defeat by Tottenham Hotspur.

Tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi insisted Palmer should have seen red for shoving his pelvis into the face of Mateus Fernandes. But, having got off with a yellow card, the Chelsea midfielder then fouled substitute Conor Gallagher.

“I haven’t seen them [the yellow cards] on TV, but as far as I have been told, he [the referee] probably got it right,” Alonso said. “So, for sure for Cole, but for everyone. We think [up until] now we haven’t received any red cards [this season] and we need to continue that way because we need to have this maturity to deal with difficult moments, when you have conceded 1-0, there was still 15-20 minutes to go, so we have to be calm. I need to check the action to talk with Cole, but it is one to learn for the future for sure.”

Asked if he thought Palmer should have been sent off for the first yellow card, De Zerbi, who was booked for his protests, replied: “Yep.”

Jordan Henderson had spoken to Palmer at the end of the previous week’s victory over Everton in which the forward could also have been booked for a second time and sent off.

But Alonso claimed he does not have any wider concerns about Palmer’s character. He said: “Today, for sure, yes, but it is not a [wider] concern. I think that Cole when he is focused on the game, when he is enjoying and today after the 1-0, it is a moment to keep calm, a moment to keep mature and for everyone.”

De Zerbi hailed his side’s character and claimed that Tottenham have “suffered enough” after two 17th-placed finishes and a slow start to the season until successive victories over Coventry City and Chelsea.

“We want to improve, improve and improve, to be better game by game, week by week. I think we have suffered enough,” De Zerbi said. “Changing the spirit of the group, changing the performance of the players, especially the more fragile players, maybe the younger players. We played very well. Great individual performances, great collective performance because we played very well. And then we put something different than Tottenham, I think, in the last period. Different attitude, different relationships with the players, different group.”

Chelsea were without João Pedro because of an injury and Alonso is waiting to find out how long the striker will be out.

“We don’t know yet because he has a lot of fluid,” Alonso said. “So he felt it yesterday [Friday] and we need to wait probably until tomorrow [Sunday] to do the test and to know the whole situation and the whole seriousness of the injury. We will know soon enough.”

News.title: Pollock at heart of scuffle that inspires Leicester to thumping win in feisty derby
News.content:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage of Leicester Tigers v Northampton Saints.

The Prem’s derby weekend continues today at Mattioli Woods Welford Road, where Geoff Parling’s side go head-to-head in with their East Midlands rivals.

Both Leicester and Northampton have two wins from the opening three rounds of the season and with both sides involved in a number of high-scoring encounters already in the new campaign, we could be in for a real treat.

Tigers started the season with a 38-40 loss at home to Saracens, but bounced back quickly with wins over Gloucester and Newcastle Red Bulls. They will be itching to right a few wrongs after suffering a chastening Champions Cup defeat in Pau last week.

Northampton, meanwhile, have notched up wins over Newcastle Red Bulls and Bath either side of loss to Bristol Bears.

A win today for Saints would be their first on the road since defeating Exeter Chiefs at Sandy Park in April.

“It (the East Midlands derby) means a lot to everyone, we know it will be a great atmosphere at Mattioli Woods Welford Road,” said Parling.

“I don’t think with this sort of game either team has to build it up too much emotionally because that just comes, so I think it’s actually about being really really calm in the moment.”

“Hopefully we can put the best of ourselves out there and I’m sure Saints will be able to do exactly the same.”

Saints are without a victory in Leicester since January 2023, when a single point decided the 18-19 result.

Since then, the last five meetings between the sides have been won by the hosts on the day – with Saints last taking home the bragging rights when a Tom Litchfield hat-trick helped Northampton to a 45-31 win on home soil in last season’s league play-off.

Kick-off gets underway at 3.05pm. Stay with us here for all the latest updates.

Sports.title: Barcelona stars wear special £500 shirts in Real Madrid defeat with fans able to buy rare jersey for eye-watering price
Sports.content:
Next

BARCELONA stars wore special limited-edition shirts worth a staggering £500 during their heartbreaking El Clasico defeat to Real Madrid.

Lamine Yamal and his team-mates stepped out in the eye-catching jerseys as they suffered a 2-1 defeat at the Nou Camp on Sunday.



The Catalan giants teamed up with Spotify and American rapper Tyler, The Creator’s fashion brand GOLF WANG to produce the exclusive shirts.

And fans hoping to get their hands on the same jersey worn by Yamal will have to fork out an eye-watering £499.99.



The limited-edition Player’s Edition shirt is available on Barcelona‘s official online store, with only 1,899 produced to celebrate the club’s founding year.

Each shirt comes with a unique number, a certificate of authenticity and special packaging, while featuring the GOLF logo on the front.



The collaboration also includes a range of clothing, with the special jersey replacing Barcelona’s usual Spotify branding for the biggest game in Spanish football.

But the expensive shirts brought no luck for Hansi Flick‘s side as Kylian Mbappe struck twice to hand Real Madrid a dramatic victory.

The French superstar opened the scoring in the first half when Yan Diomande’s cross deflected off Gerard Martin and bounced into the net off Mbappe.

Barcelona fought back after the break, with Raphinha equalising in the 61st minute following a clever pass from Pedri.

Sports.title: Lucky punter wins nearly £1MILLION from incredible £4 bet after taking chance on mind-blowing 12-fold CORNER accumulator
Sports.content:

A LUCKY punter landed almost £1MILLION after placing a 12-fold bet exclusively on corners.

The 45-year-old from Portsmouth placed £4 on 12 EFL matches.



He tipped all of them to have over 11.5 corners, which saw him win a staggering £997,385.09 in total.

The Betfair punter said: “Me and some friends usually do an accumulator on the weekend for a bit of fun, we all pick a leg and put them in our group chat, both teams to score usually, and I like to do corners.



“I had £4 in my account so I decided to do one of my own with a few more corners in.

“I’m sure that I’ll be treating my mates after winning this one, it will be my round all the time!”



The winning bet came following a second-half influx of corners in all 12 games.

The punter also admitted that he didn’t even realise he had won at first, adding: “I didn’t actually realise it had come in until about half an hour after all the games had finished.

MANCHESTER UNITED are holding discussions about the expected sacking of Michael Carrick.

Chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox arrived at the club’s Carrington training complex on Monday morning.



Intriguingly, Bruno Fernandes also arrived at Carrington even though it is a day off for the squad.

Fernandes was dropped against Bournemouth after he questioned Carrick’s tactics after the 4-1 thrashing by Como on Wednesday but he did not come on in the latest drubbing.



The 32-year-old did not warm up until the 58th minute and received a mixed reception from supporters.

The only other players who turned up on Monday are injured and it is understood the club captain was there to receive treatment.

The United hierarchy held internal talks about the club’s next move on Sunday night but are yet to thrash out a compensation package with Carrick’s agent.

Berrada was abused as he boarded the vehicle that ferried his family away from the stadium.

United players and staff almost always have a day off the day after a game and that has not changed despite a sixth defeat in 12 games.

Julian Nagelsmann and Eddie Howe have both been sounded out as possible replacements for Carrick but United have still not made a formal approach for Antonio Conte.

Howe, out of work since he left Newcastle in July, has been tracking United’s recent plight amid the possibility that the club will make him an offer.

Former United sporting director Dan Ashworth and performance advisor Sir Dave Brailsford, viewed as two allies of Howe, left two seasons ago.

Sports.title: Who is Thierry Henry’s girlfriend Andrea Rajacic and how many children do couple have?
Sports.content:
Next

THIERRY Henry is taking centre stage tonight as he hosts the Ballon d’Or ceremony in London.

The Arsenal legend’s long-term partner Andrea Rajacic has been by his side for more than 15 years. Here’s everything you need to know.



Who is Thierry Henry’s girlfriend Andrea Rajacic?

Andrea Rajacic, 39, was born in Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and has largely stayed out of the limelight despite her partner’s fame.

She studied business administration and Italian at the University of Mary Washington in the US, graduating in 2007.



Andrea later worked in corporate sales at New York’s Milk Studios and studied Spanish in Barcelona.

She also co-founded an online publication called The New York Issue.

In a 2010 interview with the Croatian newspaper Jutarnji List, Andrea addressed reports that she had worked as a model and explained why she and Thierry Henry prefer to keep their relationship private.

Translated from Croatian, Andrea said: “I’m a very private person and don’t want to make public statements.

“You know what it’s like for people such as Thierry and the pressure public figures are under. We both agree that we shouldn’t reveal details about our relationship.

“It’s true that we’ve been together for about a year and that we met in Spain.



“I’ve never worked as a model, despite what the media has reported. Instead, I studied management in America.

“I wouldn’t want to reveal anything more, especially at the moment. Perhaps I’ll change my mind in time, but for now that’s how things stand.”

Andrea has accompanied the Arsenal icon to several high-profile events, including the GQ Men of the Year Awards in Paris in November 2024 and the Joy Awards in Saudi Arabia in January 2025.

How many children do Thierry Henry and Andrea Rajacic have?

The couple share three children together – sons Tristan and Gabriel, who also goes by Gabi, and daughter Tatiana.

Tristan was born in August 2012, followed by Tatiana in August 2015. While Gabriel’s exact birth year isn’t known, it is reportedly either 2016 or 2017.



Henry also has an older daughter, Tea, born in May 2005, with his first wife, English model Claire Merry, who worked under the name Nicole Merry.

All four presented their father with the Lifetime Achievement Award at the BBC Sports Personality of the Year ceremony on December 18, 2025.

Henry dedicated the award to his kids, saying: “This is your award, not mine.

“You are educating me. You are saving me from my traumas and showing me what it is to be human, vulnerable and have empathy.



“So please bear with me, and thank you for being you.”

How long have Thierry Henry and Andrea Rajacic been together?

The couple met in Spain in 2008, while Henry was playing for Barcelona, and began dating the following year.

They made one of their first public appearances together in 2010, when they attended Formula One testing in Barcelona.

Henry and Andrea later settled in London but kept a £19million penthouse in New York, which they put back on the market in September.

They had originally listed the property for sale in 2025 before changing their minds.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Henry said: “We were and still are in love with the place. It was very difficult to leave New York.”

In March, the former striker offered a glimpse of their relationship, posting a workout video with Andrea on Instagram and captioning it: “1 HOUR session with MY PARTNER IN CRIME and a 10kg vest on WORK HARD, EAT WELL, NO SUGAR!!!”

Sports.title: Ex-Man Utd star reveals what happened when he knocked out Wayne Rooney and left him unconscious on floor
Sports.content:
Next

PHIL BARDSLEY joked he “s***” himself after knocking out Wayne Rooney.

The former Manchester United team-mates infamously sparred in Wazza’s kitchen in 2015.



In footage exclusively revealed by SunSport at the time, Rooney could be seen falling unconscious after being caught by a vicious punch.

The ex-striker, then United and England skipper, just narrowly missed hitting his head on a chair as he fell.



Appearing on Call Yourself a Fan with Alex Brooker, Sean Dyche and Jimmy Bullard, Bardsley revealed his side of the story.

“It was just a standard Sunday at the time,” the former full-back began. “We had a couple of days off in between training and this particularly Sunday we went to The Bubble Room in Alderley Edge, which is a bar familiar to a few of the lads.



“We set out to watch a couple of the games – the half one game, the four o’clock game – and before you know it you’re probably seven, eight pints deep and one thing led to another.

“We ended up back at his house watching his wedding video, which was quite bizarre. I think he likes a singsong.”



On how their scrap began, Bardsley continued: “You’re in his house, you go with it. Before you know it, I see him come out of the kitchen with a pair of pink boxing gloves and I’m thinking ‘what’s going on here?’

“He brought another pair out and went ‘they’re for you’. I was like ‘okay’. Not a wise idea after 10, 15 pints that’s for sure.”

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Rooney, now 41, could be seen lying flat on his back after the KO blow.

Asked if there was a moment of real concern, Bardsley, 41, added: “Yeah, s*** myself. He was out (cold) for a little bit.



“He was the United and England captain and we’ve got no phone signal where we are, his eyes are closed and we’re thinking ‘it’s a little bit of trouble here’.

“Anyway, he come round, I’ve got a cut lip, he’s got a broken nose or whatever it was and rest is history.”

The incident came a day after United had lost 2-1 at Swansea under Louis van Gaal.

Rooney went on to score a double in his side’s very next game, a 2-0 win over Sunderland, as United began a run of six consecutive victories.

Footage of the incident emerged just hours before United hosted Spurs in a top four race battle.



After Wazza scored in his side’s 3-0 win, he memorably mimicked the knockout as he celebrated.

BRUNO FERNANDES has ‘liked’ a cryptic Instagram post about ‘loyal’ people getting ‘pushed to the point where they no longer care’.

The Manchester United captain was an unused substitute in Sunday’s woeful 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth at Old Trafford.



Michael Carrick made the bold call to drop Fernandes, who called out the manager’s tactics after a 4-1 loss to Como last week.

That was only the SIXTH time the Portuguese, 32, had been benched for a Premier League game since signing for United in 2020.



And some have taken his recent social media ‘like’ as a pointed message.

The reel showed a giant stone figure holding up a boulder that was destined to roll down a hill and destroy a village.

When the figure accidentally damages one of the village’s buildings while trying to contain the boulder, the people of the village turn on him.

So the figure lets go of the boulder and the village is flattened.

Written above the video are the words: “Never push a loyal person to the point where they no longer care.”

And the first part of the caption read: “The person holding everything together is usually the one nobody thinks to check on.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Fernandes has been United’s standout player for most of his six years at the club.

He has netted 111 goals in 334 games, and scooped the PFA Player of the Year award last season as United finished third in the Prem.

But fans made it clear who they are angry at after the Bournemouth game by cheering Carrick off the pitch and pelting the players with loud boos.



Carrick is now thought to be on the brink of the sack, with Eddie Howe among the candidates to replace him.

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho turns back time with trademark reaction to Real Madrid's El Clasico win
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho turns back time with trademark reaction to Real Madrid's El Clasico win

Kylian Mbappe netted twice as Real Madrid won 2-1 against bitter rivals Barcelona to keep up in the La Liga title race, with Jose Mourinho enjoying the best moment of his return

View 2 Images Jose Mourinho revelled in Real Madrid's win at the Camp Nou (Image: Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

This is why Real Madrid brought Jose Mourinho back.

‌



‌



Florentino Perez's decision to hire Mourinho in the summer after a miserable campaign under Xabi Alonso and Alvaro Arbeloa was criticised by many as being stuck in the past. Mourinho had last managed Real 13 years previously and his methods have been questioned in recent years.

‌



But his knee slide after Kylian Mbappe's second goal sealed a much-needed 2-1 win over Barcelona on Sunday night was exactly the kind of moment Perez must have envisioned.

‌



It was classic Mourinho. Real came into the game as underdogs against high-flying Barca and had just 37 per cent of the ball. But they took their chances.

‌



Mbappe's opening goal owed much to good fortune, with Gerard Martin's clearance going straight into his shin and then into the net. Barca equalised through Raphinha before Eduardo Camavinga broke into the box and picked out Mbappe to tap in the decisive goal in the 87th minute.

The 63-year-old Mourinho pulled out a trademark knee slide on the touchline and, after a respectful handshake with Barca boss Hansi Flick, he delivered the sort of line he's become known for.

‌



"I dedicate this win to the Barca fans who came to the hotel and kept singing all day, I couldn't take my nap," Mourinho told Real Madrid TV. "I didn't nap, but I did beat their team. A big hug to them."

Mourinho has won six and lost six in El Clasico as Real manager across two stints, but he's actually unbeaten in the past six, boasting four wins and two draws. He is the man for the big occasion and Real are now just three points adrift of their rivals, and one behind Atletico Madrid, in La Liga.

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

View 2 Images Kylian Mbappe netted both goals for Real Madrid (Image: Josep LAGO / AFP via Getty Images)

‌



"In my view, Real Madrid do not play to win at the Camp Nou, Real Madrid play to win La Liga," Mourinho said. "We could win with luck, but we won with calmness and with all merit," he said. "It's a very strong group. Everyone works very hard. Everyone was ready to win.

"The credit goes to the players. When you win, the credit goes to the players. But when you lose, the blame falls on you. And that's why we see coaches being sacked from their positions every week."

‌



Mbappe got the goals to make it 14 strikes in 13 games across all competitions this season. But he had a strong supporting cast, with Jude Bellingham once again catching the eye in midfield, where Bernardo Silva's tenacity combined nicely with the enterprising Yan Diomande and Arda Guler.

"I've learned that I have an extraordinary group, with the quality and mindset to play," Mourinho added. "In midfield, having a mix of talents gives us more than just having two players with similar characteristics. This mix of talents gives us balance when defending and quality when we go on the attack."

Former Liverpool winger Jermaine Pennant has revealed a terrifying ordeal where he was attacked by a German Shepherd. The 43-year-old says that his dog saved his life after needing 50 stitches following an attack.

‌



‌



According to BBC Sport, Pennant was walking his two dogs in North London last week when he was attacked. The German Shepherd is said to have latched on to his leg and refused to let go as he tried to protect his dog, American Akita King.

‌



King intervened, fighting off the German Shepherd, but it left the former Red hospitalised. Pennant admitted that he may require plastic surgery on one of the wounds but he will remain under supervision while taking medication for the wounds.

"But the minute he did he fought the dog off and saved what could’ve been an horrendous situation for me. King was unhurt with a little nip on his leg, but had blood covered all over him which wasn’t mine, at this point I forgot the agony I was in, and my heart sank, but it wasn’t King's.

The incident left him with four bite wounds on his right leg after his girlfriend Mimmi Montgomery booked him an taxi to take him to A&E where he was treated for the injuries.

Following his post on social media, Pennant addressed the issue during a live-stream of Liverpool's 2-0 win over Brighton & Hove Albion. After Florian Wirtz's effort deflected off Pascal Gross, the 43-year-old displayed his bandaged leg as he celebrated the Reds' opener.

‌



He said: "It's been an interesting week but it's good to be back, hopefully to make it better Liverpool can get three points."

View 2 Images (Image: jermaine7pennant/instagram)

‌



Shortly after Alexander Isak netted a second, he added: "I had a bad week, terrible week, got attacked by a dog but this is a remedy, this is the remedy, come on Liverpool.

During an interaction with the comments section, Pennant said: "The leg is okay, thanks for asking, it's a lot better, got to take the antibiotics and all that but it's okay.

Article continues below

"Friday night I got attacked by a German Shepherd, thankfully my dog was there to save the day. My partner rushed me to A&E, then went home; thankfully, my dog was unscathed.

"May need plastic surgery for one of the wounds. All good, all good though."

Sports.title: Arsenal news: 'Internal moaning' emerges as star told he will '100% be sold'
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: 'Internal moaning' emerges as star told he will '100% be sold'

Arsenal are level with Manchester City at the top of the Premier League table and have two tough tests coming up this week

View 3 Images Arsenal are targeting another unbeaten week in all competitions (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Arsenal are ready for trips to Highbury Stadium and Anfield as Mikel Arteta targets another unbeaten week for his Gunners. The club have the Carabao Cup to contend with as well as a tough Premier League test against Liverpool on Sunday afternoon.

‌



‌



However, Fleetwood Town are up first as the fourth round of the League Cup arrives for the north London outfit. Arteta's side climbed level on points with Manchester City on Saturday after Enzo Maresca's side stumbled at Villa Park.

‌



City's 2-1 loss early in the day was followed by Arsenal's 2-0 win over Everton just a few hours later. It was a double from the backline as Ezri Konsa and Gabriel secured the three points at the Emirates Stadium.

‌



Now, Arteta will aim to continue in the Carabao Cup as they travel to the League Two side on Tuesday night. Here, Mirror Football has the latest coming out of the red side of north London.

Arsenal rocked by Riccardo Calafiori injury as Mikel Arteta confirms latest blow READ MORE :

Bukayo Saka injury update as Arsenal fear losing star for two months READ MORE :

'Internal moaning' emerges

Former Aston Villa chief executive Keith Wyness claims there'll be some internal complaining at Arsenal over staff cuts coinciding with Arteta's new contract extension. The Scot believes the club have created a "bad look" after announcing the redundancies around the same time as the Spaniard's fresh terms.

Arteta's new deal, which runs until June 2030, was made public on October 7 and has seen an increase on his £10million salary alongside bonuses of £5m a year. A week later, Arsenal announced up to 60 job cuts following a review carried out by an external company.

‌



Speaking on the Inside Track podcast, Wyness states that announcing these two pieces of news so close together has caused 'internal moaning' and is overall a "disastrous" way to handle things.

View 3 Images Some 'internal moaning' has been touted as a result of Mikel Arteta's contract extension (Image: Henry NICHOLLS / AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Arsenal coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

He said: "It is a bad look, and I think it could have been avoided. I think it was all about timing. Look, they've obviously been in discussions with Mikel and his team for quite a while. They've obviously also been handling these redundancies and looking at the cost reductions for a while.

‌



"So they've had time to think about this and to bring them out so close together. While they're not related, it's just a very bad look. There'll be a lot of moaning internally about the way it's done. And clubs exist very, very much on the staff. People don't understand just how valuable these people are within the clubs.

"We had this whole discussion about Man United and what a disastrous way they've handled it, and I must admit I would have expected a little bit better from Arsenal. Had it been two or three months apart, the whole thing wouldn't have looked connected."

‌



Star told he will '100% be sold'

View 3 Images Viktor Gyokeres has been told he will definitely be sold in the next year (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

Gabriel Agbonlahor insists that Viktor Gyokeres will "100% be sold" before next season after failing to make an impact this year. The Sweden international started the win over Everton and grabbed the slightest of assists for Konsa's opener.

‌



However, Agbonlahor slaughtered the striker on talkSPORT as he claimed the 28-year-old was "running in slow motion." He said: "Jesus Christ, Jesus Christ. Looks like he’s like running in slow motion, isn’t he? Looks like he can’t run.

"Can he hold the ball up? Yes, he can, but he will be one that won’t be at the club next season. Yeah, 100%. They would have got rid of him this season if they could have for [Julian] Alvarez. If Alvarez wanted to come and hadn’t turned Arsenal down, they would have said, 'I would give you Gyokeres and money.'"

‌



In the Premier League, Gyokeres has made the starting XI just once this season and has managed 148 minutes so far. He is yet to find the net across 10 appearances in all competitions.
