Sports.title: Man Utd news: Sir Jim Ratcliffe 'accelerates' Carrick sack plan as club legend blamed
Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Sir Jim Ratcliffe 'accelerates' Carrick sack plan as club legend blamed

Manchester United insiders have their own theory

View Image Michael Carrick cut a dejected figure after Manchester United's defeat to Bournemouth (Image: Getty Images)

Michael Carrick's Manchester United future is hanging in the balance following his side's 3-0 drubbing against Bournemouth on Sunday. Goals from Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson condemned the Reds to a third defeat in four and extended their winless run to eight matches in all competitions.

‌



‌



It has increased the pressure on Carrick, who could face the sack with United winning just two of their 12 games this season. They have dropped down to 16th in the Premier League table, having picked up seven points from a possible 24 available, and haven't won in the top-flight since beating Ipswich Town in August.

‌



Speaking post-match, Carrick cut a dejected figure and didn't seem sure if he'll be the man in the dugout for United's trip to Chelsea next Saturday. Meanwhile, Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher have both called for United to sack Carrick after the club slumped to another defeat and dropped to within one point of the relegation zone.

‌



Following the defeat to Bournemouth, Mirror Football has rounded up the latest news from Old Trafford...

United bosses to accelerate sack plan

Manchester United's board are now expected to accelerate the process of appointing a new head coach, with the expectation from insiders at the club that Michael Carrick will be relieved of his duties, according to Sky Sports.

Sir Jim Ratcliffe and United bosses feel that a change is needed to improve the club's fortunes, with former Bayern Munich manager Julian Nagelsmann and ex-Newcastle United head coach Eddie Howe the leading candidates.

‌



But the decision on who is going to replace Carrick is poised to come down to director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada, who will make a recommendation to co-owner Ratcliffe.

Giggs' attack on Neville

Rhodri Giggs, the brother of Manchester United legend Ryan, has launched an X-rated attack on Gary Neville amid the club's growing crisis. In an explosive post on X, he wrote: "Gary Neville you’re an absolute w****r. Prime Pep couldn't get a tune out of this lot. Call your mate Jim [Ratcliffe] out who got us into this mess further.

Sports.title: Fabian Hurzeler aims thinly-veiled dig at Liverpool after Brighton lose at Anfield
Sports.content:
Fabian Hurzeler aims thinly-veiled dig at Liverpool after Brighton lose at Anfield

Brighton suffered just their second defeat in 13 games this season as Liverpool's first half double did the damage at Anfield, much to the annoyance of Fabian Hurzeler

View 2 Images Fabian Hurzeler had a dig at Liverpool post-match (Image: Getty Images)

Fabian Hurzeler believes Brighton were the only side "who really tried to create and win", despite suffering a 2-0 defeat by Liverpool.

‌



‌



Quickfire first-half goals from Andoni Iraola's side settled the Premier League clash at Anfield on Sunday. Florian Wirtz's effort went in off Pascal Gross for an own goal before Alexander Isak tucked in Bradley Barcola's cross four minutes later.

‌



Yasin Ayari fired Brighton's best chance over the crossbar before striking the post with another attempt. The Seagulls could not respond to the early blitz and suffered just their second defeat in 13 games across all competitions this season.

‌



Hurzeler's side boasted 64 per cent possession and had 1.35 xG to Liverpool's 0.87 xG, but couldn't make it count, registering just one shot on target to the Reds' four. And there was more than just a hint of sour grapes in the Brighton boss' post-match press conference.

‌



"Everyone in the stadium saw that there was one team who really tried to create and try to win this game and therefore I have to praise my players," Hurzeler said. "Everyone in the stadium felt there was a missed opportunity for us, because it's not only after the goal or the goals they scored.

"Also, before they scored, we had one, two big chances and today I think it was just the difference that they scored, we didn't score.

‌



"Overall I saw a team with a lot of good things to take away. I saw a team that really had the belief in our approach, that stuck to the match plan, that always kept going, and that is very frustrating because we all have the feeling that there is a missed opportunity here today."

‌



View 2 Images Alexander Isak made it 2-0 for Liverpool in the 21st minute (Image: Jan Kruger/Getty Images)

Brighton are still third in the Premier League, a point ahead of Liverpool, whose fourth straight win in all competitions moved them up to fourth place. "I think we had today a very good opposition in front, similar to Villarreal the other day – teams that technically are really good," Iraola said post-match. "It's difficult to defend them a lot of times.

‌



"I think today the key was how we started. We needed a stronger start, be aggressive, recover the ball, win our duels, be dangerous in transitions.

"I think we've done it and it has been a different game from the last ones, where we've conceded first and after you need a comeback. Today, I think we've started better and the game has gone differently."

‌



Isak netted his sixth goal of the season and earned some individual praise from his manager. "He's a striker if we can put him in those positions, we can provide him with crosses, good situations, he will score the goals," he said.

"I think it's a matter of, in this case, Bradley winning the duel, going one-v-one, being faster than the opposition and finding good spots."

Sports.title: Harry Maguire points finger for Man Utd loss and speaks out on Michael Carrick's future
Sports.content:
Harry Maguire points finger for Man Utd loss and speaks out on Michael Carrick's future

Manchester United were beaten 3-0 at Old Trafford by Bournemouth, putting even more pressure on struggling boss Michael Carrick

View 2 Images Harry Maguire has given his verdict on Michael Carrick (Image: https://www.youtube.com/@manutd)

Harry Maguire has voiced his support for Michael Carrick amid mounting calls for the Manchester United manager to be sacked. The Red Devils fell to yet another Premier League defeat at the hands of Bournemouth, with their last win in the league coming in August against Ipswich Town.

‌



‌



The Cherries ran out emphatic 3-0 winners at Old Trafford, with goals from Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson putting the seal on a miserable afternoon for the home side. Despite this representing Carrick's third Premier League defeat in eight games, Maguire remains firmly in his manager's corner and believes the players themselves must shoulder the blame for their recent poor form.

‌



Reacting to the game on BBC MOTD, he said: "We're fully behind Michael [Carrick], coming into the team last season he turned things around and got Champions League football this season. As individuals, we're not playing well enough."

‌



Maguire also gave a scathing overview of their Old Trafford display, stating that there was a crisis of confidence within the dressing room. He said: "Very disappointed. Coming to the game we wanted to get a win for our fans and to concede another set play for the first goal is not good enough.

Michael Carrick on brink as Man Utd fans make voices heard in Bournemouth hammering READ MORE :

"We have to remain focused and when things aren't going your way you can't be giving away set plays. The second goal is a mistake and then we're 2-0 down at half time and we couldn't react. There's a lack of confidence at the moment - the results, the performances we have to look at ourselves and find something within ourselves to bring more to the team.

‌



"That's every player that I'm talking about. When things aren't going your way you have to do the basics well and conceding set plays, a simple set play is just nowhere near good enough.

"It's an individual thing - we have to stick together as a team. So early on in the season - we can still have a good season but something has got to change quick. It's been disappointing, that has to change."

‌



Carrick shouldered his share of the blame for the woeful result, conceding he feels a sense of "responsibility" for the way things are currently unfolding at United. He told Sky Sports: "It was a strange, mixed of emotions at the end of the game. It wasn't a nice way to end the game.

View 2 Images Maguire backs Carrick all the way (Image: Stu Forster/Getty Images)

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

"It was a tough day for the players. We went into the game having been rocked. You can feel that. They're really hurting and disappointed in there. It's not a nice feeling. You have to accept it, we're in that situation."

‌



He added: "It's really difficult to have a day like this at this football club and feel the emotion and dynamics of what it was like today. Not for me personally but for Manchester United.

"It was really mixed. I feel responsibility with the position I'm in. I've been at the club a long time. It hurts a lot going through this."

‌



Manchester United have a challenging fixture ahead against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge, followed by a home Champions League clash with Roma.

Sports.title: How worried should England be after another unfathomable defeat?
Sports.content:
It's not just Manchester United who've had a chastening week.

The England cricket team have shown they are more than capable of crumbling, too.

If losing once from a dominant position could be considered misfortune then to do it twice in four days is just plain careless.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from last Thursday's ODI as Sri Lanka stunned England by pulling off a chase of 430 - the second-highest in the format's history

If you look at the last two games, we've been in positions where we should have won, so that is a massive positive as a group. If in a year's time we do get to those situations again and bank on our previous experiences then we'll look back at this tri-series as a huge positive.

That is not to denigrate the achievements of Sri Lanka for chasing down a colossal 430 and Pakistan for their successful pursuit of 242 after having been 154-9. Those should be lauded.

But they did expose a few cracks in England that were not really visible during the home ODI summer as Harry Brook's team recorded bilateral series wins over India and Sri Lanka.

England are not in the disarray Manchester United are. The coach won't be sacked and the captain is unlikely to be dropped for slamming the coach's tactics. But there are things to fix. Some easy, others a little more difficult.

England missing senior players, including Archer

It is worth noting that an England side sat on three defeats from three in the tri-series - they lost their first game against Pakistan after botching a chase of 303 - is missing some key personnel.

Image: England's Jos Buttler (left) and Jofra Archer (right) are missing the tri-series through injury and rest respectively

Jos Buttler (injured), Jacob Bethell (recovering from injury) and Jofra Archer (rested) are not here. Adil Rashid has not been picked for the last two matches. Josh Tongue missed Sunday's loss.

Having Rashid - whose recent omission has been somewhat of a mystery - and Archer would clearly have bolstered the bowling, while Bethell and Buttler could have acted as strong sounding boards for Brook when things started to unravel in the field.

Bethell and Buttler's absences were also keenly felt with the bat as, let's be honest, that is where this weekend's game was lost.

The Lahore strip was not the Rawalpindi road on which England and Sri Lanka struck a combined 859 runs but neither was it a minefield.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The best of Shadab's unbeaten hundred in Lahore as he put on a match-winning 89-run partnership with last man Haris Rauf

The fact Pakistan's No 8 (Shadab Khan) scored 113 not out and England's No 10 (Gus Atkinson) hit an unbeaten 36 shows you that.

England's 241 all out was under par. They should probably never have defended it. It's just the way they failed to defend it that rankled.

The lack of middle-overs wickets that blighted England against Sri Lanka - and has done in ODIs for some time - was not an issue versus Pakistan as Jamie Overton and Liam Dawson excelled.

This time the problems came when their opponents were nine down.

Image: What role should Sam Curran have in England's ODI side?

England's Curran conundrum

During the dismal 2025 Champions Trophy campaign in Pakistan - losing all three of their games - England were crying out for the variety Sam Curran's left-arm box of tricks provides.

Since his white-ball reinstatement, Curran has made a difference, notably with a clutch final over as England staved off a humbling defeat to Nepal in the T20 World Cup in India earlier this year.

But he has had a tough time in Pakistan over the last few days, perhaps owing to the rustiness caused by missing the last two months with a groin injury.

None of Curran's variations have really worked.

His moon balls, bouncers and yorkers have been more predictable than Manchester United getting to the autumn and changing manager. A stage we may be at again.

Image: Sam Curran (right) recorded the most-expensive England ODI bowling figures against Sri Lanka, with 2-103 from nine overs

Curran's 42 with the bat helped rally England from 52-4 against Pakistan and, in isolation, his bowling figures of 0-32 from eight overs are solid. That doesn't tell the entire story, though.

In his fifth, sixth and seventh overs, Curran offered up boundary balls to Shadab and then a single, while also failing to sufficiently test No 11 Haris Rauf when he had the opportunity.

Three days prior, the all-rounder was flogged for England's most-expensive ODI bowling figures as Brook persevered with him for too long. Curran's 2-103 from nine overs against Sri Lanka trumped his own 0-98 from 9.5 overs versus West Indies back in 2023.

Stuart Broad is one of many who think you get the best out of Curran when he has a defined and prominent role - and England need to work out what that is as he feels rather bit-part at the moment. If his toils with the ball continue that could be no part.

McCullum: England 'gutted' by ODI defeats England head coach Brendon McCullum: “We will learn from this. The boys are gutted, to be honest. They were gutted after the last game and they're even more gutted after this one. "These boys are immensely talented, they're incredibly driven to perform for England. “We know that we're not the best side that we can be just yet but that's the challenge that's in front of us. "There's some good lessons and learning opportunities and we will learn from it because we are desperate to get to South Africa and have a realistic chance of challenging for that World Cup. “When you've got an inexperienced line-up and you've got a big World Cup in 12 months' time and you've only got 20 games between now and then, you need to have that level of communication and those examples of real time experiences."

Should Overton continue to excel in the middle overs, banging out a hard length and nabbing crucial wickets Liam Plunkett-style, and offer a bit more with the bat than he is currently doing, Curran could be at risk, especially if England want to get another out-and-out seamer into the XI as they prepare for the 2027 World Cup in Africa.

Why is Rashid not playing?

They also need to find a way for Rashid to return to the side at some stage - unless the leg-spinner's recent absence is because they have moved on from a man who has been a linchpin for well over a decade.

The fact Rashid, 38, is in the squad to tour Australia next month would suggest not. His spell on the bench is perhaps due to still working back to full fitness following a hand injury that ended his home summer prematurely.

But his ODI figures in 2026 have not been amazing - nine wickets in seven games at an average of 36.22 and a strike-rate of 37.50 after a quality 2025 when he averaged two wickets a game (30 in 15 fixtures at an average of 23.63 and strike-rate of 24.10).

Image: Adil Rashid has been left out of England's last two ODIs

Sky Sports' Nasser Hussain said last week that Rashid's performances had "dropped off".

Rashid being omitted for Liam Dawson - who has done excellently in the tri-series, it must be said - for tactical reasons in Rawalpindi and again in Lahore has raised questions that were not there before.

Questions across the board are inevitable when you fluff your lines twice in a week. At least coach Brendon McCullum, perhaps unlike Michael Carrick at Manchester United after Como and Bournemouth drubbings, will be around to try and provide the answers.

Sports.title: Kane, Mbappe and Lamine Yamal - who should win men's 2026 Ballon d'Or?
Sports.content:
Harry Kane is the odds-on favourite to win the 2026 men’s Ballon d’Or, which could be one of the tightest results in recent history.

England captain and Bayern Munich striker Kane is the bookmakers' favourite to become the first Englishman to win the award since Michael Owen in 2001.

Victory would see Kane become just the fifth English winner of the Ballon d'Or after Sir Stanley Matthews, Sir Bobby Charlton, Kevin Keegan and Owen, while he would also become the first Bayern player to claim it in 45 years.

When asked after Bayern's Champions League draw against Arsenal last Wednesday about winning the Ballon d'Or, Kane told Sky Sports News: "It'd be incredible if I do. It'd be special for sure. I'd love to win it, but we will have to wait and see. A big night, but I'm not getting carried away."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Harry Kane gives his thoughts ahead of Monday's Ballon d'Or ceremony

Kane's caution comes due to stiff competition from LaLiga duo Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe.

Spain World Cup winner and Barcelona forward Lamine Yamal, who is 14 years Kane's junior at the age of 19, is aiming to become the youngest-ever Ballon d'Or winner - an award he has been campaigning for.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News’ David Reed delves into whether or not age has an impact on who wins the Ballon d'Or

"Being completely honest, it's not just this year I've been at a Ballon d'Or [winning] level, but longer," he told The Guardian in September, having also appeared to dismiss Kane's credentials earlier that month in a Spanish interview.

Lamine Yamal had been the bookmakers' closest challenger to Kane for the award, but a late surge in the betting means Real Madrid striker and France captain Kylian Mbappe is now second-favourite behind Kane.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kylian Mbappe's double gave Real Madrid a win at rivals Barcelona on Sunday

A first-time winner looks set to win the award on Monday night, with Kane eyeing a poetic victory in London, where the ceremony is being held to pay tribute to inaugural winner Matthews.

Here, Sky Sports assesses Kane, Lamine Yamal and Mbappe's stats, and hears the pundits' views on who should win the 70th edition of the Ballon d'Or…

The honours…

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' David Reed explains the complicated process behind how the Ballon d'Or winner is chosen

It is important to note that players are judged for their performances over the entirety of last season from August 3, 2025 until July 19, 2026.

Looking at that period domestically, Kane helped Bayern to lift the Bundesliga and the German Cup, while Lamine Yamal won LaLiga but missed out on the Copa del Rey as both players won their respective Super Cups.

But Mbappe failed to win a trophy with either Real Madrid or France last season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player We take a look at all Harry Kane's goals for Bayern Munich in the Bundesliga last season

In Europe, Kane went further than Lamine Yamal and Mbappe as Bayern reached the Champions League semi-finals after a thrilling 6-5 last-four aggregate defeat to eventual winners Paris Saint-Germain.

Lamine Yamal's Barcelona and Mbappe's Real Madrid both exited the tournament in the quarter-finals.

But Lamine Yamal enjoyed the ultimate success with his country as he helped Spain earn World Cup glory in the summer, while Kane and England won the bronze medal after beating Mbappe's France in the third-place play-off.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A look at Lamine Yamal's best league goals for Barcelona last season

The stats…

The goal statistics are what make Kane the favourite for the award.

He hit an astonishing 73 goals for club and country last season, while Mbappe fired in 58 and Lamine Yamal scored 25 goals.

Kane's goal-laden campaign led to the ex-Tottenham striker picking up the Golden Shoe, the award for Europe's leading goal scorer, for a second time after he claimed it in 2023/24 in his debut Bayern season.

Kane hit 61 goals for Bayern across all competitions last season, 19 more than any other player in Europe's big-five leagues. In fact, it was the most by a player in a season since Cristiano Ronaldo scored 61 for Real Madrid in 2014/15.

Kane also scored 12 goals for England, with his six goals in the Three Lions' 2026 World Cup semi-final run seeing him become England's all-time leading World Cup scorer.

But Mbappe scored more goals than Kane at the World Cup and in last season's Champions League.

The ex-PSG forward won this year's World Cup Golden Boot with 10 goals - the most by a player in a single edition since Gerd Muller scored 10 in 1970 for West Germany.

The 27-year-old is now the all-time scorer in World Cup history with 22 goals.

At club level last season, Mbappe was the top goal scorer in LaLiga (25 goals) and in the Champions League, despite Real's last-eight exit, as he scored 15 goals - one more than Kane.

It was a quiet World Cup for Lamine Yamal, scoring only once in Spain's run to glory as team-mates Rodri and Pau Cubarsi picked up the player of the tournament and young player award, respectively.

Lamine Yamal, however, came into his first World Cup off the back of a hamstring injury which had initially led to doubts whether he would even play in the tournament.

Lamine Yamal picked up the injury in mid-April while playing for Barcelona, and he missed the remainder of the season before making his return as a substitute in Spain's goalless draw in their World Cup opener against Cape Verde on June 15, with his first start coming six days later as he scored Spain's first in their win over Saudi Arabia.

Despite his disrupted preparation for the tournament, he made the most dribbles both at the World Cup (58) and across Europe's top-five leagues (265) during the 2025/26 season.

Where Lamine Yamal is superior to Kane and Mbappe is in the assist column.

The winger provided 20 assists for club and country last season, while Mbappe had 13 and Kane had just eight.

It takes Lamine Yamal's goal involvements to 45, but that figure is not close to Kane's 81 and Mbappe's 71.

Sports.title: Thunder star Williams stretched off with leg injury
Sports.content:
Jalen Williams: Oklahoma City Thunder star stretchered off with significant leg injury in win over Los Angeles Clippers

Oklahoma City Thunder guard Jalen Williams suffered a significant injury during their victory on Sunday

Oklahoma City Thunder star Jalen Williams was taken off the court on a stretcher after suffering a significant lower-leg injury during their 108-101 victory over the Los Angeles Clippers.

Williams - a shooting guard who entered Sunday having averaged 18 points per game in his first 250 NBA contests - has been an All-Star and an All-NBA player already in his career, was a huge part of the Thunder team that won the 2024-25 NBA title.

He injured his lower left leg and saw his ankle turn in an unnatural angle in a drive with 1:14 remaining, with Williams immediately treated by medical personnel after going down underneath the basket on the Thunder's offensive end.

Williams' ankle was draped by towels before a stretcher was brought out, with players left visibly shaken by the incident and the game stopped for around five minutes before the Thunder completed their victory.

Williams looked emotional after seeing his injury before going off to a standing ovation

"Just feel bad for him," Thunder guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander said in a post-match interview, fighting back tears as he spoke. "Nothing more than that."

Williams, seated up on the stretcher, saluted the cheering fans with two thumbs-up signals as he was wheeled off the court.

There was no immediate diagnosis from the Thunder, though it was clear that the injury was severe - and the stretcher was called for within just a few seconds of the play ending.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

Oklahoma City coach Mark Daigneault said the team would be briefed Monday morning with the latest updates on Williams' condition.

"Our whole city will have JDub in our thoughts and prayers as he deals with this adversity and as he makes his way through his recovery," Oklahoma City Mayor David Holt posted on social media after the game.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

Williams missed 49 games last season with an array of issues, mostly hamstring problems and recovery from a significant surgery on his right wrist.

"He just loves playing, loves the competition," Gilgeous-Alexander said. "That's who he is. It's unfortunate, his luck so far. But he's equipped for it."

Sports.title: Smith beats Schindler in Dortmund thriller after Littler's QF exit
Sports.content:
Ross Smith has won the Machineseeker European Championship for a second time after overcoming a late Martin Schindler fightback to claim an 11-8 victory in Dortmund.

The 2022 champion fired a 107 average in his last-eight victory over Luke Woodhouse and rallied from 4-1 down to beat Gerwyn Price 11-7, setting up a showdown against German No 1 Schindler at Westfalenhallen.

Smith edged a tight opening session before reeling off six straight legs against Schindler, who almost fell 9-2 behind before capitalising on some wayward finishing to sneak a 20-dart break of throw.

Schindler was broken in the next but offered a four-leg burst - including finishes of 116 and 127 - to cut the deficit to 9-7 and threaten a famous comeback, but the next three legs went with throw as Smith closed out victory and the £150,000 first prize.

Victory sees Smith join Michael van Gerwen, Phil Taylor, Rob Cross and Peter Wright as the only players to win multiple European Championship titles, with his latest success following his World Series of Darts title in September and lifting him to world No 6.

Machineseeker European Championship results Quarter-Finals: Ross Smith 10-6 Luke Woodhouse, Gerwyn Price 10-3 Stephen Bunting, Martin Schindler 10-1 Jonny Clayton, Krzysztof Ratajski 10-6 Luke Littler Semi-Finals: Ross Smith 11-7 Gerwyn Price, Martin Schindler 11-6 Krzysztof Ratajski Final: Ross Smith 11-8 Martin Schindler

"I'm not going to lie, I was a bit sweaty there going to that end with Martin - he wouldn't let up, would he!" Smith said. "Full credit to him. To have this trophy in my hands, to win another major - I'm absolutely over the moon and drained, but I'm buzzing!"

Luke Littler was the pre-tournament favourite to claim the only missing ranked major from his glittering CV, only for the world No 1 to suffer a shock quarter-final exit to Krzysztof Ratajaski.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Luke Littler failed to win a maiden European Championship as he suffered a surprise defeat at the hands of Krzysztof Ratajski (Credit: ITV)

How Smith secured Dortmund title

Schindler thrashed Jonny Clayton 10-1 and despatched Ratajaski - who eliminated Littler 11-6 in the previous round - to reach his maiden ranked TV final, with the German missing chances to grab the early lead against Smith.

He wasted multiple opportunities to break in the third leg but responded with a 14-dart hold in the next, levelling the match, before Smith quickly pulled away.

Image: Smith came into the event as No 1 seed after a strong season on the PDC European Tour

Smith took out an 86 finish to break and kept the German crowd quiet by sweeping all five legs in the next mini session, with Schindler only allowed back in when his opponent squandered five darts at double to open a seven-leg lead.

The pair traded breaks of throw before Schindler followed a 15-dart hold by firing successive ton-plus checkouts, with Smith stuttering over the closing legs before wrapping up victory with his fifth match dart.

Sports.title: 'Quality of drivers very low' - Alonso criticises Albon after clash
Sports.content:
Aston Martin's Fernando Alonso hit out at Williams' Alex Albon and stated the quality of drivers in the bottom third of the grid is "very low" after the pair collided at the United States Grand Prix.

Albon tried to overtake Alonso for 12th place into the Turn 11 hairpin on the opening lap, but went into the side of the Aston Martin driver, damaging both cars.

Neither driver received a penalty and both were able to continue with Alonso finishing 16th and Albon in 17th in Austin.

"Albon forgot Turn 11 was there and he had to turn left," said Alonso.

"We need to get better and start a little bit higher up because the bottom third of the grid, the quality of the drivers is very low at the moment."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 United States Grand Prix

Alonso qualified 12th, his joint-best Saturday result of the season, and thinks points were on the cards if not for the damage, which cost him around half a second per lap.

"It was the best race by far of the year for us in terms of competitiveness. Good tyre management. We got a lot of damage on Lap 1 with the Albon incident," he said.

"Despite that, the car was still competitive. We had a P9 or P10 on merit. The best and strongest race of the year but ruined in the first lap with the Turn 11 incident."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Carlos Sainz and Alex Albon sit down with Sky Sports for a chat over Texas BBQ in Austin

Albon felt he did not need need to apologise for the collision with Alonso as Esteban Ocon was on the outside of the Spaniard and also played a role in the incident.

"It's racing. I think there was a car on his outside that squeezed [him]. I was side by side with him the whole way into the corner. It's hard to disappear," said the Williams driver.

"I thought we had some good racing. We had a second go at it later in the race. I enjoyed it at least. I hope he feels the same way on the second half. It was good fun."

Sports.title: 'The pace was rubbish' - Russell in blunt admission after Austin struggle
Sports.content:
George Russell admitted his pace in the United States Grand Prix was "rubbish", with the Mercedes driver at a loss to why he trailed race-winning team-mate Kimi Antonelli by such a large margin.

Russell finished 54 seconds behind the sister Mercedes in the 56-lap race in an eighth place that only just kept him in mathematical championship contention heading to this week's race in Mexico, where Antonelli is set to clinch the crown.

Russell had held his grid position of sixth through the race's first stint but dropped to eighth after serving a five-second penalty at his sole pit stop for an incident with Oscar Piastri in the opening lap, when he was judged to have gained an advantage over the McLaren by running off track and retaining position.

Russell subsequently spent the final 26 laps on the similarly one-stopping Piastri's tail but was unable to find a way back past.

Russell told Sky Sports F1: "The pace was rubbish. That's the long and short of it.

"The five-second [penalty] didn't help things and probably cost me two or three positions but the pace wasn't good enough when it needed to be."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli got a flying start at the United States Grand Prix as George Russell was handed a five-second penalty

Russell made no excuse for his lack of competitiveness and said he had no immediate answer for why his Austin weekend was such a struggle.

"Just not been quick enough," he added.

"I need to try and understand why that is. It's strange when you're so far off.

"Hopefully there are some answers somewhere but at the moment I don't have them."

What went wrong for Russell?

Antonelli's win was his ninth of the year and represented what Toto Wolff, Mercedes' team principal, believes was "the best race that he's delivered so far".

It was the first win for Mercedes upgraded car, which has taken time for the world championship leaders to get the best out of since the aerodynamic revisions debuted at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia at the start of October.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 United States Grand Prix

The team have said, however, that the changes have narrowed the car's optimum set-up window.

On Russell's weekend, Wolff said: "George just struggled so much. And I believe this is because the operational window of the car is so difficult.

"In Q2 he was there and thereabouts. Q3, it didn't work. He said, 'that goes on me'.

"And today in the race, I don't know, we got stuck behind Piastri, which looks a bit unfair why he didn't get past. It's the same engine, it's the same electric charging and deployment. But I'm going to see him now."

'He's not 54 seconds slower over a race distance'

Analysis from Sky Sports F1's Jenson Button:

"George has had a lot of tough races but also some great races and that's the thing that's really difficult to understand - how he's able to get the maximum out of that car on some tracks but not at others.

"Austin was difficult as he started so far down. He was in the pack and when you're in the pack, sometimes it's difficult to move forward. You're in the dirty air. You try to do something different with strategy but then you get a five-second penalty which puts you back further.

"I don't believe his pace is that far off. He's not 54 seconds slower over a race distance."

Sports.title: Antonelli wins United States GP but made to wait for world title
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli moved to the brink of becoming Formula 1's youngest-ever world champion with a superb drive to victory in the United States Grand Prix.

Antonelli had an outside chance of clinching the 2026 title as early as Sunday's Austin race provided he won, Lewis Hamilton finished outside the top four and George Russell was ninth or lower.

And while he held up his side of the bargain by brilliantly claiming a ninth win of the season on a one-stop strategy to his nearest rivals' two, Hamilton took fourth and Russell eighth to stay in mathematical contention.

But Antonelli has moved 123 points clear of Russell, and 124 points clear of Hamilton, with just a maximum of 125 left to play for this season to make a coronation at next Sunday's Mexico City Grand Prix all but inevitable.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli got a flying start at the United States Grand Prix as George Russell was handed a five-second penalty

Antonelli, who only turned 20 in August and is in his second season of F1, will definitely clinch the title with four rounds to spare in Mexico if he finishes anywhere in the top nine.

"We are very close," said the Italian, who will also be assured of the title at the next round if neither Russell nor Hamilton win the race.

"We try to finish on a high and hopefully we can clinch it very soon."

Antonelli won at the Circuit of The Americas by 13 seconds with Charles Leclerc finishing a fine second for Ferrari after winning out against Red Bull's Max Verstappen in the battle of the two-stop strategies. Leclerc overtook Verstappen at Turn 12 after an entertaining battle with seven laps to go.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Charles Leclerc makes two great overtakes on Lando Norris and Max Verstappen

Hamilton was fourth, crossing the line just one second behind Verstappen after also fast-catching the Red Bull late on, with Lando Norris fifth on a one-stop strategy ahead of Red Bull's Isack Hadjar.

While Antonelli was peerless up front, team-mate Russell's difficult Austin weekend, and indeed season, was summed up by his disappointing eighth-place finish.

Russell, who had started sixth, dropped behind the McLarens after having to serve a five-second penalty at his sole pit stop after being judged to have gained an advantage by going off track in battle with Oscar Piastri on the first lap.

United States GP Result: Top 10 1) Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes



2) Charles Leclerc, Ferrari



3) Max Verstappen, Red Bull



4) Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari



5) Lando Norris, McLaren



6) Isack Hadjar, Red Bull



7) Oscar Piastri, McLaren



8) George Russell, Mercedes



9) Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls



10) Pierre Gasly, Alpine

The elongated pit stop dropped Russell behind Piastri, whom he was then unable to pass despite following closely for almost half the race. He described his race pace as "rubbish".

Liam Lawson continued his relentless points-scoring form with ninth for Racing Bulls, while Pierre Gasly was 10th for Alpine.

Faultless Antonelli returns to winning ways - and verge of history - in style

Despite his inexperience in just his second year of F1 and the fast-looming spectre of achieving his lifelong dream of becoming world champion, Antonelli had already barely put a foot wrong across the title run-in during a period when Mercedes have rarely had the fastest car.

The Italian had not won a race since his fortuitous triumph at the Spanish Grand Prix in mid-September and Mercedes' most recent upgrade, first brought to the car two races ago in Malaysia, had initially not delivered the results the team had expected.

But any suggestion that the season's world championship-leading team and driver might have to take a defensive approach to the final rounds of this season to get over the title-winning line was firmly put to bed in Austin.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli looks ahead to Mexico as he moves to brink of a title win

Antonelli's pole position - his first in eight races since the Belgian Grand Prix since July - had been perhaps his most unexpected of the season and had led Mercedes boss Toto Wolff to play down the Italian's prospects of victory.

On Sunday, the Italian was alone among the top five on the grid to opt for the medium tyres for the race start and yet, despite his rivals behind having the grippier softs for the crucial uphill run to COTA's wide first corner, Antonelli had a dream getaway and easily converted his starting advantage into a lap-one lead.

It was instead second-placed Verstappen who came under pressure from behind, the Dutchman initially overtaken by Leclerc through the Esses before getting back ahead of the Ferrari into Turn 13 later round the opening lap.

But Antonelli had soon opened an early lead of four seconds and, struggling to keep up, Red Bull pitted Verstappen surprisingly early on lap 13. He took on a second set of soft tyres, locking him into a two-stop race given the requirement to run two different tyre compounds.

Ferrari soon followed suit with their drivers but Mercedes stuck to their guns on a projected one-stopper and did not pit Antonelli until the end of lap 24. When they did they switched him onto the more durable hard compound, ensuring he could go to the end of the race without stopping again.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes Team Principal Toto Wolff says that Kimi Antonelli's performance at the United States Grand Prix was 'exceptional'

Antonelli rejoined in fourth place but was back in the lead by lap 32 by passing the long-running Leclerc.

Verstappen had by then pitted for a second time having run into a more problematic second stint on softs. And while the fresher tyres of the Red Bull and Ferrari into the closing laps meant Antonelli's lead over both came down, neither had sufficient speed to truly cause Mercedes alarm.

"It was the result we needed," said Antonelli. "The whole team deserve it so much.

"All this time putting so much work into bringing this new package and finally seeing the result is very pleasant.

"It was also perfect execution from strategy to call the one-stop. Really happy we made it stick. Today was a great team effort."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen reflects on the United States GP, in which he finished third

Verstappen had looked the most likely to challenge Antonelli on his two-stopper but, in the end, it was Leclerc who got closest.

Ferrari's soft-medium-medium tyre strategy allowed the Monegasque to display impressive turn of speed from his first stop onwards, eventually fighting back from his final stop to pass the long-running Norris and then Verstappen during his final stint.

"It was quite a good race," said Leclerc. "Unfortunately we came short of the victory which was our target.

"At the end of the day, a positive race. We had good pace. The first stint was more difficult."
