Sports.title: Mbappe's late strike earns Mourinho and Real Clasico glory at Barca
Sports.content:
Kylian Mbappe's double took Real Madrid to a famous 2-1 Clasico win, which had Jose Mourinho sliding on his knees in celebration in Barcelona.

It was the 87th minute when Mbappe tucked in from Eduardo Camavinga's cutback following some sublime skill from Jude Bellingham. The celebrations from Real Madrid were wild, with their head coach unable to contain himself, his staff on the pitch, and his players clashing with Barcelona fans.

Real had been on the defensive after Raphinha's snapshot had levelled a pulsating clash, with Lamine Yamal narrowly clipping wide as LaLiga's defending champions pushed for a winner. Instead Real have closed to within three points of their great rivals. Atletico are second just two off Barca now.

Image: Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe celebrates after scoring against Barcelona

It's been a bad week for Hansi Flick's side, whose 11-game winning streak at the start of this season was halted with defeat in the Champions League at Paris St-Germain. This loss will sting far more - it's Real's first win in Barcelona in three years.

Mbappe's opener had been fortuitous, Gerard Martin slamming a clearance in off him. But Real's move to get to that point had been excellent and throughout the contest they showed they were willing to go toe-to-toe with their more favoured hosts.

There was controversy before Raphinha's equaliser, with Joao Cancelo not punished for putting his studs into Yan Diomande's calf. But Mourinho and Real Madrid will leave Spotify Camp Nou celebrating.

Key moments at Spotify Camp Nou...

18: SHOT! It's end-to-end as Guler steps in off the right and forces Garcia into a save moments after Gordon tested Lunin.

Image: Barcelona's Anthony Gordon, right, is challenged by Real Madrid's Arda Guler

24: SHOTS! Raphinha whacks one over the bar from 16 yards and then links up brilliantly with Gordon before bending a low effort just wide.

33: OVER! Mbappe scissor-kicks over the bar after a brilliant move featuring a big Bellingham tackle and Guler's gorgeous cross.

41: GOAL! Mbappe gives Real the lead when Gerard Martin whacks the ball against him from Diomande's cross into the box! A bizarre goal at the end of a fine team move from the visitors.

50: CHANCE! But Bellingham can't find the pass to Mbappe after skipping away on the counter to set up a two-on-one against Martin, who shuts him down.

57: CONTROVERSY! Cancelo puts his studs into Diomande's calf. The Real winger continues his attack before going to ground - but there's no retrospective punishment for the Barca defender.

61: GOAL! Pedri reverses a pass into Raphinha and his snapshot beats Lunin, who got a hand to the ball but couldn't keep the equaliser out.

Image: Barcelona's Raphinha celebrates after scoring against Real Madrid

66: SAVE! An amazing save from Lunin, as he claws away Martin's powerful header from a corner.

78: CLOSE! Lamine Yamal skips past a couple of challenges then clips a shot at goal - but the ball bounces just wide.

87: GOAL! Mbappe sensationally wins it for Real, slotting in after Camavinga cuts the ball back to him following sublime skill from Bellingham.

Mourinho not happy Cancelo was not sent off

Real Madrid head coach Jose Mourinho:

"First of all, I think it was a great match. A high-level match. One that the whole football-loving world surely stopped to watch, and wasn't disappointed, with two teams that played to win.

"In our case, it's more my place to talk about my own team than the other. The boys played an extraordinary match: very organized, very focused, with a lot of courage to play out from the back against an opponent that presses hard. We had good chances to make it 2-0 at the end of the first half.

"At the start of the second half, we had a situation with Jude and Kylian. Obviously, Barcelona, being behind, had a strong reaction in the second half, but we always stayed very calm and organized.

"At 1-1 we never lost our composure. For me, it was a great victory for the boys, I repeat, against a great opponent, with a referee who I think did a very good job, and a VAR that was asleep at minute 60 on a decision that could surely have had a big influence on the match: a clear red card for João on Diomandé.

"But a great match for me, a great match, a great victory, and the boys deserve it."

Mbappe: Real Madrid back in title race

Mbappe celebrated the "team victory" that brought Real Madrid back into the LaLiga title race, saying it sent a "good message."

"In the end, winning and still being in the title race is very important for us," Mbappé told Real Madrid TV. "But we have to keep going.

"We know it's a big game, but it's worth three points, and we need a lot of points to win the league. Today sends a good message but we can't think that the season is over, because nothing has been decided.

"It's a team victory. The credit goes to the team and the group, because we knew we had to play like men, but also as a team.

"We prepared well in our recent games because we won and played well. We came into this with the right mentality, and today we gave everything we had.

"If we want to have any hopes of achieving things this year, we have to do it as a group and as a team, because the quality is here/ When you look at the players here, anyone who says there's no quality is a liar.

"But we have to do everything as a team and as a group, because that's how we're going to achieve what we want to achieve.

"Everyone knows I like scoring goals and helping the team that way. But I think today that's just a detail. This victory will give the group a lot of confidence, and there will be many more goals, so it's not that important."

Flick: Barca lacked freshness

Barcelona head coach Hansi Flick:

"We had two defeats and we're disappointed. First half was not good. Second half, after 1-1, was better. We controlled the game. We missed a little bit of luck. Against the ball they gave us not so much space.

"You could see today we missed also the freshness.

"It's our first defeat in LaLiga. We won nine in a row. It happens, defeats are a part of the game. Now we have to analyse, make things better, and this we'll do. Now it's important we make a reaction.

"It's a long way until the end of the season."

Sports.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
Sports.content:
1 Cherries buy smart while United burn billions

The three Bournemouth goalscorers cost a combined £85m, joining from Vasco da Gama, Middlesbrough, and Porto. The Cherries are smart at investing, far more so than Manchester United, who have wasted a lot of money by failing to look outside the box for players like Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson. United may not have the wealth they previously showed in the transfer market but Bournemouth are showing what can be done within a budget and, more importantly, will be able to make a profit on signings. United, however, only know losses as everyone’s price tag diminishes the moment they come through the Old Trafford door. Jason Wilcox and others can point to certain factors that are against them but there are quality signings to be made at the right price if you have the ability to find them. Will Unwin

View image in fullscreen Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox look on dejectedly at Old Trafford after another loss. Photograph: Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images

2 Suzuki slots in seamlessly

Aston Villa were quite happy to sell Emiliano Martínez but many feared it would be difficult to find an upgrade on the World Cup-winning goalkeeper. They have seemingly done so in the form of the £30m signing Zion Suzuki, who was superb against Manchester City. Nicolas Jackson’s goals stole the headlines but Suzuki’s bounty of saves ensured that Villa were victorious, while also impressing with his distribution. ”He’s ambitious. I think it’s very important, his mentality,” Unai Emery said. “Of course, we need a keeper first to save us in the goal, but as well we need one keeper to try to help us in our buildup. And in buildup, he’s a really fantastic player because he can play short, he can understand where is the superiority to break the opponent’s press. He has qualities to do long ball, getting our players in attack. So, we are very, very impressed how he adapted so quick with us.” WU

3 Anfield warms to Araújo’s fighting spirit

Aside from the reaction to the half-time and full-time scores from Old Trafford, the biggest noise at Anfield was generated by Ronald Araújo showing no mercy in his challenges on Malick Yalcouyé and Charalampos Kostoulas. The on-loan Barcelona defender immediately endeared himself to the Kop with his commitment and quality, and was again in commanding form to help Andoni Iraola record his first Premier League home win as Liverpool head coach. “I think we all enjoyed watching Ronald fighting,” said Iraola. “He’s very good in the duels. Even the first goal, he wins two duels in a row and defensively he’s been really, really good. I’m happy for him because I’ve taken him out in the last two games because we needed more offensive things. But he has continued working with no issues and today we needed him more. He has given a very, very good 90 minutes.” Andy Hunter

4 Striker problems at the Bridge

João Pedro is unlikely to make a swift return after picking up an injury in training. The Chelsea striker missed the defeat to Tottenham and had a scan on Sunday. Xabi Alonso did not sound optimistic after the Spurs game. The expectation is João Pedro will miss this week’s games against Liverpool and Manchester United as a minimum, leaving Alonso with problems in attack. It was strange he did not start Danny Welbeck against Spurs. Chelsea had no focal point and there are questions over their depth. Emmanuel Emegha, another struggling with injury, is yet to play since joining from Strasbourg. It is fair to wonder if selling Nicolas Jackson to Villa was the right move. Chelsea have played two league games without João Pedro this season and have lost both without scoring a goal. Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers are not as effective without him. Jacob Steinberg

View image in fullscreen Mateus Fernandes challenges Cole Palmer during Tottenham’s 2-0 win. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

5 Arteta says he is not worst strayer

Mikel Arteta says he has been compiling a dossier of evidence of other managers straying outside the technical area after the Arsenal manager was shown a yellow card during the 2-0 win over Everton. It was his second of the season and leaves the Spaniard at risk of suspension if he gets one more, although Arteta suggested he is by no means the worst offender. “There are managers who have the record in the league, 36 times in 10 minutes [they] leave the touchline – no yellows,” he said, naming no names. “I am clipping all of that so I now have a massive storage of images, so if somebody comes to me I can say: ‘I am not in the record yet.’ Somebody else has the record so let’s see. Then it’s 36 yellow cards in 10 minutes for the managers. I don’t know what we are going to do – let’s see.” Ed Aarons

6 González increases his value at Newcastle

Nico González cost Manchester City £50m when they signed him early in 2025, as part of that January spree as Pep Guardiola tried to arrest the first real slump of his Premier League career. Although he started nine league games that season and 17 last, González made very little impact at the Etihad. He probably wasn’t even the best Nico González in world football, given the Argentinian winger’s performances for Juventus and Atlético. But the Spanish Nico González clearly is a player of substance, his calm in midfield one of the few undoubted positives for Newcastle so far this season. Only Lewis Hall has made more tackles per game than him, he set up Sven Botman’s goal at Coventry, while he’s made more key passes per game than anybody other than Harvey Barnes. At £48m, he may end up representing extremely good value. Jonathan Wilson

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

7 Sunderland earn a good point

To ask a question that might be a segment on the Football Cliches podcast, is there a more “swirling litter” venue in the Premier League than the Stadium of Light? At this point it should be obvious this was not a classic. In part that is down the conditions – long balls ran away from players on both sides with frequency, and crisp packets were the only thing to trouble the nets at either end. Managing the Europa League was always going to be a challenge for Sunderland and returning from a midweek trip to Poland to earn a point against a team who have had a week to prepare is a good result, even if the Black Cats finish the weekend at the foot of the table. Tom Bassam

Match report: Sunderland 0-0 Leeds

8 Bobb eases the pressure on Arbeloa

In spectacular style, Oscar Bobb’s wait for a first Premier League goal for Fulham came to an end at Coventry. Bobb was signed in January, fitting the recruitment template that brought success and stability under Marco Silva, a manager adept at regenerating talent. Social media footage from the away end showed Fulham fans ask what Bobb, weaving and bobbing, was doing only for him to feint past two Coventry defenders and score. That broke the deadlock when Coventry appeared fully capable of claiming a point or better. It remains to be seen whether Álvaro Arbeloa possesses the some restorative powers as Silva. After two wins in succession, two clean sheets and a first win away from Craven Cottage since February, early-season panic has dissipated. For now. If survival is Fulham’s first objective, then successive wins over the promoted teams Hull and Coventry were minimum requirements. Though should Fulham aim much higher? Silva departed because his ambitions were not met. John Brewin

View image in fullscreen Oscar Bobb blows a kiss to the Fulham fans after scoring against Coventry. Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Action Images/Reuters

9 Brentford struggle to make chances count

Brentford are still yet to win away from home in the league but are also unbeaten on their travels. The draws at Leeds, Bournemouth and Aston Villa can be considered decent results, but this goes in the missed opportunity pile. So far Hull have presented a stiffer challenge at MKM Stadium than predicted, but in terms of expectations for Brentford this fixture has more in common with playing Sunderland at home than it does with their previous draws on the road. Against Sunderland and at Hull, Keith Andrews’ side struggled when the onus was on the them to make the game. The Bees play like they would rather not have the ball. In this one, they had plenty of shots – 14 in total – but only Dango Ouattara and belatedly Jaidon Anthony truly troubled Konstantinos Tzolakis. Brentford need Igor Thiago firing again. TB

10 Delap under pressure to find the net

With Nottingham Forest the Premier League’s joint-lowest scorers, the pressure on Liam Delap is increasing. At Ipswich, where he was a rare bright spot with 12 goals in the relegation season of 2024-25, Delap was booed on every touch. The jeers got louder when each of his four attempts on goal missed their target. Only three of 18 Premier League shots in a Forest shirt have been on target. The raw materials that Chelsea moved for in summer 2025 remain present, the physical prowess and ability to find promising positions. The finishing touches are, at present, lacking, when Forest need someone to start scoring. Failing to take their chances at Portman Road left Forest in the relegation zone, endangering Oliver Glasner, when the ownership is trigger-happy with managers. Chris Wood, previously Forest’s talisman, came on in the 89th minute for Delap, but has been no super-sub so far, without a goal or assist from seven cameo league appearances. JB

Sports.title: Fernandes gamble leaves Carrick to carry the can for United’s institutional failures | Will Unwin
Sports.content:
Dropping your captain, who has held the team together for most of the past five years, is a bold move from a man whose job is on the line. It was very much a make-or-break decision from Michael Carrick to leave out Bruno Fernandes against Bournemouth. It did not work and Carrick knew the consequences if it failed and will probably pay the price for it, but he should not be alone.

Carrick said the decision to drop the Portuguese playmaker was purely based on football reasons but criticising his manager after the desperate defeat to Como cannot have helped. Clearly Carrick disagreed with his captain’s comments on the lack of pressing in the Champions League fixture. It was somewhat telling that Lisandro Martínez kept his place despite pointing out the director of football, Jason Wilcox, was a hindrance to the club the previous week.

Fernandes has been a long way from his best this season, with three goals and one assist in the Premier League, all in one game against Ipswich. It would have been justifiable to give someone else an opportunity in the No 10 role, especially when the squad contains far too many of those. But then, no one at United is in form, so keeping an angry Fernandes in position may have made more sense. United have won almost half the Premier League fixtures Fernandes has started since he joined in 2020, and less than a third when he is absent.

Some question Fernandes’ attitude based on his complaints when things are not going right, but that is his way of showing he cares. He may not be a leader in the Bryan Robson or Roy Keane mould but is certainly the one who sets the example, shown by a banner in the Stretford End depicting the two former captains and Eric Cantona alongside the word “STANDARDS”. Those have dipped here. This is a mid-table team, made worse by a lack of desire.

Everything was pedestrian in thought and execution. One promising attack lost momentum and United decided the most sensible course of action was to pass the ball all the way back to Senne Lammens, resulting in deserved boos. It felt like a moment that indicated Carrick’s days were coming to an end.

Hypotheticals are pointless, as was Youri Tielemans, Fernandes’ replacement. The central midfielder has not impressed since joining from Aston Villa in the summer and the extra responsibility for an experienced player did not spur him on. He was ponderous in midfield, repeatedly losing the ball as he struggled to cope with the pace of the game against a Bournemouth team eager to press and hunt in pairs. The No 10 is supposed to be a creative influence in the final third but the Belgian was a lost boy against men.

View image in fullscreen The Stretford End made it clear with their banner what they think is missing at Manchester United. Photograph: Simon Stacpoole/Offside/Getty Images

A poorly defended first goal resulted in the inevitable cutting by the cameras to a sullen Fernandes sunk into his seat on the bench. It was a goal that summed up the mood at Old Trafford, Rayan was left in space to volley home at the back post after Ayden Heaven needlessly gave away a free-kick. He looked miserable and the majority inside the ground felt exactly the same.

United lack pace across the pitch so require someone in key areas to speed up play, but Tielemans is not capable of doing so. His main influence on the match was getting booked in the first half, which all but confirmed his exit at the break. It was telling that Carrick turned to Matheus Cunha to take over the duties behind the labouring Bryan Mbeumo in the desperate hope he could spark his team into life.

Carrick has been left with an unbalanced squad, lacking quality in key areas. It would be hard to suggest on Sunday’s viewing that United were the Champions League team and Bournemouth in the Europa League. The Cherries can boast a wealth of smart recruitment, acquiring the likes of Adrien Truffert and Rayan – two players who would walk into the United team – for half a Harry Maguire.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The shambles of the third goal was on Lammens and Maguire, the former for running out too fast and the latter for not knowing how to run fast. Evanilson nipped in and flashed in the definitive game-ender. It sent Fernandes back to the bench with the expression of a man who had sipped sour milk. The final insult came when Carrick sent on the academy graduate Shea Lacey and left his captain to brood.

View image in fullscreen Manchester United fans have been venting their anger at the club’s hierarchy for some time. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

It is not solely one bottle; the whole dairy has curdled. Carrick can take some of the blame; the Glazers, Sir Jim Ratcliffe, Wilcox and Omar Berrada should receive more. United are not fit for purpose and the supporters’ ire was largely aimed at the directors’ box, demanding the owners sell up and go home, with slightly less savoury language. The Old Trafford faithful know where the fault lies, offering more creativity than any of their team with a fine repertoire of chants against the hierarchy, most pointedly at Wilcox, whose signings left Carrick in trouble before the season started.

Carrick had his name chanted, the full-time boos not for him. The manager – for now – did a lap of honour, cheered by the fans who jeered the players. Another era is nearing an end and finding reasons to be optimistic would be a greater waste of time than playing up front for United. Change will almost certainly come but it will not be enough.

Sports.title: Isak applies finishing touch as Liverpool bring Brighton’s winning run to an end
Sports.content:
Brighton’s impressive run was blown off course at Anfield where Liverpool performed with an appetite and urgency at both ends of the pitch that showed Andoni Iraola’s methods taking root. It was Liverpool, deserving winners on home soil for the first time in the Premier League this season, who looked upwardly mobile.

There was more evidence of the expensive trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola feeling at home and adapting to Iraola’s demands. Wirtz was instrumental in an opening goal officially credited to Brighton’s Pascal Gross and Isak scored for the sixth time in six Premier League appearances to shatter the visitors’ sequence of four successive league wins. The sight of Barcola sprinting back to help his defence and Ronald Araújo smashing into challenges, as Liverpool stubbornly defended their lead and their box in the second half, satisfied Iraola just as much as his side’s incisiveness before the break.

Fabian Hürzeler praised the Brighton performance and the self-belief necessary to take the game to Liverpool when trailing to two quickfire goals. But he exaggerated the threat they displayed. Yasin Ayari missed a glorious chance to open the scoring and also struck a post, but Alisson was troubled more by his own distribution after Liverpool’s second goal than by anything the visitors engineered.

“I think everyone in the stadium saw there was one team who really tried to create and tried to win this game and therefore I have to praise my players,” claimed the Brighton head coach, prompting a mass raising of eyebrows in the post-match press conference. “The difference was that they scored and we didn’t. They blocked a lot of shots and defended the box well. We didn’t have that efficiency. We couldn’t keep the clean sheet because we made easy mistakes and lost some important personal duels but overall I saw a team with a lot of good things. It is very frustrating because we all have the feeling that there is a missed opportunity here today.”

Storm Boelo raged outside the stadium but inside it was relatively calm, vindicating the decision to proceed with the game. But not for Brighton. Liverpool’s attacking force devastated the visitors’ hopes of a fifth straight win and clean sheet in succession in the Premier League. The hosts were aggressive and sharp from the start, in contrast to their opening against Villarreal in the Champions League, and opened the scoring just as Brighton were beginning to exert their first serious spell of pressure.

There was an element of good fortune about the breakthrough but it also encapsulated the differing intensity between the teams when Wirtz held off Lewis Dunk and Araújo beat the Brighton captain and Olivier Boscagli to the loose ball. His low cross rebounded off two Brighton players before going to Wirtz, whose first-time shot deceived Bart Verbruggen via another deflection off Gross. Wirtz’s low-key celebration hinted at what was to come. It was not his first league goal of the campaign and second goal in successive games after all. The breakthrough was officially credited as an own goal from the Brighton midfielder.

View image in fullscreen Florian Wirtz’s shot was credited as an own goal by his fellow German, Pascal Gross. Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPA

It should also have been a Liverpool equaliser rather than the opener. Diego Gómez and Gross combined to pierce Liverpool’s left flank and present Ayari with a free sight of goal with Alisson dragged across to his left. The Brighton forward blazed high into the Kop and would soon have added reason to rue the miscue.

Liverpool soon doubled their lead when capitalising on more casual Brighton defending. Boscagli was again found wanting when attempting to deal with Alisson’s clearance. The left-back struck a clearance straight at Barcola and was left floundering as the France international, deployed on the right, brushed aside his efforts to recover possession. Isak steered Barcola’s delivery inside the far corner with a deft, side-foot finish to score in three consecutive league games for the first time since January 2025. There was no surprise whatsoever when Boscagli was withdrawn at half-time.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Brighton attacked with greater conviction than they defended but with Araújo, Jérémy Jacquet and Virgil van Dijk making telling interventions, and receiving impressive support from all quarters, Alisson was not seriously extended. The visitors’ best hope of a recovery stemmed from the Liverpool keeper’s own risky pass to Alexis Mac Allister, which gifted possession back to Brighton and resulted in Ayari striking a post from 20 yards out.

Jack Hinshelwood, Boscagli’s replacement, and fellow substitute Malick Yalcouyé injected more energy and bite into Brighton’s second-half display but an end product from the visitors remained lacking. Too many overhit crosses and poor final balls enabled Liverpool to protect their lead in comfort.

Iraola said: “It is a very valuable win. The key was how we started. We needed a strong start, to be aggressive, recover balls, win our duels, be dangerous in transitions, and we’ve done it and it has been a different game from the last ones when we’ve conceded first.”

Sports.title: Terland strikes late as United end Manchester City’s winning start in WSL
Sports.content:
At long last, a weakness has been spotted. Finally, the 100% winning start ends for Manchester City, much to the pleasure of Manchester United, who struck late through Elisabeth Terland to claim a point in a well-contested and at times breathless derby.

Khadija “Bunny” Shaw’s second-half strike – her 91st WSL goal on her 100th appearance in the division – appeared to have settled the game and kept the defending champions top of the table, and it had looked likely to be the same old story, of City finding a way to win a game that was on a knife-edge, because they have the game’s deadliest finisher.

However, Eva Olid’s ever-improving hosts fought back and were good value for the draw, which they eventually earned when Terland found the bottom corner after the ball fell kindly to her in the penalty area.

Olid, in fact, repeatedly said in her post-match press conference that her side had “deserved to win”.

United climbed to fourth in the table, while that late strike meant City dropped to ­second – now behind Chelsea on goal difference – and breathed fresh life and intrigue into the title race. Perhaps more strikingly, if any United fans who saw their men’s team being humbled by Bournemouth earlier on Sunday managed to navigate the winds of Storm Boelo and get to Leigh for this 6pm kick-off, they will have seen a team with characteristics unrecognisable from those wearing red at Old Trafford; hard work, resilience, teamwork, running – real, hard running – and fighting spirit.

This United team markedly improved on last season’s league meetings with their local rivals, both of which ended in 3-0 victories for City. This time Andrée Jeglertz’s visitors were given a real test.

Quick Guide WSL roundup: Show Chelsea came from behind to beat Crystal Palace 3-1 after Molly Bartrip’s shock opener. It was the first time Chelsea had trailed all season and they struck back in the second half with two Melvine Malard goals, before Sandy Baltimore converted from the penalty spot in the 90th minute. London City Lionesses stayed third after drawing 2-2 at Liverpool, with the visitors denied all three points by a stoppage-time own goal from Jana Fernández. Freya Godfrey and Kadidiatou Diani had earlier wiped out Beata Olsson’s penalty. Aston Villa moved level on points with Everton after winning 3-2 at Goodison Park. Amalie Vangsgaard’s double put Villa three up after Noelle Maritz’s early goal, before the hosts made it a nervy finish with two late goals. Birmingham won for the first time this season as Wilma Leidhammar’s effort midway through the second half saw off Charlton 1-0. Press Association Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

For spells of the first half, City’s fluid pass-and-move football, their speed down the left-wing with ­Lauren Hemp, and the technical prowess of Yui Hasegawa and Aoba Fujino in particular, made it feel as though there was only one likely outcome, as Fujino fizzed an effort narrowly wide of the United goal.

United, though, proved a tough nut to crack and, against the run of play, created the better chances of the opening 45 minutes.

Terland was unable to reset her feet and ­connect properly with Andrea Medina’s ­cutback. Later Ella Toone and Jess Park both had efforts saved by Ayaka Yamashita.

View image in fullscreen Khadija Shaw blasts Manchester City into the lead against United. Photograph: Craig Brough/Action Images/Reuters

Park’s powerful, driven shot clipped the top of the crossbar around the hour mark, after Yamashita had saved well from Terland one-on-one.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Not long later, though, last season’s WSL Golden Boot winner Shaw ­delivered the breakthrough with a ruthless, low strike that was hit with too much venom for Phallon ­Tullis-Joyce to react. Shaw, who had been booed by the home fans after exchanging robust challenges with Maya Le Tissier in the first half, ran across to celebrate in front of the City fans, many of whom were waving inflatable bananas in the air. She almost had a second goal moments later but whipped a close-range, rising shot just over the bar.

Shaw glanced a header wide from a City corner and Grace Clinton missed a huge chance to seal it for the ­visitors. Continuing to battle, United were eventually rewarded when Le Tissier’s hopeful, high ball into the box, after a free-kick was taken short, was met by a defensive header from Shaw, but that only dropped as far as Terland who lashed in first time to draw huge roars and clenched fists from the United technical area.

Jeglertz is staying calm, insisting: “Nothing has changed. We are absolutely on the right track, in everything we are doing. We are playing well in most of the games and getting the result in most of the games. But this league is challenging. [We are just going] to stay calm and focusing on the next task.”

As for United, this late goal felt like a pivotal moment for Olid, giving the club a lift. Her tenure began with chastening losses to London City and Chelsea but this rally against their neighbours showed they are rapidly improving. She said: “That was one of our best performances, in general, in terms of fight, hard work, how we were ­pressing and how we played with the ball.

“How this team has built in confidence from day one to now, in a short period of time – just two months and a half working together – the progression has been massive.”

Sports.title: Pierre Sage regrets ‘missed 15 minutes’ as defeat increases heat on Crystal Palace manager
Sports.content:
Pierre Sage blamed a 15-minute loss of concentration for Crystal Palace’s 2-0 defeat by Newcastle and insisted he remains the right man to lead the south London club. “We missed 15 minutes when we came back from the dressing room,” the Frenchman said. “When you let your opponent take the initiative without pressure, without reply, it’s difficult.”

Palace have conceded 19 goals in eight games and have the worst defensive record in the Premier League, an obvious contrast to last season when Sage’s Lens side had the second-best defensive record in Ligue 1. “When we concede all these goals … you can interpret that through the style of play and also how well we are playing, especially defensively,” Sage said.

“My way, my idea, is that the best way to defend is to have the ball.” The problem with that is that only the three promoted sides have had less possession than Palace. “Here every mistake, every situation that is bad for the team will be a goal,” Sage said.

Palace conceded two goals against Besiktas on Thursday to the only shots on target they conceded. Newcastle similarly scored with both their shots on target. “We conceded fewer chances with our defending in open play today but it’s not enough,” the Palace manager said. “For the moment the pressure is always the same because I don’t find the solution. Today was not a tactical problem but a mental problem. When we came back from the dressing room we let our opponents have too many things. When you don’t control the ball you give the initiative to the opposition.”

Sage is sure he can improve ­Palace’s fortunes – they are 17th having lost back-to-back Premier League games, the other being a 5-0 thrashing by their rivals Brighton – and said that although he remains in regular contact with the Palace chair, Steve Parish, the issue of his future has never been raised. “Inside, we are just really focused on solutions,” Sage said. “How to be better, how to create the conditions to compete, and we will continue our work. There’s no noise inside, if you want.”

There was relief for Matthias Jaissle as he oversaw a first ­Newcastle win in three games. “It was a tough game especially in first half,” the ­German said. “We couldn’t get ourselves the reward for the intensity of our possession.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“The first half out of possession was not that bad but we didn’t have our attacking mindset. The second half was much better. Even if you don’t play a fantastic game in possession, keeping a clean sheet is the fundamental of football.”

Sports.title: Ouattara rescues point for Brentford as Hull maintain unbeaten home record
Sports.content:
Hull’s unbeaten home record remains intact but the Tigers have not tasted victory for seven games after this draw with Brentford.

The opening goal came courtesy of a 24th-minute Oli McBurnie penalty, awarded when Aaron Hickey flattened Tim Iroegbunam while trying to hook the ball away.

Although Brentford’s Caoimhín Kelleher guessed right, he could not stop McBurnie scoring his first Premier League goal for more than 900 days.

After the break, Hull were left to rue some inattentive defending as Igor Thiago found his way to Dango Ouattara, who slotted the ball home under very little pressure to make it 1-1 in the 63rd minute.

Jaidon Anthony pushed for a second Brentford goal and saw a shot land just wide before getting a second chance, which forced a save from Konstantinos Tzolakis, but there was a quick counter as Mohamed Belloumi raced in the other direction before firing over from distance.

An 88th-minute chance was Hull’s last opportunity to find the winning goal, but Mohamed-Ali Cho’s cross to Joe Gelhardt resulted in an off‑target shot that ensured the Tigers took no more than a point.

Hull’s manager, Sergej Jakirovic, was pleased with the improved efforts of his side after the defeat by Fulham the previous weekend. “I think we played a good game, especially in the first half,” he said. “We were much more aggressive in duels, we won a lot of first and second balls. Maybe there were some cheap mistakes, bad passing, bad receiving, but you see how fast they are – in five seconds they were in our box. We should have scored one or maybe two more with better decisions.”

Both clubs were required to pick through the detritus of the pre-match display in the opening minutes as balloons and litter were carried by the strong winds of Storm Boelo on to the pitch.

The first chance of note fell to the visitors, with Hull faltering in midfield after 11 minutes and allowing Hickey to unleash a shot that was comfortably dealt with by Tzolakis.

View image in fullscreen Oli McBurnie (left) hugs Mohamed Belloumi after putting Hull ahead from the penalty spot. Photograph: Mike Egerton/PA

Ten minutes later Belloumi found McBurnie inside the box, but as the Scot was preparing to strike Mathias Jensen rushed in to foil the attempt.

After 22 minutes the visitors offered their hosts a golden chance when Hickey, having failed to collect a ball from Kelleher, lunged at the legs of Iroegbunam and floored him to give away a penalty. McBurnie stepped up and made no mistake.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Brentford had to wait until the 63rd minute to equalise, Ouattara made the most of lax Hull defending to collect an Igor Thiago ball and tap home.

Belloumi then reacted with a sprint towards the Brentford goal with Cho – on as a substitute – in pursuit as backup, but the long-range shot was too high and flew into the stand.

The final roll of the dice was Cho’s cross in to Gelhardt, but he was wide of the mark and the whistle blew on a 1-1 draw that maintains unbeaten records home and away. Jakirovic said: “I can regret the chance we had through Mohamed-Ali Cho and Gelhardt, maybe it should have been 2-1, but in the end I think it’s a fair result.”

Brentford’s head coach, Keith Andrews, who had a spell at Hull as a player, was happy to see the response from the players who were brought off the bench during the second half in the leadup to their equaliser. “It was a tough game and it was always going to be a tough game, “ he said.

“I’ve got a lot of respect for Sergej and the journey he’s taken this team on – I think it’s been remarkable. We reacted well at half-time, the impact from the bench was pretty good but it was a tough game.”

Sports.title: Roefs and Trafford stand firm as Sunderland and Leeds battle for point
Sports.content:
Régis Le Bris can usually do impassive to perfection but, by the final whistle, even Sunderland’s ultra-balanced manager was looking more than a little fed up and frustrated.

His bottom-placed team had arguably just about deserved a second Premier League win of the season but, instead, had to settle for a draw on an afternoon when the hugely disruptive Storm Boelo proved the enemy of good football.

While Daniel Farke will doubtless regard his resilient side’s fifth league draw of the season as a fair return on the windblown road, much now hinges on Sunderland’s visit to Coventry on Saturday.

At least Le Bris’s side ended a run of four straight league defeats on a day when they could have done without meeting James Trafford’s goalkeeping excellence. “It’s so hard to win games,” said Sunderland’s manager. “But it’s a positive point; we played with intensity and togetherness. We were Sunderland today.

“It’s still a long journey but I think we’ve shown we’re embracing the challenge. We probably deserved more today. But there’s no drama, no panic.”

The wind was strong, and capricious enough, to bend the corner flags out of shape, send pieces of rubbish swirling around the pitch and turn passing calibration horribly awry but it would take a hurricane to throw Brian Brobbey off balance.

The good news for Sunderland was that their formidable centre-forward had recovered from a hamstring injury and seemed to be relishing the physicality of his duel with Jaka Bijol.

Along the way Brobbey had a ­couple of first-half chances. First came the connection with an Enzo Le Fée cross and the slightly deflected shot that prompted a decent save from Trafford.

Then there was the moment when Brobbey bullied Bijol into attempting a short back-pass before charging after it and ­getting there before Trafford. Hats off to Farke’s England goalkeeper for keeping his cool, bravely ­standing his ground and eventually saving cleverly with a leg.

Leeds possess a not-too shabby centre-forward of their own in ­Dominic Calvert-Lewin. He passed a late fitness test on a bruised foot and, although initially less involved than Brobbey, seemed on a mission to engage Luke O’Nien in a personal subplot.

View image in fullscreen James Trafford denies Brian Brobbey from close range. Photograph: Owen Humphreys/PA

It soon became clear that Calvert-Lewin had little enthusiasm for being marked by O’Nien’s central defensive partner, Nordi Mukiele, and duly manoeuvred himself into cameos against the former at every ­opportunity. Yet although O’Nien endured a couple of wobbles he also made a vital, quite possibly goal-preventing tackle on Calvert-Lewin as half-time beckoned.

The second half had barely begun before fortune frowned on Sunderland. An attempted clearance ­concluded with O’Nien throwing out an elbow and accidentally catching Mukiele in the throat. T he former Paris Saint-Germain defender requiring lengthy treatment as Le Bris looked on anxiously.

Eventually it became apparent a distressed Mukiele – who, Le Bris reported, fully recovered – could not continue and the recently erratic Omar Alderete stepped off the bench.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

By now, a generally ­second-best Leeds were renascent and it took important interceptions from Alderete and Le Fée to break the ­dangerous stride of Jayden Bogle and Ao Tanaka respectively. Undeterred, Sunderland rallied. Nilson Angulo was in encouraging form and two shots from the Ecuadorian forced Trafford into a couple of smart saves.

Shortly after the hour mark the fading Brobbey was replaced by the inexperienced Ukrainian striker Timur Tutyerov as, simultaneously, Farke introduced fresh attacking legs of his own.

They belonged to Noah Okafor and Anton Stach who filled the spaces behind Calvert-Lewin from where Harry Wilson and Brenden Aaronson had struggled to ­destabilise Sunderland’s backline.

The game remained in the balance. Trafford did well to somehow scramble the ball to safety as Granit Xhaka’s corner very nearly curved beyond him but Robin Roefs was required to dive at Calvert-Lewin’s feet after spilling Tanaka’s shot. Calvert-Lewin wanted a penalty but Stuart Attwell disagreed and a video assistant referee check endorsed that viewpoint.

When the former Newcastle midfeilder Sean Longstaff, on as a Leeds substitute, unleashed a dangerous low, 20-yard shot, Stadium of Light regulars feared the worst but Roefs proved equal to it, making a superb one-handed save to turn the ball around a post.

There was still time for Longstaff to have another shot cleared off the line but Farke remained sanguine. “I’m not complaining about the draw,” said the Leeds manager. “It’s always good to have a clean sheet. It’s fair to say that, in weather like this, it wasn’t the nicest game.”

Inevitably, Farke was invited to praise Trafford and his concession of a mere six league goals in eight games. “He chose a good team,” he said smiling before turning serious. “He delivers, he has the potential to be England’s No 1.”

Sports.title: Scottish Premiership: Durán caps Celtic’s comeback win over Hibernian
Sports.content:
Camilo Durán moved into double figures for the season as Celtic reasserted themselves at the top of the Premiership by coming from behind to defeat beleaguered Hibernian 2-1 at windy Easter Road.

After another Europa League setback at home to Celta Vigo on Thursday, the champions bounced back with a victory that restored their four-point cushion over Rangers at the top. The home side, who are bottom, took an early lead through Owen Elding but it was swiftly cancelled out by a Jason Kerr own goal before Duran’s 10th of the season edged the visitors ahead just before the break.

It proved enough to secure a ninth win in 10 league games and ensure the recently appointed home boss, Marink Reedijk, suffered a third straight defeat since succeeding David Gray.

There were a couple of blemishes for Celtic, however, as substitute Alistair Johnston’s return from injury lasted barely 20 minutes before he had to go off, while £11million forward Kasper Hogh – restored to the starting line-up after notching in just one of his 13 previous matches for the Hoops – again drew a blank before being replaced in the 64th minute.

Derek McInnes asked his Rangers side to be “brilliant” against St Johnstone and was rewarded with a 4-0 win at Ibrox on Saturday. After dropping two points at Dundee, the Light Blues dominated the first half but only led at the interval through a goal in the 29th minute from the Venezuela forward Kevin Kelsy.

Saints started the second half brightly but goals from the Gers striker Ryan Naderi in the 61st minute and Kelsy again five minutes later had the home side cruising. The Saints substitute Kai Fotheringham was shown a straight red card by Chris Graham in the 74th minute for his high challenge on the midfielder Nico Raskin, before the substitute Tochi Chukwuani added a fourth for the hosts with three minutes remaining.

View image in fullscreen Rangers’ Kevin Kelsy scores the third goal against St Johnstone. Photograph: Steve Welsh/PA

McInnes said: “It’s quite ironic in the sense that we were so good and so brilliant at times in the first half and create so many opportunities, that we were only a goal to the good at half-time. And obviously, we don’t want to let the frustration of those missed opportunities and dominance filter into the second half.

“I think half-time came at a bad time for us because, despite the conditions, some of the play was really good. I asked the players to be brilliant today, not just win the game, can we really commit to being the best we can be, as good as we can be? And I thought we were in the first half. Everything was brilliant except the result at half-time because we should have been more in in front.”

Cláudio Braga and Calvin Miller scored to help Hearts secure a 2-0 win over Motherwell at Fir Park on Sunday. A return to winning ways after last weekend’s humbling 7-1 defeat by Celtic leaves Hearts four points behind second-placed Rangers and eight off the leaders. Motherwell sit 10th after this sixth straight defeat, equalling a record from 2003. They were booed off the pitch at the interval and at full time.

Dundee United won a rollercoaster game 3-2 against Aberdeen at Tannadice on Saturday. Zidane Iqbal scored for the hosts before the visitors equalised through Nesta Guinness-Walker – both players scoring their first goals for their clubs.

United took the lead once more thanks to a Dylan Tait strike, with Connor Ronan drawing Aberdeen level after the break. Zac Sapsford secured all three points for his side, with the win moving United up to fourth – one point behind Hearts, who are at Motherwell on Sunday – while Aberdeen dropped to ninth.

Two own goals helped Falkirk climb to seventh with a 3-0 victory over Kilmarnock. Centre-backs Cathal McCarthy and George Stanger scored past their own goalkeeper either side of a Jacob Murrell header. St Mirren ended their losing streak with a 2-1 victory over Dundee with goals from Calvin Ramsay and Eseosa Sule before Bradley Fink pulled one back for the visitors.

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes aims ANOTHER swipe at Michael Carrick: Captain likes cryptic 'loyalty' social media post less than 24 hours after Man United boss dumped star to the bench
Sports.content:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has seemingly aimed another dig at Michael Carrick after being dropped against Bournemouth. The Portuguese liked a cryptic Instagram post about 'loyalty' and 'no longer caring' on Sunday following the club's disastrous 3-0 thrashing at Old Trafford. Fernandes was axed for the clash after criticising his beleaguered manager's tactics in the aftermath of their 4-1 hammering at Como in the Champions League in midweek. 'Never push a loyal person to the point where they no longer care,' read the post, which the talisman liked. It is not clear why he did so, and his like appears to have been removed. The clip was from an animation film called A Tale of Momentum and Inertia, and shows a huge creature formed from rocks trying to stop a boulder from rolling onto a town. Carrick could be sacked after a dismal run of two wins in 12 games since being appointed on a two-year deal in the summer, with United 16th in the Premier League. The Manchester United hierarchy are in crisis talks over his future after the humbling defeat by Bournemouth, though supporters sang Carrick's name throughout the match. Bruno Fernandes has seemingly aimed another dig at Michael Carrick after Manchester United's 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth The captain liked an Instagram post which read: 'Never push a loyal person to the point where they no longer care' His decision to leave Fernandes simmering on the bench seemed to backfire, as United were thoroughly beaten by their opponents but the 32-year-old has failed to capture his best form this campaign. Gary Neville has sided with his old team-mate Carrick, accusing Fernandes of being an 'excuse merchant'. 'Eric Cantona was very unorthodox as a captain. Roy Keane could sometimes be explosive in his interviews after matches, but they weren't whingers about the tactics, about pressing, or excuse merchants,' he said on his Sky Sports podcast. 'Bruno can't press. To come out and whinge after the game about the manager's tactics, when you've just lost 4-1, and a few thousand fans have paid thousands of pounds to travel over in that far corner and get wet through. I'm sorry, read the room, Bruno. 'This is not a time for whingeing, throwing your arms up in the air. This is a time for you to stand up and say, that's not good enough. Be positive. Do something with a positive influence as a captain. But he's not. 'He's gone and basically thrown his manager under the bus the week after [Lisandro] Martinez did the same.' Neville added: 'They weren't singing for Bruno Fernandes to come on today. They're backing Michael Carrick. 'So get in your box. You know where you stand. Michael Carrick's won things for the football club on a constant basis, and proven that he can have the humility, the resilience. And Bruno has got that. Bruno has delivered for Manchester United in more ways than any other player in the last 13 years. Carrick dropped Fernandes to the bench after his recent outburst - but the decision backfired Gary Neville believes Carrick will be 'disgusted' by his Manchester United players 'He's massively talented but he let himself down this week. He didn't need to do that because he's basically stuck the knife into his manager.' Carrick did a lap of Old Trafford at full time, clapping the fans, but insisted he was not saying goodbye in doing so. 'It wasn't a farewell from me,’ Carrick insisted. ‘I probably didn't really expect that off the supporters, if I'm honest, but I've always felt the support and that connection with them. ‘It will take a bit of time to digest, but I certainly appreciate their support. It's difficult for me to have a day like this at this club and feel the emotion. ‘I’m carrying on as normal. I love this place. I'll always do what I feel is going to be the best for the football club and I won’t change that now, whatever decision is made. ‘It's a tough situation, there's no hiding from it. What it looks like and what's next I really don't know. I love what I do and I feel the responsibility. We'll have to wait and see. ‘Of course, I take responsibility. I respect the position that I'm in, and the responsibility is mine. What else can I say really right now? ‘I've been at the club a long time. It hurts an awful lot to see us going through this at this moment in time. The situation is where we are and we haven't had results or performances that have been good enough. United were beaten 3-0 at home by Bournemouth and the manager is hanging on by a thread ‘I'm feeling it for my players, they're going through a tough spell. There's a lot of emotion in the changing room right now, there's a lot of the boys quite hurt, to be fair. ‘It's not like they don't care or they want to be in this position. The ones I've spoken to, it’s affecting them a lot.’ There are questions about how much support Carrick has in the dressing room after Fernandes' outburst last week. Fernandes, who is usually very deliberate in what he says in the media, was scathing in his criticism of coaches after the Como debacle. 'It's a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little space in behind and try to get the ball in the first moment, to wait for them, to give them the ball,' he said. 'But sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confident, they have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot, make people get frustrated, and then obviously when you recover the ball the legs are, and the brain, much more difficult to make it work.' But Harry Maguire came out in support of his gaffer after the Bournemouth loss, saying: 'At the moment we're not doing enough as players. Michael turned our season on its head last year and we played brilliant football and got brilliant results. This season we haven't performed well enough as individuals. 'We have got to find something, question yourself, look in the mirror, that's the most important thing - think what you can do more and contribute to the team and if we do that we'll get somewhere.' Former United defender Ashley Young, who won the 2012-13 Premier League title with the club, accused the players of 'giving up'. 'There have been different managers [in recent seasons] but it's the same players,' he said on Sky Sports. 'There have been a few changes in players but they're just not showing anything. You could tell today that it was like they'd given up - they're not running for this manager and they're not wanting to fight. 'The fans deserve so much more, you can tell they want more and they know he's been let down by those players.'

Sports.title: Lucky football punter, 45, wins nearly £1MILLION from a £4 corners accumulator
Sports.content:
There is a good day at the races and then there's this. A Portsmouth-based punter hit the acca of his life over the weekend, winning close to £1million from a £4 stake.

The Aston Villa fan, 45, put his spare change on 12 EFL matches all having over 11.5 corners, a bet that had odds of 249,346/1 on Betfair when placed.

Incredibly the bet landed – and the £997,385 winner is planning to treat his family and betting pals with his newfound wealth.

‘It was emotional, I felt little bit sick at first making sure it was real, and then obviously the reality kicked in,’ he said.

‘My wife was out at the time when I checked, I needed her to come back to clarify the amount that was in there, I kept asking her “this is right isn't it?” It didn't seem real, it's hard to put into words.

‘I didn't sleep much last night, thinking about what we can do with the money. It's a really good feeling, it's brilliant!’

A Portsmouth punter has become a millionaire after his 12 game acca paid out (pictured: Jimmy Dunne scoring from a corner for QPR against Swansea on Saturday)

At half-time on Saturday afternoon the bet looked to be a foolish investment with just one corner between Reading and Barnsley and four between Cambridge and Plymouth.

In the second half, however, the tides shifted and the set-pieces arrived in serious numbers, with Oxford v Bradford having 14 corners between them despite the game finishing goalless.

‘Me and my friends usually do an accumulator on the weekend for a bit of fun, we all pick a leg and put them in our group chat, both teams to score usually, and I like to do corners,’ he explained.

'I had £4 in my account, so I decided to do one of my own with a few more corners in. I'm sure that I'll be treating my mates after winning this one. It will be my round all the time!'

The punter didn't even find out his acca had made him a millionaire until the evening, saying that: 'I didn't actually realise it had come in until about half an hour after all the games had finished.

'I'm an Aston Villa fan and was out with my son watching the early kick-off, which started the day really well! Then we walked back home and got soaked with the weather, and when I checked my account I couldn't believe it.'

The jubilant football fan has humble plans for his £1million prize, hoping to pay off his mortgage, buy a car and book a week in the sun with the family, as well as going to watch more games at Villa Park with his son.

Betfair spokesman Sam Rosbottom said: 'We are absolutely delighted for this Portsmouth punter and couldn't be happier to pay out such a large sum of money.'

Sports.title: Lewis Hamilton says he 'loves' spending time with Kim Kardashian's kids as he gives rare insight into their romance
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton has offered a rare glimpse into his relationship with Kim Kardashian and admitted he 'loves' spending time with her four children.

The pair have been romantically linked since February, and have since gone Instagram official.

But the Formula One legend spoke about his relationship with the reality TV star in a rare moment at this week's US Grand Prix in Austin.

During a panel event at Circuit of the Americas, the Ferrari driver said: 'My niece and nephew always gave me a lot of happiness.

'My girlfriend's kids, I love spending time with them,' he added, referring to North, 13, Saint, 10, Chicago, 8, and Psalm, 7.

'She's got four, so I'm getting to play with these kids. I got them a dog this year, so little Halo is a new member of that family.'

Lewis Hamilton has revealed he 'loves' spending time with Kim Kardashian's four children

Hamilton offered a rare glimpse into their romance during an event in Austin this weekend

Kardashian exuded glamour as she strutted out of the Bulgari Hotel in Rome on Friday night

Kardashian, who shares her four children with ex-husband Kanye West, has been to support Hamilton at some races this season but skipped Sunday's race in Austin because she's in Rome celebrating her 46th birthday with mom Kris Jenner.

It comes just days after Kardashian admitted she is 'really, really happy' with how their romance is going during an episode over her reality show.

Kim made the coy admission on The Kardashians and revealed the iconic driver meets every requirement on her famously demanding relationship checklist.

The star discussed a list of more than 50 qualities she wanted in her ideal partner, before suggesting she had finally found someone who fulfilled them all, while speaking to comedian Nikki Glaser, 42, on the set of their film The Fifth Wheel.

When producers pressed her to reveal more about the mystery man, Kim said: 'Oh, you guys are really trying to get this out of me.'

She added: 'Let me just say this – I am just really, really happy. That's all I'll say for now.'

Since going public with their romance, Kim has been seen supporting Lewis at his Formula One races across the globe.

The couple also took a trip to Japan earlier this year, and they are said to have spent a weekend at luxury hotel Estelle Manor in the Cotswolds, and visited Paris – the 'city of love' – in February too.

In the same month, they appeared publicly together at the Super Bowl, when they were shown on the stadium's big screen during the game between the New England Patriots and the Seattle Seahawks.

Lewis – who has previously been linked romantically with singer Nicole Scherzinger, 48, and actress Sofía Vergara, 54 – and Kim had known each other for several years prior to their relationship.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick is not the man for Man United but he has been let down by money-hungry Glazers, sulking prima donna Bruno Fernandes and Sir Jim Ratcliffe's woeful mismanagement, writes CHRIS WHEELER - they still need 'open heart surgery'
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick is not the man for Man United but he has been let down by money-hungry Glazers, sulking prima donna Bruno Fernandes and Sir Jim Ratcliffe's woeful mismanagement, writes CHRIS WHEELER - they still need 'open heart surgery'

Once the third goal went in and defeat was inevitable, the Stretford End launched into their tribute song to Michael Carrick and then turned on the people they blame for bringing humiliation on their football club.

On the Glazer family. On Sir Jim Ratcliffe. On director of football Jason Wilcox. And, finally, on the players themselves.

There is no doubt in their minds where the responsibility lies. No doubt at all that Carrick has been hung out to dry from the boardroom to the dressing-room.

But they know that one man in particular always pays the price in moments like these, and Manchester United will shortly be looking to make a third managerial appointment this year.

Carrick insisted that his lap of the pitch after the final whistle, applauding supporters and patting his heart to the Stretford End as he disappeared down the tunnel wasn't farewell, but it certainly felt like one.

The moment he was out of view, the cheers turned to boos as the players followed behind him.

Michael Carrick is pictured leading his team off the pitch after their 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth

So how has it come to this? How has a team that suffered just two defeats in 17 games after Carrick replaced Ruben Amorim in January lost half of their 12 matches this season and left their head coach facing the axe?

Some will say it was inevitable. That a man whose only other managerial job had ended in the sack at Championship club Middlesbrough seven months earlier should never have been in charge of Manchester United in the first place, no matter how good a player he was here or how steeped he was in the Old Trafford traditions.

They made the parallels with Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, uncanny as they are, and will look at United's horrific slump this season as vindication of those views.

United's decision to only give him a two-year contract suggested that their faith, too, was hardly unshakeable.

Certainly, Carrick needs to take his share of the blame, and he wasn't trying to duck it after the 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth left United in 16th place. He is a good man.

But he is not an inspirational leader and at times the passion and intensity missing in the team have felt like a reflection of their head coach – even more so in recent weeks when he has stood on the touchline next to adversaries such as Diego Simeone, Roberto De Zerbi and Cesc Fabregas.

On Sunday, he was frozen in a familiar pose as the misery continued, only unfolding his arms when it was time to stroke his chin.

'I don't think now sitting here is the perfect time to go through everything,' said Carrick afterwards. 'To finish third last season was a really good achievement in the circumstances to get to where we did and the amount of results that we did.

Carrick is not an inspirational leader but he has been badly let down by his players

'We definitely knew we hadn't cracked it and there was a lot of work to be done, but that doesn't mean to say it should have gone this way.

'We understood where that left us and what was next; what needed to be done, how we needed to improve, and kind of where we were at as a team and as a group at that stage.'

And that is where the real problem lies. Whether he was the right man for the job, Carrick knew what was needed to take United to the next level and his employers knew it.

But the money wasn't there to make improvements this squad needs because the Glazers continue to drain money out of United, and the mismanagement under Ratcliffe has fallen woefully short of Ineos' best in class mantra.

'Sell United and f*** off home,' chanted the United fans on Sunday.

United failed Carrick in the transfer market last summer by only spending £150million, just as Lisandro Martinez said they did in Madrid earlier this month. It wasn't by chance that the fans directed their fury at Wilcox here.

Yes, United's midfield needed work, but they also needed a striker and a left-back to provide cover for Benjamin Sesko and Luke Shaw. When both players quickly succumbed to injury at the start of the season, it felt like an act of gross negligence.

Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Ineos' mismanagement has contributed to the current demise

Of the midfielders brought in, Carlos Baleba wasn't able to play until October and Youri Tielemans has been so poor that he was hooked at half-time against Bournemouth. Andrey Santos is a poor imitation of Casemiro.

It has left United's squad still in need of the 'open heart surgery' interim boss Ralf Rangnick identified five years ago, a lack of quality that has undermined a succession of managers since then.

Bournemouth have now won 3-0 on three of the last four visits to Old Trafford (the other result was 4-4). Those three defeats came under three different managers – Carrick, Amorim and Erik ten Hag – which indicates that what happened here is not an aberration and it will happen again unless there is fundamental change at United beyond sacking the manager.

Which brings us to the players. They too have let down Carrick having done enough for him in the second half of last season to pick up their bonuses for qualifying for the Champions League.

Bruno Fernandes is a sulking prima donna and was not brought on by Carrick

Bruno Fernandes, in particular, has gone from PFA Player of the Year to a sulking prima donna in the space of a few months, culminating in his personal criticism of Carrick after the disastrous defeat in Como on Wednesday night.

Carrick responded by dropping his captain to the bench on Sunday and then left him stewing there as a he sent on four substitutes including teenager Shea Lacey.

It was a show of strength from Carrick, but one that may have come too late. Rather like Jose Mourinho leaving Paul Pogba on the bench during his last stand at Anfield in December 2018, it will make no difference to what happens next.

United are set to sack Carrick and then the same people at the top will bring in someone else to manage the same group of players, and the whole sorry cycle will start again.

Sports.title: Ex-Premier League player Jermaine Pennant is left needing 50 stitches after being mauled by dog while walking his own pet
Sports.content:
Ex-Premier League star Jermaine Pennant was left needing 50 stitches on a leg wound after he was viciously mauled by a dog.

The former Liverpool midfielder, 43, had been walking his own dog - an American Akita named King - when he was pounced on by a German Shepherd.

Pennant said it came after he 'stepped in to protect' King when the other dog 'had a go at him', only for the footballer to eventually be attacked himself.

He told The Sun: 'It was really scary. The other dog had a go at King, so I stepped in to protect him.

'The next thing I know, it was attacking me. I was on the floor and it was on my leg for at least five seconds.

'I felt this huge pressure. Imagine the force of a dog bite. King jumped in to protect me.'

Gory images showed the extent of Pennant's injuries, with his right shin left bloodied and scarred in the aftermath of the incident.

The former Stoke City star was treated for four bite wounds on his leg and told he may need surgery for one larger one.

Jermaine Pennant, 43, shared a picture from a hospital bed after having more than 50 stitches

The ex-Liverpool midfielder was attacked by a German Shepherd while walking his American Akita, named King

Pictures shared by the TalkSport host showed large wounds on his left shin

Pennant later thanked his dog for 'saving his life' in a heartfelt Instagram post

But Pennant ultimately had more than 50 stitches inserted at the hospital, before crediting King for standing up to the German Shepherd and 'saving his life'.

In an emotional Instagram caption accompanying a picture of him embracing his dog, Pennant wrote: 'So I was attacked by a German Shepherd, I tried to protect king but the dog got my leg, I was on the floor with the dog still attached with no sign of letting go, until king intervened as he didn’t know what was going on.

'But the minute he did he fought the dog off and saved what could’ve been an horrendous situation for me.

'King was unhurt with a little nip on his leg, but had blood covered all over him which wasn’t mine, at this point I forgot the agony I was in, and my heart sank, but it wasn’t kings.

'My hero still protecting me and trying to look after me, KING you’re a legend love you, man’s best friend, thanks for taking care of us both.'

Pennant said he has no intention of reporting the matter to the police.

There were some 29,400 cases of out-of-control dog attacks last year, marking a rise of 83 per cent on the 16,040 recorded in 2020.

Pennant retired from football at the age of 35 in 2018 following a 17-year career.

The 43-year-old made 231 Premier League appearances during stints with Stoke, Liverpool, Birmingham City, Leeds United, Portsmouth and Arsenal.

Sports.title: Man United's players 'aren't professional, don't go to bed at the right time, don't eat the right things and have CONNED Michael Carrick' - he will look at them 'in disgust', rages Gary Neville
Sports.content:
Gary Neville has accused Man United's players of 'conning' Michael Carrick and branded them 'unprofessional' in an eviscerating attack. Sunday's abject 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth at Old Trafford followed the dire 4-1 embarrassment in Como and looks likely to spell the end of the manager's tenure. Carrick, 45, received a warm reaction from the Stretford End despite the latest miserable loss and the home faithful then turned on the squad, booing them off the pitch. Neville appears to agree with the sentiment shown by fans, saying he has 'no time for the players', some of whom he claims 'don't eat the right things' or 'go to bed at the right time'. 'They've teased him, haven't they? They've conned him for a few months. They have they've conned him,' Neville said on his Sky Sports podcast. 'Honestly, he would never say this publicly because he's got class. I can say it for him though. He'll look at those players with disgust. Some of them, he'll be disgusted with some of those players. Gary Neville believes Michael Carrick will be 'disgusted' by his Manchester United players 'A few of them aren't that professional. I live in Manchester. Some of them aren't that professional. So I've got no time for them. 'There's a few of them that don't go to bed at the right time, don't eat the right things, don't think about Manchester United every single minute of every day, and aren't living and breathing this football club as they should be - and as professionals should. 'Why? Because it's gone to their heads. They are nothing, some of those players.' Carrick chose to leave Bruno Fernandes on the substitutes bench on Sunday after the club captain's scathing remarks about team tactics in midweek and did not turn to him, even with the team losing. It represented the first time Fernandes has been pulled from the line-up for non-fitness reasons since Carrick, again, took him out against Villarreal in November 2021. Jamie Carragher believes Carrick 'deliberately tried to embarrass' Fernandes by snubbing him on Sunday. For Neville, the simple fact that Fernandes was willing to break rank as he did and publicly take a swipe at Carrick shows that the players have turned on the manager. He went on: 'He's not been able to get a tune out of them and they've turned on him. I know that because if Bruno has turned on him publicly, with that little statement, imagine what they're like behind the scenes. 'If that's your captain saying that, imagine what they're saying in the dressing room behind closed doors when no one's listening. That's horrific.' United were beaten 3-0 at home by Bournemouth and the manager is hanging on by a thread United are 16th in the Premier League and some bookmakers have suspended betting on Carrick being axed. Eddie Howe remains the current betting favourite to take the helm if indeed United choose to pull the trigger just months after making Carrick permanent boss following his interim spell. Carrick put his hand to his chest and showed his appreciation for the support fans offered him after the Bournemouth defeat but insisted his gestures should not be interpreted as a farewell. Asked if he expects to be sacked, Carrick said: ‘I totally understand the situation. I'm not expecting anything either way. ‘I’m carrying on as normal. I love this place. I'll always do what I feel is going to be the best for the football club and I won’t change that now, whatever decision is made. ‘It's a tough situation, there's no hiding from it. What it looks like and what's next I really don't know. I love what I do and I feel the responsibility. We'll have to wait and see. ‘Of course, I take responsibility. I respect the position that I'm in, and the responsibility is mine. What else can I say really right now? ‘I've tried to do everything I can to not be in this position, of course I have. For a number of reasons, we've not been able to stop that happening to the position we're in right now. ‘I've been at the club a long time. It hurts an awful lot to see us going through this at this moment in time. The situation is where we are and we haven't had results or performances that have been good enough.’ ‘It wasn't a farewell from me,’ Carrick insisted. ‘I probably didn't really expect that off the supporters, if I'm honest, but I've always felt the support and that connection with them. ‘It will take a bit of time to digest, but I certainly appreciate their support. It's difficult for me to have a day like this at this club and feel the emotion. ‘I'm feeling it for my players, they're going through a tough spell. There's a lot of emotion in the changing room right now, there's a lot of the boys quite hurt, to be fair. ‘It's not like they don't care or they want to be in this position. The ones I've spoken to, it’s affecting them a lot.’ READ: This was the end for Michael Carrick after his gang of the damned were relentlessly dismantled 3-0 by Bournemouth... he will be the next to walk into Man United's endless winter, writes OLIVER HOLT READ: Man United 0-3 Bournemouth PLAYER RATINGS: Which 3/10 star was totally off the pace in Old Trafford disaster? Sports.title: Betting SUSPENDED on Man United to sack Michael Carrick after humiliating 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth - with Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann favourites to replace him
Sports.content:
Bookmakers have suspended betting on Michael Carrick being sacked by Manchester United. The 45-year-old manager presided over yet another humiliating defeat on Sunday, watching his side go down 3-0 at home against Bournemouth. His United future is hanging by a thread and almost all major betting companies are no longer offering a market on Carrick being dismissed. Attention inevitably then turns to who might replace Carrick if indeed the axe does fall, with United languishing in 16th in the Premier League table. And ex-Premier League winner Conte (5/1) left Napoli by mutual consent at the conclusion of last season.
