This high-growth, capital-light platform broadens the Group’s exposure to advisory, asset management, trusteeship, brokerage and securities activities, reducing reliance on traditional banking spreads.

Why the investment case is strengthening

FirstHoldCo’s investment case is increasingly persuasive because improvement is visible across several reinforcing dimensions: faster earnings growth, better operating efficiency, expanding transaction-led revenues, stronger capital, disciplined loan growth and an improving asset quality position. These are not isolated gains; they describe a franchise becoming more resilient and better positioned to convert scale into sustainable returns.

The Group is well positioned to unlock the next phase of value creation by building on its current momentum. Continued progress toward a single-digit NPL ratio, sustained coverage, recovery in net interest margin, disciplined deployment of deposits, and greater fee income contribution provide clear pathways to stronger, more resilient earnings. Consistent execution should improve earnings quality and deepen market confidence.

Enhanced dividend policy reinforces the shareholder-value proposition

The market is already recognising this stronger proposition: as of 23 October 2026, FirstHoldCo’s 200.84% year-to-date share-price gain had delivered the highest total shareholder return in 2026 among its banking peers, signaling strong investor confidence in the Group’s earnings momentum and outlook.

Reinforcing these market gains, FirstHoldCo earlier this year reaffirmed its commitment to shareholder returns through an enhanced dividend policy. Under the policy, the Board approved a minimum annual distribution of 60% of profit after tax, commencing with the 2027 accounts. The policy gives shareholders a clearer route to participate in earnings growth and signals confidence in the Group’s profitability, capital and cash-generation.



The timing is strategically important. Beginning with the 2027 accounts allows FirstHoldCo to consolidate capital strength, further improve asset-quality and fund disciplined growth before the higher payout takes effect. Subject to distributable reserves, regulatory approvals and prevailing financial conditions, the policy offers a credible path to stronger shareholder returns.

Outlook: Disciplined growth with meaningful optionality

FirstHoldCo enters the final quarter of 2026 with a stronger balance sheet, improving credit metrics and enhanced operating leverage. Its N22.91 trillion deposit base provides substantial funding capacity, while the improved capital position creates room for selective expansion. Targeted investment in technology, innovation and customer experience can deepen transaction volumes and strengthen the durability of non-interest revenue.



The investment story therefore extends beyond stronger earnings. Capital strength, franchise depth, cost discipline and diversified capabilities make performance more sustainable. Margin pressure and the remaining NPL stock still require attention, but each also presents a defined opportunity for improvement.

Overall, the 9Months 2026 results show a Group regaining strategic flexibility and converting reform into measurable progress. Continued improvement in asset quality, margin recovery and disciplined capital allocation provide a credible path to resilient earnings and durable long-term value

World.title: Afternoon thunderstorms possible in southern Gauteng on Monday
World.content:
Isolated afternoon showers and thundershowers are expected in southern Gauteng on Monday. Image: Unsplash

Parts of southern Gauteng could experience afternoon showers and thundershowers on Monday, 26 October, while warm to hot conditions continue across the province.

The South African Weather Service (SAWS) forecasts partly cloudy skies across Gauteng, with isolated showers and thundershowers expected in the south during the afternoon.

However, not all areas will receive rain, and some places could remain dry throughout the day.



What to expect in other provinces

While Gauteng could experience afternoon thundershowers, several other provinces are also expecting rain.

Mpumalanga: Isolated showers and thundershowers could develop over the eastern and southern Highveld.

The province will experience partly cloudy and warm conditions, while temperatures in the Lowveld will climb to hot or very hot levels.



Limpopo: Fine skies and hot to very hot temperatures will dominate the province.

North West: Partly cloudy, windy and hot conditions will continue, with isolated showers and thundershowers in some areas.

Free State: The province will experience partly cloudy, windy and warm to hot weather.



Isolated showers and thundershowers are expected, becoming scattered in the extreme east and along the Lesotho border.

Northern Cape: Partly cloudy, windy and hot conditions will affect much of the province, while the extreme south will remain warm.

Isolated afternoon showers and thundershowers could develop in the east.



Western Cape: Cloudy skies will bring isolated rain and showers to the south and adjacent eastern interior, where conditions will range from cool to warm.

Other areas will experience fine and warm weather, with partly cloudy skies along the west.

Eastern Cape: The western half will experience cloudy and cool conditions, with isolated rain and showers along the coast and adjacent interior. Isolated thunderstorms could develop over the interior and northern areas.



The eastern half will remain cloudy and cool to cold in places, with scattered showers and thunderstorms.

KwaZulu-Natal: Morning fog could develop over the interior before partly cloudy and cool to warm conditions take over. Northern areas will become hot in places, while scattered showers and thundershowers could affect the province.

What should residents keep in mind during thunderstorms?

Residents planning outdoor activities should check their local forecasts, particularly in areas expecting afternoon showers and thunderstorms.



Motorists should also take care on wet roads, as rainfall could reduce visibility and make driving conditions slippery.

SAWS encourages the public to follow its latest forecasts and weather warnings as conditions change.

World.title: Proteas vs Australia: Coetzee replaces Nortje for Newlands Test
World.content:
Anrich Nortje is replaced for the Proteas third Test against Australia after an injury. Image: Zoobit1, Ellisroger (Flickr).

The Proteas begin their decisive third Test against Australia tomorrow (27 October).

With Anrich Nortje out injured, coach Shukri Conrad had some decisions to make.

Here’s who will replace the pace bowler for the third Test match in Cape Town.



Proteas vs Australia: Series results so far

The first Test was played from 9-13 October at Kingsmead in Durban.

Australia posted a first-innings total of 390, and the Proteas could only manage 284 in reply.

The Baggy Greens then declared on 314/6 in their second innings, leaving South Africa a huge target of 447.



The Proteas were bundled out for just 206, thanks to a six-wicket effort by Australia’s Josh Hazlewood.

Things changed in a rain-soaked second Test at St George’s Park in Gqeberha, from 18-22 October.

Australia bowled only 54 overs across the first two days, making a draw look likely.



Instead, captain Temba Bavuma anchored a stunning 425/9 first innings total.

Australia were then bowled out for just 99 as Marco Jansen claimed a five-wicket haul.

Having to follow on, the visitors had hopes of salvaging a draw late on day 5.



However, the Proteas got the job done eventually, winning by an innings and 31 runs.

This leaves everything to play for in the third Test, from 27-31 October at Newlands in Cape Town.

Who will replace Anrich Nortje?

The pace bowler, who had only recently returned to the longest format, suffered a groin injury during the second Test.



However, the question remained who could step up, and whether coach Conrad would stick with a mostly pace lineup.

The Proteas’ Instagram post confirmed the playing XI just after lunch today (26 October).

Aiden Markram

Marques Ackerman

David Bedingham

Temba Bavuma

Matthew Breetzke

Ryan Rickelton

Wiaan Mulder

Marco Jansen

Simon Harmer

Gerald Coetzee

Kagiso Rabada

Playing XI for Third Dafabet Test vs Australia 🚨#TheProteas skipper, Temba Bavuma, confirms the playing XI for tomorrow’s third and final Dafabet Test, with the series on the line at YesPlay Newlands. 🇿🇦



🔁 One change for #TheProteas sees Gerald Coetzee coming in for Anrich… pic.twitter.com/lRZobnN0OQ  October 26, 2026

While some fans believed Coetzee was an obvious choice, he has not played a Test in nearly two years.

According to ESPN Cricinfo, his last long-format game was against Sri Lanka in November 2024.

Some fans were gutted that Dane Paterson did not get a chance in front of his home crowd.



Others criticised the decision to omit Corbin Bosch and Senuran Muthusamy.

Instead, the Proteas have stuck with their strong pace core of Rabada, Jansen, and Mulder.

The fast attack worked wonders against Australia at St George’s, claiming 18 of the 20 total wickets.



According to News24, pace bowlers record better numbers at Newlands, which is good news for Coetzee.

WHO WILL WIN THE PROTEAS VS AUSTRALIA TEST SERIES?

World.title: Orlando Pirates boss has ‘favourite player’ backed up by stats
World.content:
Orlando Pirates boss Abdeslam Ouaddou trusts a key core of his title-winning squad. Who’s the ultimate favourite?

Ouaddou relies on a consistent core at Orlando pirates

Abdeslam Ouaddou recently underlined the importance of having several leaders dotted through the spine of his team selection. Continuity in selection has also been a key theme, with four players already racking up 50 appearances under the French-born Moroccan tactician. Tshepang Moremi is the most recent player to achieve the feat, and his red-hot form in front of goal makes him arguably their most important attacker right now. Moremi joins the 50 club along with Oswin Appollis, Sipho Chaine and Lebone Seema. Moremi has netted in two of the club’s last three matches, notably the only goal away to African Stars in CAF Champions League qualifying. Moremi has four goals in six league outings this term.

50 – Tshepang Moremi has made 50 appearances for Orlando Pirates, becoming the fourth player at the club to reach the mark under Abdeslam Ouaddou. Trusted. pic.twitter.com/MVyRL3wdD4  October 22, 2026

What’s next for Orlando Pirates?

The Sea Robbers face Milford FC in the Nedbank Cup on Tuesday, 27 October at 19:00. They arrive in good form, winning three matches on the bounce across all competitions and not conceding a single goal in that sequence.

Mbokazi’s options after the MLS

In today’s financial climate, elite European clubs can part ways with €20m (R369 million) and not consider it much of a risk. In fact, it could turn out to be an incredibly shrewd investment with massive upside. 21-year-old former Orlando Pirates star Mbekezeli Mbokazi could start to outgrow his surroundings in the United States MLS. What are his next stepping stones if he leaves Chicago Fire and looks at offers from England and Italy?

Is Moremi Pirates’ most important player? Add your thoughts by clicking the red comments banner below!

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs rumours: Maboe, Da Cruz future, McCarthy, new wonderkid
World.content:
Today’s Kaizer Chiefs news wrap looks at Lebohang Maboe’s fitness, Fernando Da Cruz’s future, Aden McCarthy’s lucky transfer twist and Steven Mendes’ rise to the first team.

Did McCarthy get lucky?

Following a winter move to Azerbaijani outfit Sabah FK, it’s been a steady growth curve for 22-year-old defender Aden McCarthy. The former Kaizer Chiefs man scored his first goal in Europe’s elite club competition, the Champions League, on Wednesday night in Sabah’s 1-2 defeat to Borussia Dortmund. Sabah beat Slavia Praha 2-0 on matchday 2, their first ever win in the competition. Some local online chatter speculates that McCarthy earned his big move to Sabah because his agent has a strong European passport, and therefore has easier access to contacts on the continent. It’s a theory, for sure.

Kaizer Chiefs playing catch-up and it’s October

After just eight games of the new Betway Premiership campaign, Kaizer Chiefs are already trailing leaders Sundowns by nine points, and Orlando Pirates by eight. They’ve only triumphed in one of their last seven clashes across all competitions. With just a solitary piece of silverware in the last 10 years (a Nedbank Cup triumph in last year’s final against Pirates), it’s difficult to escape the conclusion that Chiefs are horribly underachieving, given their fanbase and huge financial might. If results don’t improve quickly, it’s easy to envisage Da Cruz being sacked before Christmas. If they’re out of contention for CAF Champions League football, that should be the final nail in his coffin. Next up for the Glamour Boys is a Nedbank Cup clash against TS Galaxy at Soccer City on Tuesday, 27 October at 19:00. Playmaker Lebohang Maboe is still unavailable through injury.



Mendes is one to watch for Kaizer Chiefs

18-year-old Steven Mendes won the Golden Boot at the recent COSAFA U20 tournament in Maputo, Mozambique. Mendes, nominally a midfielder, was converted into a striker for the event. He’s nicknamed ‘Stevie G’ by some teammates and could feature for the senior side sooner rather than later. After all, Vela Khumalo knows what he’s talking about when it comes to talented youngsters.

Will Chiefs sack Da Cruz before Christmas? Add your thoughts by clicking the red comments banner below!

World.title: Applying for a digital nomad visa? The paperwork that could get you rejected
World.content:
Most digital nomad visas require proof of income, insurance and remote work. Image: Pexels

Digital nomad visa requirements can trip up even the most organised South African.

Working from a beach or a mountain cabin sounds simple.

The paperwork isn’t.



And one missing document could be enough to get your application rejected.

Here’s what could get you rejected: most digital nomad visas ask for proof of income, health or travel insurance and proof that you work remotely.

Some also ask for extra documents that many applicants only discover at the last minute.

A VALID PASSPORT

It sounds obvious, but it catches people out.

The Department of International Relations and Cooperation (DIRCO) advises that South African passports should be valid for at least six months after your return date, with at least two blank pages.

For a long stay abroad, check your passport’s expiry date against the full length of your planned visa, not just your flight dates.



PROOF OF INCOME

Most nomad visas set a minimum monthly income.

For example, Namibia’s digital nomad visa requires at least $2,000 (about R32,900) a month, according to the Namibia Investment Promotion and Development Board (NIPDB).

Applicants usually need to prove their income with documents such as:

recent bank statements,

payslips,

or contracts with clients, if you’re a freelancer.

Make sure your statements clearly show regular income that meets the country’s minimum.

PROOF THAT YOU WORK REMOTELY

Nomad visas are designed for people who work for employers or clients based outside the country they’re visiting.

You’ll usually need to prove this, for example with:

a letter from your employer confirming that you can work remotely,

confirming that you can work remotely, your employment contract,

or contracts with international clients.

In Namibia’s case, applicants must work for companies or clients based outside Namibia.

HEALTH OR TRAVEL INSURANCE

This is one of the most common reasons applications fall short.

Many countries require insurance that covers your entire stay, not just your first few weeks.

Georgia, for example, has required all tourists to have health and accident insurance, with minimum cover of GEL30,000 (about R181,000), since 1 January 2026, according to Georgia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Border officials check it on arrival, and visitors without a valid policy can be refused entry.

Before you buy a policy, check:

the minimum cover the country requires,

the country requires, that the policy covers the full length of your stay,

of your stay, and that it covers medical emergencies, not just lost luggage or flight delays.

OTHER DOCUMENTS YOU MIGHT NEED

Depending on the country, you may also be asked for:

a police clearance certificate, which can take several weeks to get from the South African Police Service (SAPS),

which can take several weeks to get from the South African Police Service (SAPS), proof of accommodation, such as a rental agreement,

such as a rental agreement, documents for family members, if they’re travelling with you,

if they’re travelling with you, or proof of funds to support yourself during your stay.

Some countries also require official documents to be legalised, which you can arrange through DIRCO.

TIMING MATTERS

Some programmes require you to apply well before you travel. Seychelles, for example, asks remote workers to apply for its Visitors Workcation Permit at least two weeks before travelling.

Start gathering documents early, since things like police clearance certificates and legalised documents can take weeks.

DIGITAL NOMAD VISA REQUIREMENTS: DON’T FORGET TAX

Before you go, check how working abroad could affect your tax.

If you remain a South African tax resident, the South African Revenue Service (SARS) can still tax your worldwide income, although you may qualify for an exemption on part of it.

World.title: Ben Youssef identifies biggest weakness with Mdu Shabalala at Chiefs
World.content:
Former Kaizer Chiefs coach Khalil Ben Youssef has identified an area of concern in Mduduzi Shabalala’s game, pointing to decision-making and player development as key issues affecting the midfielder.

The 22-year-old has struggled in front of goal this season despite being presented with several opportunities to find the back of the net.

Shabalala endured a frustrating outing against Red Arrows in the second leg of the CAF Confederation Cup preliminary round, missing two golden opportunities that could have helped Amakhosi secure a place in the group stages.



Ben Youssef, who coached Shabalala at Kaizer Chiefs, believes that while talent is important, a player’s mindset, understanding of the game and ability to make the right decisions are equally crucial.

“I think talent is important in football, but for me, the most important thing is the mindset. Also, if you understand football, you will know how to run and where to run. You will know what to do when you receive the ball,” he told SoccerBeat.

“Like you said about Shabalala, one-v-one, what decision do you have to make and how do you finish the situation?”



Mdu has been missing a lot of chances for Kaizer Chiefs

The Tunisian coach pointed out that Shabalala’s struggles in front of goal are not new, recalling a similar situation last season in the Carling Knockout Cup match against Stellenbosch FC.

“You remember last season, we had the same problem with Shabalala. It was in the Carling Cup game against Stellenbosch. He found himself one-on-one with the goalkeeper and missed both chances,” Ben Youssef said.

For the former Chiefs coach, Shabalala’s struggles reflect a broader concern about the development of South African footballers.



“For me, the big problem in South Africa is the development of the player,” he added.

Shabalala has scored twice for Kaizer Chiefs this season, and improving his decision-making and composure in front of goal will be important if he is to become more consistent in the final third.

World.title: Forget city lights: 5 of the best places for stargazing in South Africa
World.content:
South Africa’s dark skies make it one of the best places in the world for stargazing. Image: Pexels

Stargazing in South Africa is some of the best in the world.

Away from the city lights, the night sky comes alive with stars, planets and even neighbouring galaxies.

You don’t need a telescope to enjoy it.

You just need to know where to go.

WHY SOUTH AFRICA IS GREAT FOR STARGAZING

South Africa’s wide open spaces, dry air and low light pollution make many parts of the country ideal for stargazing.



From the Southern Hemisphere, you can also see sights that aren’t visible from Europe or most of North America, including the Southern Cross and the Magellanic Clouds, two small galaxies close to our own Milky Way.

SUTHERLAND, NORTHERN CAPE

Sutherland is South Africa’s stargazing capital.

It’s home to the South African Astronomical Observatory (SAAO) and the Southern African Large Telescope (SALT), the biggest single-mirror optical telescope in the Southern Hemisphere.



Visitors can tour the observatory, and the town’s high altitude and clear skies make it ideal for stargazing.

Just pack something warm, since Sutherland is known as one of the coldest towns in the country.

THE KAROO

The vast, sparsely populated Karoo has some of the darkest skies in South Africa.



Many guest farms and small towns across the region offer stargazing evenings, often with a telescope and a guide who can point out the constellations.

NIEU-BETHESDA, EASTERN CAPE

This tiny Karoo village is known for its quirky charm, and for its remarkably dark skies.

With very little light pollution, it’s one of the best places in the country to see the Milky Way stretching across the sky.



THE CEDERBERG, WESTERN CAPE

The Cederberg mountains, about three hours from Cape Town, combine dramatic rock formations with clear night skies.

It’s a popular escape for Capetonians who want to see the stars without travelling too far.

THE KALAHARI, NORTHERN CAPE

The Kalahari offers some of South Africa’s emptiest landscapes, and some of its most spectacular night skies.



WHEN TO GO STARGAZING

Check the moon. Plan your trip around the new moon , when the sky is darkest. A full moon can wash out fainter stars.

Plan your trip around the , when the sky is darkest. A full moon can wash out fainter stars. Watch for meteor showers. The Geminid meteor shower peaks on the night of 13 to 14 December 2026 , and the moon will be a thin crescent, so it won’t wash out the show. From South Africa, you’ll see fewer meteors than in the Northern Hemisphere, and the best time to watch is from midnight until just before dawn .

The peaks on the night of , and the moon will be a thin crescent, so it won’t wash out the show. From South Africa, you’ll see fewer meteors than in the Northern Hemisphere, and the best time to watch is from . Check the weather. Summer afternoons can bring thunderstorms in some inland areas, so keep an eye on the forecast.

TIPS FOR BETTER STARGAZING

Give your eyes time to adjust. It can take around 20 minutes for your eyes to get used to the dark.

It can take around 20 minutes for your eyes to get used to the dark. Avoid looking at your phone, or use a red light, so you don’t lose your night vision.

or use a red light, so you don’t lose your night vision. Download a stargazing app to help identify stars and constellations.

to help identify stars and constellations. Bring warm clothes, since even summer nights can get cold in the Karoo.

There’s something humbling about lying on your back in the Karoo, staring up at more stars than you ever knew existed.

I think every South African should experience a truly dark sky at least once.

My advice? Leave the city behind, switch off your phone and just look up.

World.title: From Carnegie to Claude: AI wealth could reshape philanthropy
World.content:
NEW YORK - A wave of American wealth created by artificial intelligence companies could produce some of the largest charitable sums since the era of Andrew Carnegie and John D. Rockefeller, raising questions about where the money goes.

Anthropic, the maker of the Claude chatbot, has said it would commit 5 percent of its shares to a new Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, a stake that could be worth around $100 billion if the company reaches the $2 trillion valuation investors are eyeing for a stock market debut expected as early as November.

Combined with pledges by its seven co-founders to give away 80 percent of their equity and a program matching employees’ donations, Anthropic says roughly a fifth of its shares will be dedicated to public-benefit purposes.

"This might be one of the biggest stories in corporate philanthropy ever," said Michael Moody, a professor of philanthropic studies at Indiana University’s Lilly Family School of Philanthropy.

The OpenAI Foundation, the nonprofit that controls ChatGPT maker OpenAI, holds a 26 percent stake in the company that was valued at about $130 billion when it was restructured a year ago, more than the endowment of the Gates Foundation.

Nan Ransohoff of payments firm Stripe has described the moment as a "third wave" of American philanthropy, after the industrial fortunes of the late 19th century and the internet billionaires of recent decades.

World.title: AI ad blitz distorts US midterms
World.content:
WASHINGTON - The video looks hyper-real, depicting a US Senate candidate laughing at cards that read "Death to America" and "Celebrate 9/11." But it is part of a multimillion-dollar blitz of AI-generated political ads ahead of the midterm elections.

Reality-bending deepfake ads -- dubbed AI "slopaganda" by researchers and used by both sides of the political aisle to target rivals -- are proliferating across the airwaves and social media ahead of the November 3 vote.

"His family values are wrong for Michigan," said one ad that portrays Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed playing a board game with two people wearing traditional kaffiyehs, the checkered Arab scarves.

The lifelike ad features cards bearing incendiary statements and depicts a fabricated family photo of the Muslim candidate with four women wearing head-to-toe veils.

"Destruction of Israel and the West isn't just a game for them," a voiceover says. "It's a mission."

Front Line Action, a political action committee aligned with Republican Senator Ted Cruz, was behind the video. It spent over $92,000 on advertising opposing El-Sayed, according to a filing with the Federal Election Commission.

The ad carries a disclaimer that it was "created in whole or in part with the use of artificial intelligence."

Most AI-created ads do not carry such a label, researchers say, further distorting an information landscape already plagued by election disinformation.

- 'Slippery slope' -

The Wesleyan Media Project, which tracks election ad spending, has so far identified 220 political ads nationwide -- most sponsored by Republicans -- that were generated at least in part using AI tools.

It estimates that the ads cost more than $137 million. By comparison, it identified less than $50,000 in spending on AI-generated ads in the 2024 election cycle.

Eighty-one percent of the AI-created ads were sponsored by Republican candidates or groups, 12 percent by Democrats, and the remainder by independent candidates or groups, it added.

"AI is making its way into the 2026 midterms in a big way this year," said Erika Franklin Fowler, co-director of the Wesleyan Media Project.

She added that only 27 percent of the ads carried an AI disclaimer, calling the trend "problematic."

The group said its ads tally was almost certainly an undercount as it was difficult to determine definitively whether AI tools had been used in their creation.

There were no federal mandates that political ads carry an AI disclaimer, though some states have legislated to restrict the use of AI or require disclosures.

"It is deeply troubling to see these deepfake videos used to fabricate political advertising," Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff told C-SPAN last month.

"And it's a slippery slope toward the destruction of truth in political debate."

- 'Mobilising voters' -

Ossoff's comment came as he demanded the removal of a fabricated ad -- which carried no AI disclosure -- portraying him receiving beauty treatments at a salon and covering up his "ugly record."

The Senate Leadership Fund, a political action committee that describes itself as "solely dedicated to protecting and expanding the Republican Senate majority," was behind the ad.

The proliferation of such ads in the midterms -- which the London-based Institute for Strategic Dialogue called the first US election in which AI is built into every major social media platform -- comes against the backdrop of declining trust in the technology.

In a recent survey by the nonprofit AAPC Foundation, 73 percent said it was "unacceptable" for a political campaign to use AI to generate images or video in an ad.

Ninety-five percent said it was unacceptable to "create a video of an opponent saying something they never said."

But researchers played down concerns that the ads could influence election results.

"Political slopaganda is likely more effective at mobilising voters or raising money than it is in impacting candidate selection," New York University's Center on Tech Policy said in a research report earlier this month.

"Like digital memes, there may be limits to its attentional staying power, especially as we become more and more inundated with AI slop."

World.title: Antonelli looks to seal title 'in style' after US Grand Prix win
World.content:
MEXICO CITY - Kimi Antonelli said his mindset will not change as he heads to next week's race in Mexico seeking the two points he needs to become Formula One’s youngest world champion.

The 20-year-old Italian delivered a well-executed and dominant drive to claim his ninth victory this year for Mercedes in Sunday’s United States Grand Prix and move within reach of the title.

Antonelli is on the brink of smashing the previous record for youngest champion, held by Sebastian Vettel who was 23 years and 133 days old when he won his first title in 2010

He is also set to become the first Italian to win the title since Alberto Ascari in 1953.

"The best way, the perfect way, would be to finish off in style and then just enjoy the rest of the season,” he said.

"I'm very aware that it's very close but the mindset doesn't change.

"I want to finish the season on a high in order to then go with high hopes into 2027. But we'll first focus and worry about finishing this well, and then we'll see."

After Sunday’s triumph at the Circuit of the Americas he leads with 365 points ahead of nearest rival and team-mate George Russell on 242 and seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton of Ferrari on 241.

He will be champion if he finishes in the top nine or, if he doesn't score, Russell or Hamilton fail to win.

But on current form, after winning again for the first time in four races, he looks certain to take the title in his own happy, generous and infectious style.

"That was the perfect way to end the weekend,” he said.

“It was an incredible team effort, especially from strategy, to believe in me and go for one stop because I wasn't sure whether one or two stop was the quickest.

"But I’m really happy that we made it stick. Today was a really important victory for me and for the team, especially after having a couple of difficult races, so being back on top feels very good."

Antonelli's ability on the track and infectious attitude off it have landed him numerous admirers around the paddock, including 1996 world champion Damon Hill.

“The team love him, he's enjoying everything he's got in F1 and he's very grateful for all the breaks they've given him at Mercedes," Hill said on the BBC.

"But he delivers. He's such a nice kid. It's incredible. Twenty years old and he's on the verge of winning his first championship, which I'm sure will be the first of many.”
