World.title: Kenya: Nairobi Water Shutdown to Hit Parts of Nairobi for Three Days
World.content:
Nairobi — Residents in several parts of Nairobi will experience a three-day water supply interruption following an emergency shutdown of a major pipeline for repairs.

The Nairobi City Water and Sewerage Company (NCWSC) said the shutdown of the NCT-Kigoro-Gigiri-Kabete pipeline by the Athi Water Works Development Agency (AWWDA) would begin on Monday, October 26, and end on Thursday, October 29, at 11.59pm.

The interruption is expected to affect residential estates, hospitals, businesses and institutions across several parts of the city, including Westlands, Parklands, Lavington, Kilimani, Kileleshwa, Lang'ata, Karen, Nairobi West and Upper Hill.

Other affected areas include Riverside, Ngong Road, Kibera, Jamhuri, Woodley, Adams Arcade and parts of Mbagathi Road.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

In Upper Hill, the shutdown is expected to affect Kenyatta National Hospital and Nairobi Hospital, while residents of Lang'ata will experience interruptions in areas including Uhuru Gardens, Southlands, Civil Servants Estate, Moi Lang'ata Barracks, Sunvalley and Royal Park.

Residents of Nairobi West, Madaraka, Siwaka, Wilson Airport and surrounding estates will also be affected.

In the western and northern parts of the city, the affected areas include Westlands, Brookside, Lantana Road, General Mathenge Road, Peponi Road, Lower Kabete Lane, Parklands, Highridge, Limuru Road, Chiromo Lane and Waiyaki Way.

The shutdown will also affect parts of Ngara, Park Road, City Park, Forest Road, Kipande Road and Desai Road, as well as the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP), the US Embassy and surrounding areas.

Residents of Kihingo Estate, Magnolia, Kinanda Valley, Lower Raphta Road, Upper Lantana Road and parts of James Gichuru Road have also been listed among those likely to experience interruptions.

The company urged customers in the affected areas to conserve the water available to them as repair works continue.

In a public notice signed by managing director Martin Nang'ole, Nairobi Water apologised for the inconvenience and said the shutdown was necessary to facilitate emergency repairs on the pipeline.

"We appeal to our customers for indulgence and urge them to use their available water sparingly as we work towards restoring the supply," the company said.

The interruption comes as households and businesses in the affected neighbourhoods are expected to make alternative arrangements for their water needs during the repair period.Nairobi Water said supply would be restored following the completion of the works.

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - October 26, 2026
World.content:
Ruto Mourns 23 Killed in Kenya Road Crash

Kenyan President William Ruto has mourned the deaths of 23 people in a road accident at Kanga, near Mtito Andei, along the busy Nairobi-Mombasa Highway. In a condolence message shared on social media, Ruto expressed sympathy with the victims' families and friends, describing the incident as a devastating loss for the country. He also wished those injured a speedy recovery and urged motorists to exercise greater caution and comply with traffic regulations. The President specifically called on drivers operating public service vehicles (PSVs) to prioritise passenger safety and directed the relevant authorities to conduct thorough inspections to ensure vehicles meet the required safety standards. The crash has renewed concerns about road safety and the enforcement of traffic regulations along one of Kenya's key transport corridors, which carries passenger buses, commercial vehicles and private motorists between the capital and the coastal region.

Nigeria Tracks 53 Contacts After Confirming Ebola Case

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Nigeria's Centre for Disease Control and Prevention has identified 53 contacts linked to the country's confirmed Ebola case in the Federal Capital Territory. The contacts include healthcare workers, the patient's husband and domestic staff, as well as personnel involved in collecting samples. Authorities said that none had tested positive or developed symptoms at the time of the briefing, and all are being monitored for 21 days after their last possible exposure. Nigeria is strengthening laboratory capacity, infection prevention measures and preparedness in higher-risk states. Investigations are also examining a possible link with Ebola cases in Kenya, following findings of genetic similarities between the viruses, although authorities say there is no evidence the Nigerian patient travelled to Kenya. The NCDC has urged the public to cooperate with contact-tracing teams, report symptoms and rely on verified information from health authorities.

Gabon Lifts Eight-Month Social Media Ban

Gabon has lifted its eight-month social media ban, which was introduced in February over concerns that online content was fuelling conflict and deepening divisions. The ban took effect on 17 February, with the High Communication Authority (HAC) saying online content was fuelling conflict and deepening divisions in the country. The restriction drew widespread criticism, particularly from young people and businesses reliant on platforms such as Facebook, TikTok, YouTube and Instagram. Many users resorted to virtual private networks (VPNs) to bypass the ban. The ban came at a time when Gabonese President Brice Oligui Nguema faced a wave of social unrest less than a year after his election. The suspension came amid social unrest, including strikes by teachers and civil servants over pay and working conditions. The opposition said the suspension was an abuse of power.

Nigerian President Tinubu Launches Campaign for Second Term

Nigerian President Bola Tinubu has officially launched his campaign for re-election ahead of the country's presidential election in January 2027. Addressing thousands of supporters at a rally in Kaduna, Tinubu defended his administration's record and promised Nigerians a better future, citing economic recovery, growth and new opportunities. However, his campaign comes amid public frustration over the rising cost of living, inflation and poverty following the removal of long-standing fuel subsidies after he took office in 2023. Tinubu blamed previous administrations for the country's economic difficulties, maintaining that his reforms were intended to address longstanding weaknesses. Security is also expected to feature prominently in the election, as Nigeria continues to face armed banditry, kidnappings and a prolonged jihadist insurgency. At least 20 people were reportedly killed in a gun attack in the country's northeast on Friday. Tinubu is expected to face strong competition from former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and former governor Peter Obi.

Africa CDC Calls for Immediate Lifting of Sanctions on Zimbabwe

The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) has endorsed the African Union's call for the immediate and unconditional lifting of unilateral sanctions imposed on Zimbabwe. In a statement issued on 25 October, the continental public health agency warned that restrictions affecting health financing, procurement and legitimate financial transactions could increase costs and disrupt access to essential medical supplies and services. Africa CDC Director-General Dr Jean Kaseya said that healthcare must not become collateral damage in political disputes, warning that patients could be denied life-saving treatment and health workers left without essential supplies. The agency called for uninterrupted access to medicines, vaccines, diagnostic equipment and essential care, particularly for children, pregnant women and people requiring continuous treatment. It also urged governments, international partners, financial institutions and suppliers to remove unnecessary barriers to health-related cooperation. Africa CDC reaffirmed its commitment to supporting Zimbabwe's Ministry of Health and Child Care in strengthening disease surveillance, laboratory services, healthcare staffing and emergency preparedness, emphasising that protecting Zimbabwe's health system is vital to wider African health security.

UN Condemns Surge in Deadly Drone Attacks Across Sudan

Close 

The United Nations has condemned an escalation in drone attacks across Sudan after documenting at least 306 deaths and hundreds of injuries during the first three weeks of October. The attacks, attributed to both the Sudanese Armed Forces and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces, have targeted civilian areas and critical infrastructure, including homes, markets, hospitals, displacement sites, electricity stations and water sources. UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk warned that the increasing use of drones was worsening civilian suffering, forcing further displacement and deepening the country's humanitarian crisis. Among the incidents documented were attacks on shelters housing displaced people in West Kordofan, where at least 25 civilians were killed, and a strike near a displacement site in Blue Nile state that killed at least 31 people, mostly women and children. Another drone attack on a transport truck in Dibab, West Kordofan, reportedly killed at least 139 people on 18 October. Markets and healthcare facilities have also been hit, with one hospital forced to suspend operations after an attack injured two health workers. Türk urged both sides to cease attacks on civilians, stop the flow of weapons fuelling the conflict and commit to a ceasefire. Separately, the UN Security Council condemned deadly drone strikes in the disputed Abyei region and called for a transparent investigation, accountability and the withdrawal of military forces to protect civilians.

World.title: Kenya: Police Rescue 59 Ethiopians, Including Four-Year-Old Child, in Marsabit Smuggling Operation
World.content:
Kenya Red Cross continues to support families displaced by insecurity due to conflict across the border in Moyale, Marsabit County.

Nairobi — Police have rescued 59 Ethiopian nationals, including a four-year-old child, in a multi-agency operation targeting suspected human smuggling in Marsabit County.

The operation, conducted on Saturday, also resulted in the arrest of a caretaker suspected of harbouring the victims at a residential house in Jirime Location, Marsabit Central Sub-County.

According to a police report, officers from the Counter Intelligence and Operations Team (COICT) in Moyale, Kenya Police Service (KPS) Marsabit, Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI) Marsabit and Administration Police Service (APS) Marsabit conducted the operation following a tip-off.

The officers first raided a residence belonging to a man identified as Aden Lama, where they rescued 30 Ethiopian nationals comprising 23 males and seven females.



A suspect identified as Halkano Guyo Galgalo, who was reportedly the caretaker of the residential property, was arrested on suspicion of harbouring the victims.

Police said the suspect was detained to assist with investigations into the suspected human smuggling operation.

Further intelligence gathered during the operation indicated that additional victims had been moved to another location, prompting officers to pursue them.

The multi-agency team subsequently rescued another 29 people, comprising 28 adults and a four-year-old child, approximately 14 kilometres towards Shegel area along the Marsabit-North Horr Road.

The second group included 20 male and eight female adults, alongside the minor.

The rescue brought the total number of Ethiopian nationals recovered during the operation to 59 adults and one child.

Police said the operation was led by the Sub-County Police Commander (SCPC) for Marsabit Central, while COICT Moyale was tasked with investigations.

The arrested caretaker was taken into custody as investigators sought to establish the circumstances under which the Ethiopian nationals were being accommodated and whether other individuals were involved in the suspected smuggling network.

Police did not immediately disclose the intended destination of the victims or how long they had been held at the locations.

The authorities also did not provide details regarding the condition of the rescued individuals or whether additional suspects were being pursued.

The operation comes amid continued efforts by security agencies to combat human trafficking and smuggling networks operating across Kenya's northern border regions.

Marsabit County's proximity to Ethiopia and other countries in the Horn of Africa makes it a strategic area for cross-border security operations.

Close 

The rescued Ethiopian nationals and the arrested suspect were expected to assist investigators as police continued inquiries into the incident.

Authorities have not yet announced whether the suspect will face formal charges.

The investigation is ongoing.

World.title: Kenya: Ruto Mourns 23 Killed in Kanga Road Crash
World.content:
Nairobi — President William Ruto has mourned the 23 people killed in a road accident at Kanga near Mtito Andei along the Nairobi-Mombasa Highway, calling for greater caution among motorists and stricter safety inspections for public service vehicles (PSVs).

In a condolence message shared on social media, Ruto expressed sympathy with the families and friends of the victims, describing the incident as a devastating loss for the affected families and the country.

"I convey my heartfelt condolences to the families and friends of the 23 people who lost their lives in the tragic road accident," the President said, adding that the country shared in their grief.

He also wished those injured in the crash a quick recovery.



The President urged all motorists, particularly drivers operating public service vehicles, to exercise caution and observe traffic regulations to prevent further loss of life on Kenyan roads.

Ruto further directed relevant authorities to conduct thorough inspections of public service vehicles to ensure they comply with the required safety standards.

The directive comes amid renewed concerns over road safety following the fatal collision at Kanga, near Mtito Andei, on the busy Nairobi-Mombasa Highway.

The President said vehicle inspections should help ensure that public service vehicles meet the required safety standards, as part of efforts to prevent road accidents.

The accident has renewed calls for motorists to adhere to traffic rules and for authorities to strengthen enforcement of road safety regulations.

The Nairobi-Mombasa Highway is a key transport corridor connecting the capital to the Coast, carrying passenger buses, commercial vehicles and private motorists.

Ruto's call places renewed emphasis on responsible driving, compliance with traffic regulations and regular inspections of public service vehicles.

The President's message did not provide further details on the cause of the crash or the condition of those injured.

World.title: Jonathan Taylor's wife knows things so dire family is on 'Colts transaction watch' expecting trades or firing
World.content:
The 2027 NFL offseason has seemingly begun for the Indianapolis Colts and the most stunning part of it is people within the organization understand that's true.

That's how things are following a loss to the previously winless Tennessee Titans last week, the firing of general Chris Ballard one day later and a follow-up loss to the punchless but somehow undefeated Minnesota Vikings on Sunday.

That is definitely the way things are when the wife of the team's biggest star is talking openly about her husband getting traded.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

SEASON IS ALREADY OVER FOR THESE FOUR NFL TEAMS AFTER WEEK 5, YOU CAN WRITE THEM OFF NOW

Yes, you read that right.

Jonathan Taylor's wife Ayanna Taylor over the weekend posted two videos on Instagram saying "players that once seemed untouchable," like her husband, "may now be on the table" in potential trades.

Want the most depressing part of this for Colts fans? Jonathan Taylor agreed with his wife's videos that make it clear their family is on what she called "a Colts transaction watch."

"I think it's been out there already so her adding doesn't really change anything," Taylor said after Sunday's loss. "Everybody's on TikTok these days so we just have to come in to work and focus."

MYSTERY TEAM IN MARVIN HARRISON TRADE STEPS FORWARD, AS TEXANS DEMECO RYANS CONFIRMS REUNION WITH CJ STROUD

Ayanna Taylor posted about the dire situation facing her husband's team by painting in her second video the truly depressing picture of what's next.

"Look at the situation that they put themselves in," she said. "They have a losing record, they just fired their 10-year GM, and they have no draft picks. How are they going to get new leadership to come in when they really have no options for new leadership to transform the team?

"Let's think about it: What do you do when you don't have what you need and you don't have the money to pay for it? ... You trade. That's what brings us back to my husband."

FROM THE CHARGERS TO THE COLTS AND FALCONS, WHICH OF THE NFL'S EIGHT WINLESS TEAMS ARE ALREADY IN PANIC MODE

Taylor, who scored a touchdown and averaged 5.3 yards per rush against the stifling Vikings defense, is obviously a trade chip for interim general manager Ed Dodds.

If Dodds can move Taylor, or right defensive tackle DeForest Buckner, or left defensive tackle Grover Stewart or guard Quenton Nelson, or anyone not named Tyler Warren, before the Nov. 10 trade deadline, then it is a good bet he's going to consider it.

That, of course, is going to make coach Shane Steichen's life a little tougher. But maybe Steichen should have considered that before his team lost 12 of its last 14 games dating back to last season and is the only one in the NFL to lose to the Titans this season.

Besides, Steichen has bigger problems.

Bigger problem No. 1: Whether or not to bench quarterback Daniel Jones who has been a bitter disappointment. Jones threw another interception in a key situation on Sunday when the Colts were trying to rally for a go-ahead touchdown.

Jones has thrown four touchdown passes and seven interceptions in seven games and he's completing passes at a career-low clip of under 60%.

"I have not thought about a quarterback change," Steichen said after the game.

Well, Steichen should be thinking about it and problem No. 2: Owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon put him and Ballard on notice at the end of last year that the expectations for this year would be high.

Ballard is gone, so if the current trend continues firing Steichen is the next logical move. Maybe Steichen can survive the looming garage sale of players over the next couple of weeks.

But Steichen would be wise to also put himself on "Colts transaction watch."

World.title: $800-a-day penalty threatens to bleed investigative reporter dry as explosive legal fight escalates
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Former Fox News investigative reporter Catherine Herridge is asking the Supreme Court to protect her confidential sources after a federal court ordered her to identify who helped expose a woman's alleged ties to China's military.

The outcome of the case could dramatically reshape the legal protections afforded to journalists working in the U.S. under the First Amendment.

Herridge was held in contempt and ordered to pay $800 per day for refusing to reveal sources behind her 2017 reporting on Yanping Chen, a Chinese American businesswoman who operated a university attended by U.S. military personnel. Her reporting raised questions about Chen's alleged past as a colonel for the People's Liberation Army (PLA) of China and the potential exposure of sensitive information about American service members.

The Department of War subsequently cut off military tuition assistance funding to Chen's university following a national security review, according to a filing by Herridge's legal team. The school had been receiving approximately $200,000 a month in taxpayer-funded tuition assistance.

NEW YORK TIMES BLASTS ‘ABUSIVE’ TRUMP SUBPOENAS TARGETING REPORTERS’ SOURCES

Now Chen, who was investigated by federal authorities but never charged with a crime, is pursuing a lawsuit against the federal government, alleging that officials improperly disclosed her private records to Herridge in violation of the Privacy Act. She has sought to compel Herridge to identify her sources as part of that litigation.

The dispute has reached the Supreme Court, where Herridge's attorneys are asking the justices to reconsider the legal standard used to force journalists to disclose confidential sources in civil cases.

Her legal team argues that the lower courts failed to adequately weigh the broader circumstances of Chen's lawsuit, including the Pentagon's national security findings and whether Chen can ultimately prevail in her claims against the government.

The case also exposes a longstanding disagreement among federal appeals courts over the scope of the reporter's privilege, an issue the Supreme Court has not comprehensively addressed in more than five decades.

Herridge's original investigation, published while she was working at Fox News in 2017, examined Chen's background and her operation of the University of Management and Technology in Arlington, Virginia, which enrolled U.S. military personnel using Defense Department tuition assistance.

The reporting included photographs appearing to show Chen in a Chinese military uniform and examined allegations that she had concealed her previous military service when applying for U.S. immigration benefits.

It also raised concerns about the university's collection of information on American service members, including details about their military training and professional backgrounds. A whistleblower interviewed for the investigation alleged that information stored on the school's computers could be accessed remotely from China.

WASHINGTON POST BOASTS IT STARED DOWN ‘UNWARRANTED’ JUSTICE DEPARTMENT SUBPOENA

Federal authorities had previously investigated Chen over potential immigration violations and counterintelligence concerns, but prosecutors in the Eastern District of Virginia declined to bring charges.

Following Herridge's reporting, the Pentagon completed a review of Chen's university and terminated its eligibility for military tuition assistance funding, according to her filing.

Chen subsequently filed suit against the federal government, alleging that confidential information from government records had been improperly disclosed to Herridge. She contends that identifying the officials responsible for the alleged disclosures is necessary to establish her Privacy Act claims.

Herridge refused to identify her sources, arguing that compelling disclosure would undermine the ability of journalists to obtain sensitive information from government officials and whistleblowers.

A federal judge ultimately ordered Herridge to disclose the sources and held her in civil contempt when she refused. The U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit upheld the order, prompting her appeal to the Supreme Court.

Fox News Media has continued to support Herridge's legal fight, including covering her legal fees, despite her departure from the network in 2019.

At the center of Herridge's petition is a disagreement among federal appeals courts over how judges should evaluate a journalist's claim of privilege when confidential sources are sought in civil litigation.

The filing argues that the D.C. Circuit applied a narrow test focused primarily on whether Chen needed the information to pursue her lawsuit and whether she had exhausted alternative means of obtaining it.

They contend that courts should also consider the strength of the underlying lawsuit and the consequences of compelling disclosure, particularly when confidential national security sources may be involved.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The distinction could prove significant for journalists reporting on sensitive government matters. Under the standard challenged by Herridge, a plaintiff could obtain a reporter's confidential sources even if other deficiencies in the lawsuit would ultimately prevent the plaintiff from recovering damages, according to the petition.

World.title: What will we leave our children? The American Dream demands more than comfort
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

As Americans prepare to vote in the Nov. 3 midterm elections, much of the national conversation centers on which party will control Congress and what the next two years will mean for the country. Those are important questions, but a more consequential one reaches beyond the next election and our own lifetimes: What kind of America are we leaving to our children and grandchildren?

For much of our history, the American Dream was rooted in the conviction that the next generation should inherit greater freedom and opportunity than the one before it. Men and women crossed oceans, endured hardship, established communities and sacrificed their own comfort because they believed their children could enjoy opportunities they might never experience. They understood that the measure of a generation was not simply what it accumulated, but what it preserved for those who followed.

Consider the early settlers who crossed the Atlantic seeking religious freedom. They knew their journey would demand sacrifice, yet they believed the freedom to worship according to conscience was worth securing. Their convictions helped shape the American understanding that faith and conscience belong to the individual, not the government.

ARKANSAS TAKES HOME TOP RANKING FOR RELIGIOUS FREEDOM AFTER GOV SANDERS EXPANDS KEY PROTECTIONS

In his 1802 letter to the Danbury Baptists, President Thomas Jefferson affirmed the constitutional protection of religious conscience against government interference. Religious liberty was never intended to remove faith from public life. It was intended to protect the right of every American to freely exercise their religious beliefs and worship without government subjugation.

Later generations of immigrants came seeking economic opportunity. They worked difficult jobs, built businesses and raised families hoping their children might achieve more than they had. Their circumstances differed from those of the early settlers, but they shared a fundamental understanding of the American Dream: sacrificing something in the present to secure something greater for the future.

SEN TIM SCOTT: MY FAMILY'S JOURNEY SHOWS AMERICA'S FOUNDING PROMISE IS ALIVE AND STRONG

Somewhere along the way, we began losing that generational perspective. The American Dream increasingly became a question of what we could acquire and enjoy during our lifetimes rather than what we could build for those who followed. We became more concerned with protecting our immediate comfort than confronting the difficult decisions necessary to preserve our children's future.

Our national finances illustrate that shift. The federal government continues operating with enormous annual deficits, adding to a national debt future generations will inherit. Reasonable people disagree over spending priorities, taxation and government's proper role. Yet every American should consider whether we are willing to make difficult decisions today or are content to pass their consequences to children who have no voice in making them.

AMERICA’S DEBT CRISIS THREATENS OUR CHILDREN’S FUTURE. WE THE PEOPLE NEED TO FIX IT

This is ultimately a question of stewardship that extends far beyond government spending. A free society cannot survive indefinitely on previous generations' sacrifices while refusing to make sacrifices of its own. Religious liberty, economic opportunity, strong families and healthy communities require more than appreciation for what we inherited. They require the conviction to preserve those blessings for people we may never meet.

Christians should understand this responsibility. Scripture calls believers to care for others and pass the knowledge of God from one generation to the next. In John 13:34, Jesus commands His disciples to love one another as He has loved them. That love is demonstrated through what we are willing to give of ourselves for others.

AMERICA’S NEXT 250 YEARS DEPEND ON PASSING FAITH AND FREEDOM TO OUR CHILDREN

Yet I wonder whether we have become so accustomed to inherited freedoms that we have forgotten what preserving them requires. Previous generations endured persecution and extraordinary hardship to secure religious liberty. Today, Christians sometimes hesitate to express their convictions because doing so might cost them their reputation, influence or standing within their circles. We should consider what that reveals about our understanding of sacrifice.

Pastors and Christian leaders know the pressure to avoid controversy. Biblical teaching can offend cultural sensibilities, challenge prevailing assumptions or invite criticism. Yet Hebrews 4:12 (KJV) reminds us that "the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword."

SOUTHERN BAPTIST PRESIDENT CALLS ON PASTORS TO 'STEP UP' AHEAD OF MIDTERM ELECTIONS

Scripture was never intended to conform to the prevailing opinions of the culture, but to penetrate the hearts and consciences of those who hear it. The temptation is to soften the message, avoid difficult subjects and preserve comfort through silence. Yet Christian leadership has never been about making faith comfortable. It is about proclaiming biblical truth without compromise, equipping believers to live faithfully and preparing the next generation to understand the convictions entrusted to them.

A free society cannot survive indefinitely on previous generations' sacrifices while refusing to make sacrifices of its own.

The church cannot fulfill that responsibility by retreating from questions shaping American life. Christian communicators, whether standing behind a pulpit, speaking into a microphone or reaching audiences through digital media, must communicate truth with clarity and courage. The platforms may change, but our responsibility to pass on what we have received does not.

EXCLUSIVE: NEW CHURCH CAMPAIGN SAYS AMERICA'S FAMILY CRISIS WON'T BE SOLVED BY POLITICS, BUT BY PASTORS

November's elections will determine who holds political power for a season. They will not determine whether parents teach their children the value of freedom, pastors faithfully proclaim Scripture or Christians sacrifice their comfort for future generations. Those responsibilities cannot be delegated to Washington, nor do they disappear when an election ends.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

The American Dream was never meant to be a purely personal arrangement, a private guarantee that each of us, in our own lifetime, could claim "Life, Liberty, and the pursuit of Happiness" for ourselves alone. It was always a longer promise: a commitment to build and keep a country in which those same freedoms and opportunities would remain available to the generations who follow.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

We enjoy the possibility of that dream because earlier Americans treated it as something worth protecting beyond their own lifetimes. They understood that the real measure of the work was not only what they could enjoy, but what they left standing for those who had not yet arrived. In that sense, the dream was never finished in any single generation; it was entrusted, again and again, to the next.

World.title: People living past 100 in one tiny village share 3 daily habits
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

National Geographic researchers believe they may have discovered a new "blue zone."

A blue zone is a geographic region where residents show unusually high rates of longevity and survival into old age. The newest blue zone candidate is a small village called Bolotana, located on the Italian island of Sardinia.

In a 2024 snapshot, 10 of the village's 2,262 residents were at least 100 years old, according to National Geographic — roughly 10 times the Sardinian average and 11 times the U.S. average.

PEOPLE WHO LIVE TO 100 HAVE 3 DRINKS IN COMMON, LONGEVITY EXPERT SAYS

A team of researchers, including Dan Buettner — founder of Blue Zones, a company focused on longevity, and a National Geographic Fellow — set out to investigate Bolotana’s exceptional lifespan.

The findings were published in Frontiers in Aging.

Buettner highlighted three lifestyle habits that are common among Bolotana’s long-lived residents.

They move throughout the day: Residents walk steep streets to shops, cafés, workplaces and friends’ homes. They eat a largely plant-based diet: Beans, vegetables, wheat, olives and olive oil are traditional staples. They stay socially connected: Residents regularly gather with friends, family and neighbors through meals, church and community activities.

"Here, men are participating more, and that could explain why women are doing better."

The study did not establish that these habits directly cause longevity, but researchers are examining how the village’s environment and traditions may contribute to its unusually high survival rates.

"The international team of demographers, their population scientists … were able to examine the birth records, death records and baptismal records and see that this is probably the richest, most complete data on centenarians in the world," Buettner told Fox News Digital.

AMERICA'S LIFESPAN HAS DOUBLED SINCE 1776 — EXPERTS REVEAL WHAT CHANGED

"For those of us who want to make it into our 90s and 100s in full health, this place does it better than anyplace else in the world."

The strongest longevity advantage appeared among Bolotana’s women, who ranked second only to Hong Kong for life expectancy at age 70 and survival from age 70 to 100.

What sets Bolotana apart

The original Sardinian blue zone was identified in the late 1990s and formally described in research published around 2000. Located in the mountainous region roughly 68 miles from Bolotana, it is known for unusually strong male longevity, according to Buettner.

Although Bolotana remains partly pastoral, it is also an agricultural community. Buettner suggested that this may mean men spend more time at home helping with household responsibilities, potentially reducing the burden on women.

"In the original blue zone in the highlands, the [women] worried about the finances and raising children and the leaky roof," he said. "They're all alone. Here, men are participating more, and that could explain why women are doing better, because they're only bearing half the stress load instead of almost all of it."

Buettner believes the village’s strong social connections may be one factor behind the women’s longevity, although the study did not establish a cause.

GEORGIA WOMAN CELEBRATES 112TH BIRTHDAY, REVEALS HER SECRET TO A LONG LIFE

"We see women gathering in the library, baking bread together, making sweets together and going to church together," he said. "So, you see a much more socially connected society among the women in Bolotana than in the other blue zones."

As in many parts of Italy, Bolotana has a strong Catholic tradition. Buettner said church attendance may provide residents with faith, social connection and a sense of belonging.

"It’s a sense of community, but it's also people proactively understanding that sitting down with a friend and talking about your troubles and your day with somebody who cares about you is a much more powerful drug than a pharmaceutical," Buettner said.

"The human species has shown this over and over, and Bolotana is a perfect example."

The Bolotana diet

Diet varies among blue zones, but Bolotana’s traditional fare is largely plant-based, with a focus on beans, vegetables, wheat, olives and olive oil, along with some cheese and meat.

DOCTOR'S 10 RULES FOR LIVING LONGER, CELEBRATING MORE BIRTHDAYS AND MAKING EXTRA YEARS COUNT

"About 90% of a centenarian's diet has been all plant-based," Buettner said. "Not protein, by the way. These aren't protein loaders. These are complex carbohydrate loaders."

A Bolotanese breakfast might consist of a piece of bread or cheese with local olives and a cup of coffee. Lunch, the biggest meal of the day that starts in the early afternoon, is "almost always" a minestrone soup made with locally grown seasonal vegetables and lots of beans.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

"Beans are the cornerstone of the longevity diet here," Buettner said. "Garbanzo beans, lentil beans, pinto beans, cannellini beans — these are really the all-star of the diet."

CLICK HERE TO 

Traditionally, residents ate meat about five times per month, usually as a celebratory food.

In the highlands, people traditionally cooked with lard, Buettner said, while Bolotana residents use olive oil from ancient trees.

Researchers are studying whether the oil’s unusually high levels of odd-chain fatty acids could be relevant to longevity.

‘Not chasing’ longevity

Bolotana residents are not deliberately pursuing longer lives, the longevity researcher noted. The region has little emphasis on gym culture or biohacking.

"These are real humans with an average set of genes," Buettner said. "These aren’t superhumans with superhuman discipline or better genes."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"They’re not chasing longevity," he added. "It is the product of their environment."

Because Bolotana’s streets are steep and residents rarely drive within town, they typically walk to shops, cafés, workplaces and friends’ homes, Buettner said.

"It’s this sort of unconscious walking that’s far more important for longevity than going to the gym."

Buettner said Bolotana is an example of how daily routines and surroundings can encourage movement without requiring residents to schedule formal exercise.

Residents of walkable American communities have a three- to five-year life-expectancy advantage over those in less-walkable areas, he said.

"If we want a healthier America, we have to start thinking about shaping our neighborhoods and our cities so people can unconsciously move and not rely on heaping another obligation on their busy lives to remember to go to the gym," the expert said.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"Most of the things that lead to Bolotana longevity are also pleasant and make the journey a joy," he added.

World.title: NFL's dumbest moment of the week once again welcomes Jets coach Aaron Glenn, who is on the hot seat
World.content:
When it was over, Aaron Glenn was blaming and second-guessing himself after another New York Jets loss. And this has become perhaps too familiar for the team's coach this season.

The Jets lost to the previously winless Miami Dolphins on Sunday, and while that can happen because the other guys get paid, too, the Dolphins had been getting paid without winning before this one.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

In fact, the Dolphins had been getting paid without even leading a game all season.

WINLESS DOLPHINS END HISTORIC DROUGHT AND THEY DID IT AGAINST THE ALMOST-AS-HAPLESS JETS

But against Glenn's team, the Dolphins looked like a playoff contender. That left Glenn disappointed. And defeated.

"When it comes to this game, highly disappointed," Glenn lamented. "Disappointed in myself, first and foremost."

NFL'S DUMBEST MOMENT OF WEEK 2 GOES TO JETS COACH AARON GLENN WHO PLAYED NOT TO LOSE AT END OF REGULATION

Glenn is familiar with losing this season, but when the head coach is blaming himself for his clock management, that familiar spot is problematic. And that's exactly where Glenn was for the second time this season — guilty of the dumbest moment of the week.

That Week 7 moment:

The Dolphins held a 14-7 lead with 8:44 left before halftime, and then they went on the Earth's longest drive.

They marched from their own 9-yard line to the Jets 32-yard line with only two minutes remaining until half. Holding all his timeouts, Glenn stood idly on the sideline like a spectator.

'I LOST US THAT GAME': NICK SIRIANNI MAKES DECISION THAT OPENED DOOR TO A JACKSONVILLE JAGUARS COMEBACK WIN

"Yeah, I think that's one they were already down in the red zone, correct?" Glenn asked reporters who wanted an explanation. "That’s the one you’re talking about?"

Well, the Dolphins weren't in the red zone. They were at the New York 25 with 1:16 to play. But Glenn saved his timeouts for use in the year 2037, when he maybe gets his next head coaching opportunity.

So the clock ticked, and ticked and ticked, and the next time Miami ran a play, there were only 35 left on the clock.

The Dolphins eventually scored again, and the moment passed, but the clock management from the coach was curious.

"Man, we felt like we were going to stop them," Glenn said. "And maybe we should have called our timeouts to get it back, but at that point, we just felt like we were going to stop them and be able to get the ball back.

"That's something that we should have done is use our timeouts."

Yes, correct.

Glenn's explanation actually makes zero sense because if the Jets had done as he thought and held the Dolphins scoreless, using the timeouts would have given the Jets the football back with more time remaining on the clock.

As it was, the Jets got the ball back with six seconds remaining in the first half, which New York used to merely take a knee.

The second half witnessed something of a Jets rally before the Dolphins eventually prevailed 28-25, but that made the failure to a call time out more glaring because the Jets might have used that extra time in the first half to manage a field goal — which eventually was the difference in the game.

The Jets, by the way, are 2-5 and Glenn is in serious trouble. His teams are terrible just before halftime, having been outscored 107-6 in the coach's 24 games.

And owner Woody Johnson has not given Glenn a vote of confidence like he did at this stage in the 2025 season. Johnson declined to speak with reporters at the League Fall Meeting last week.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"We all have to get better, from coaching to playing to everything that we’re doing, we have to get better," Glenn said. "... We know what’s going to happen from the outside in, we accept that, and it is what it is.

"This is a time where our guys, we’ve got to lock arms to make sure that everything that we get as far as energy and connection is going to be built from within, and we understand that.

"But we’ve got to play better, and our fans deserve better than that, and that starts with me."

If Glenn continues to mismanage the clock, a coaching change is going to start with him.

World.title: Alaska Senate candidate Mary Peltola delays campaign events after car crash
World.content:
Former Rep. Mary Peltola is rescheduling several upcoming campaign events after she and her family sustained “minor” injuries in a car crash, her campaign announced Sunday.

“Mary and her family sustained minor injuries but are in good spirits. Unfortunately, per the advice of medical professionals, Mary’s upcoming events in Fairbanks and Bethel will be rescheduled for later in the week as she takes time to recover,” Peltola campaign manager Cheryl Bruce said in a statement.

“Mary is disappointed that the accident is delaying the start of her Alaska Always Tour, and she is eager to get back on the campaign trail to speak directly with Alaskans about her plan to take on the rigged system and lower costs for working families,” Bruce added.

Peltola was en route to the Alaska Federation of Natives’ annual banquet Saturday when a vehicle transporting the candidate and her family was struck by another driver, according to the campaign. A spokesperson for the campaign said they had no reason to believe the accident had been politically motivated.

The police department in Anchorage confirmed Sunday that a collision involving three vehicles occurred on evening and those involved sustained “non-life threatening injuries.”

Police added that the incident is under investigation.

Peltola, a Democrat, is locked in a competitive Senate race against GOP Sen. Dan Sullivan. She was elected to the House in 2022 but narrowly lost her re-election bid in 2024, the same year that President Donald Trump won the state by 13 percentage points.

Sullivan’s re-election race, in which he’s seeking a third term, is tighter than expected, with Alaska voters tying Trump to high gas and grocery prices resulting from the ongoing war with Iran.

Trump and Vice President JD Vance rallied voters in Alaska separately earlier this month.

Republicans have accused Democrats of recruiting another candidate named Dan Sullivan to run for the Senate, saying that voters may be confused by the presence of two Dan Sullivans on the ballot if they plan to vote for the incumbent senator.

Democrats have not taken credit for recruiting the second Dan Sullivan into the race. He’ll appear on the ballot as Dan J. Sullivan, while the incumbent senator will be identified by his name, political party and a clear notation that he’s the incumbent.

Last week, the Justice Department sued Alaska’s election officials, seeking to block certification of the election if Sen. Dan Sullivan loses. It cited Dan J. Sullivan’s presence on the ballot as a point of “voter confusion.”

On Saturday, Democrats filed a motion urging a federal judge to dismiss the case.

World.title: NFL Week 7: A divisional duel in Detroit, and Aaron Rodgers keeps winning
World.content:
Week 7 of the NFL season featured a Super Bowl contender getting back on track and a thrilling divisional showdown in the NFC North, plus another comeback win for one of the NFL’s most surprising teams.

Here’s what you need to know about from Sunday.

The Lions won a wild one at home

What a game between the Detroit Lions and the Green Bay Packers in the late window. The Lions won 20-17 on a walk-off field goal after a drama-filled affair that included controversial calls, plenty of offense and even an offensive lineman running a drag route.

Both quarterbacks were dealing. Detroit’s Jared Goff completed 27 of 45 passes for 274 yards in the win, while Green Bay’s Jordan Love was 22 of 32 for 303 yards. Love could have had an even bigger day, but his receivers had multiple drops in big moments.

The game was also filled with miscues. The Packers missed two field goals, both of which were shorter than 40 yards. Detroit, meanwhile, had two turnovers after not having given the ball away even once since Week 1.

The fourth quarter was especially intense. The Lions went for it on fourth-and-1 from their own 24 but were stuffed on a run.

Green Bay couldn’t take advantage on its ensuing possession, however. After they picked up only 5 yards, the Packers lined up for a 35-yard field goal, but Trey Smack’s kick was deflected.

Detroit’s offense finally finished the job from there, going 71 yards and running out the clock for a game-winning kick by Jake Bates. The Lions improved to 4-2, while the Packers fell to 4-3.

Can the Browns keep getting away with this?

Cleveland improved to 5-2 after a last-minute, 27-24 victory over the Tennessee Titans.

The Browns are not only one of the NFL’s most surprising teams; they are the league’s comeback kings so far this season. Quarterback Deshaun Watson has led a game-winning drive in each of the team’s five wins this year, and those five game-winning drives are the most by any Cleveland quarterback in a single season this century, per ESPN.

The Browns got a breakout game from rookie wide receiver KC Concepcion, who had eight catches for 129 yards. Tight end Harold Fannin Jr. made a huge play late with a 36-yard catch and run to set up a game-winning field goal.

Can Cleveland keep this up? All five of its wins have come by four points or less. The Browns have a negative-13 point differential despite their winning record. Cleveland keeps winning, but the margins are super thin.

J.J. McCarthy gets his first win for the Giants

A week after he threw 243 yards in relief of Jameis Winston, J.J. McCarthy got the start for New York and led the Giants to a 27-21 win over the Houston Texans in overtime.

McCarthy played a clean game, completing 20 of 28 passes for 252 yards. He improved to 7-4 in his career as a starter, and New York is now 4-2-1 — and atop the NFC East. McCarthy got a huge boost from his rushing attack, as Cam Skattebo ran for 124 yards and a score, while former Texan Devin Singletary ran for the winning touchdown in the extra period.

The Rams have a get-right game

It’s been a frustrating season for Los Angeles, which entered Week 7 with a 2-4 record. The Rams’ last three losses came by a combined nine points, a sign the team was closer to the preseason favorite most assumed it would be.

Los Angeles finally lived up to its potential in a 35-21 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. The Rams scored 28 points in the first half alone, thanks in large part to a rushing attack that averaged 5.2 yards per rush en route to 199 yards. Reigning MVP Matthew Stafford was efficient, finishing the game with 195 yards on 23 of 29 passing.

Los Angeles’ next three games are against the Los Angeles Chargers, the Washington Commanders and the Arizona Cardinals — an opportunity for the 3-4 Rams to get back over .500.

Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers keep winning

After quarterback Aaron Rodgers looked every bit his age in a sluggish start to the season, the 42-year-old four-time MVP has led Pittsburgh to a 4-1 record in its last five games. The Steelers squeaked out a 16-10 victory over the New Orleans Saints in Paris in a game played without incident amid protests in France.

Rodgers has completed at least 60% of his passes in each of the last three weeks, all of which were Pittsburgh wins. On Sunday, he even dialed back the clock to pick up a key first down late with his legs, effectively icing the game.

The Steelers are tied with the Browns atop the AFC North, though Cleveland is in first place by virtue of a head-to-head tiebreaker.

An undefeated falls, and a defeated rises

The San Francisco 49ers fell to 6-1 in a 29-20 loss to the Atlanta Falcons. The 49ers entered injury-depleted (particularly at receiver) and then lost running back Christian McCaffrey during the game. Brock Purdy threw two interceptions, but it’s far from panic time in the Bay.

Meanwhile, the Miami Dolphins picked up their first win of the season and the first career win for head coach Jeff Hafley. The Dolphins outlasted the New York Jets 28-25, and it’s possible losing to a previously winless Miami team puts Jets coach Aaron Glenn on a seat too hot to come back from.

World.title: Eric Bauza, voice of Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck and Porky Pig, dies at 46
World.content:
Eric Bauza, best known for voicing the lovable “Looney Tunes” characters Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck and Porky Pig, has died, his family said Monday.

He was 46.

Bauza’s family issued a brief statement on his official Instagram page stating that he had “passed away suddenly,” without giving further details.

The Emmy Award-winning voice actor was the “modern voice of iconic “Looney Tunes” characters Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, along with dozens of other beloved cartoon characters,” the statement said.

Bauza died Sunday at his residence, according to the Los Angeles County medical examiner’s office, which noted that he had been diagnosed with hypertensive cardiovascular disease.

“Eric was a unique and versatile voice actor who was loved by everyone he knew and worked with,” his manager, Judy Coppage, told NBC News by email.

“His sudden passing is a shock to all of us, and he will be deeply missed. It’s a profound loss for his family, the animation industry and his fans,” Coppage added. “The pleasure of watching him succeed and excel to become one of the most accomplished voices in animation was rewarding and thrilling.”

Bauza was the voice actor for Daffy Duck's character in "The Day the Earth Blew Up: A Looney Tunes Movie". Capital Pictures / Alamy

The Canadian-American won three Emmy awards between 2022 and 2025 for his work, including voicing characters such as Elmer Fudd, Marvin the Martian and Tweety.

He was also the first person of color to voice Bugs Bunny in the “Looney Tunes” cartoons, which he told NBC News in a 2021 interview led to a deluge of encouragement and adoration from the Asian American community.

“Looney Tunes transcends all languages and all cultures,” he said at the time. “It doesn’t matter what part of the planet you’re from. You get the comedy.”

Bauza said he grew up a massive ”Looney Tunes” fan, noting that the classic cartoons were part of the bond between his Filipino immigrant father and grandfather. He also said his obsessive attention to detail and persistence formed the foundation of his craft, as he grew up mimicking cartoon voices.

Bauza voiced the character Wile E. Coyote in the 2026 film "Coyote vs. Acme". Ketchup Entertainment

Bauza also voiced some of the biggest animated characters in the 2021 movie “Space Jam: A New Legacy” and appeared in the 2023 “Super Mario Bros. Movie” and, most recently, the 2026 “Coyote vs. Acme” film.

He also lent his voice to characters including Stimpy Cat in “Ren & Stimpy,” Foop from “The Fairly OddParents,” Fozzie Bear from “Muppet Babies” and the Beagle Boys from “DuckTales,” according to his IMDb page.
