World.title: Waiting list for specialized care may outlast those needing it
World.content:
Specialized care funding in Estonia is so lacking that around 2,000 people in need of assistance are waiting for services.

One such person is Alex, a young man with a profound disability who needs round-the-clock care.

Alex, 19, was born extremely prematurely, suffering severe brain damage as a result, "Aktuaalne kaamera" reported. Alex needs assistance with everyday activities including eating and getting dressed.

Alex's mother, Merje Liiv, said she cannot even get to do household chores while looking after Alex as he needs her by his side constantly. "He has epileptic seizures, he gets tired of being in one position, and I have to monitor him all the time," Liiv said, adding she needs to be present not only physically but also mentally.

"I am his link to the world, I am his eyes and hands," she went on. Liiv also provides her son with emotional experiences. "Alex is very grateful that he hasn't been left somewhere in the dark, and that people engage with him, and he enjoys that," she continued.

The family had assumed that once Alex finished school, he would enter specialized care. Specialized care services are primarily intended for people with severe mental disorders or intellectual disabilities who cannot get the assistance they need via other social welfare measures and channels. However, it turned out that Alex's case was too severe and he was not eligible for the service.

"Obviously, our sense of security disappeared immediately as we had been counting on it," Liiv noted. She added that being denied the service came as painful for the family. What hurt most, however, was the realization that for as long as Alex was of compulsory school age, the law required the state to acknowledge his existence. Once compulsory schooling ended, he was essentially written off by the state, however.

"For them, Alex was a client who was too complicated, but not so complicated that he should be left entirely in his family's care. That was what hurt," Liiv recounted.

Merje Liiv with Alex. Source: ERR

Her local municipality then assigned Alex a personal assistant who visits him on weekdays. More broadly, however, there is a growing problem of people not fitting into predefined categories and being left without the support they need.

The problems facing specialized care can be summed up as chronic underfunding. This has led to a situation in which more than 2,000 people in need of assistance are waiting for services.

Ragnar Vaiknemets, board chair of social services organization AS Hoolekandeteenused, said if someone puts a child or other family member on the waiting list for specialized care nowadays, that person may not even get a place within their lifetime.

"As harsh as it sounds, there is currently no regular triaging of the waiting list, as there is in healthcare," he explained.

Vaiknemets noted that people's need for assistance is not reassessed regularly. He said there are clearly too few places, particularly for certain services, such as those intended for people with autism or multiple disabilities. These are cases in which people require the service throughout their lives.

Currently, priority on the waiting list for specialized care services is determined primarily by when a person was added to the list, rather than how urgently they need assistance. The Riigikogu's Social Affairs Committee is working on a bill which would require waiting lists to take into account a person's actual need for the service, rather than simply the date they joined the list.

In spring this year, the Supreme Court issued a landmark ruling stating that if a person needs a place in a specialized care home, the state must provide it. People in need of assistance cannot be placed on an indefinite waiting list on the grounds of insufficient funding or a shortage of places.

While the 2027 state budget bill has passed its first reading, funding for specialized care within the bill and over the wider picture remains disputed. €200 million is needed over four years, yet only €37 million in additional funding has been allocated to the entire social affairs and healthcare sector. Also, it is not yet known how much of that €37 million is intended for specialized care.

Opposition Social Democrat MP Riina Sikkut noted there should not be a situation where people in need of assistance get asked why they did not lose their mobility in the first half of the year, when funding was still available, rather than at the end of the year, by which time the funding has run out.

Riina Sikkut. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

"Wait until the new year for your crutches, wheelchair, orthosis or whatever other aid you need," she said, noting that this is exactly what is now happening with regard to specialized care.

Sikkut said a fixed amount of money is allocated in the budget, and services are provided only to the extent that this funding allows.

"If more people need assistance, or the need for assistance is greater than what we can provide with the money allocated in the budget, then we tell them to wait in line," she said.

According to Sikkut, a former health minister, the solution is not to wait a year or two or ask people in need to find some other arrangement. "In reality, there is no other solution," she said, adding that people in need of assistance require services specifically suited to their needs.

The government in the 2027 state budget bill set aside €7.4 million in a reserve for the social affairs sector. This is intended for negotiations with the opposition to secure parliamentary support for the minority government's budget.

"I have never seen anything like this in my life, where state budget problems are resolved via an unallocated reserve left for the Riigikogu to decide on," Sikkut noted.

Even an MP from the coalition Reform Party was critical of the situation. Signe Riisalo (Reform), chair of the Social Affairs Committee, said that if she were a minister, she would have included such an important issue in the state budget so that the Riigikogu could decide on it in the same way as the rest of the budget.

"I would not have left it unresolved," she added.

Specialized care funding protest on Toompea Hill. Source: Siim Lõvi / ERR

Riisalo, a former social security minister, noted that allocating at least the existing €7.4 million from the state budget for next year, followed by the same amount in subsequent years, bringing the total to €37 million over four years, would make it viable to create some new places. She added that it would also allow for a modest pay increase, as staffing is another major concern.

Vaiknemets said that if the social affairs sector as a whole does not receive the funding it needs, the problem will eventually return back to the state.

"It will come back to the state in the sense that people will start knocking on more doors: calling ambulances and the police, visiting healthcare providers and local municipalities, trying to get help somewhere," Vaiknemets explained.

He added that people who cannot access services or receive assistance do not simply go away.

Vaiknemets said the need remains and is if anything likely to become even greater. According to him, the state will end up using very expensive resources to pay for problems that could have been prevented.

"As the saying goes, we'll end up using a laptop to hammer nails into the wall," Vaiknemets concluded.

World.title: Estonian musicians refuse to perform alongside Chinese orchestra with Russia links
World.content:
The Estonian Festival Orchestra canceled a concert last week in China after it was revealed that the local symphony orchestra had close ties to Russia.

The Estonian Festival Orchestra, conducted by Paavo Järvi, is on tour in China and was scheduled to perform at Wuxi Symphony Hall, in eastern China, with the local orchestra on October 23.

The Wuxi orchestra toured Russia last year as part of an official China-Russia Years of Culture event and has performed with the Russian National Orchestra.

After learning about their partner's background, the Estonian musicians refused to take part in the joint concert.

The cancellation could cost the Estonian Festival Orchestra hundreds of thousands of euros, although the exact amount is not yet known.

According to the Estonian musicians, going ahead with the concert would have conflicted with their principles and caused irreparable reputational damage.

World.title: Longtime Center Party MP joins Isamaa
World.content:
Longtime Center Party member and former television and radio journalist Enn Eesmaa has said he will join the opposition Isamaa Party and will run in the Riigikogu elections next March.

Eesmaa was a member of the Center Party for over 20 years, from 2003 to 2024.

"Throughout my career, whether in journalism or politics, I have been a team player. Isamaa's team is strong and capable in the economy, culture, national defense and other areas, and I am pleased to be able to contribute to its work," Eesmaa said in a press release issued by Isamaa.

"In the upcoming elections, together with [Isamaa Chairman] Urmas [Reinsalu] and others, we will stand for ensuring that Estonia is protected, that our voice is heard loud and clear on the international stage, and that the Estonian language and culture are preserved and respected in our country," he said.

Reinsalu welcomed Eesmaa's decision to join Isamaa.

"I have worked with Enn in various capacities over the years. Most recently, when I was foreign minister, Enn was deputy chairman of the Foreign Affairs Committee. Enn is a very balanced and principled person, and I am pleased that he has decided to run for the Riigikogu on Isamaa's list," Reinsalu said.

In recent months, several MPs have changed parties as the election draws closer and the active phase of campaigning starts.

World.title: Tallink cancels MyStar trips on Monday due to a malfunction
World.content:
Ferry operator Tallink has canceled the passenger ferry MyStar's scheduled sailings on the Tallinn-Helsinki route on Monday due to a technical fault.

MyStar, which departed Tallinn at 7:30 a.m., was unable to continue its journey and had to return to the Port of Tallinn due to a technical fault, Tallink's Communications Manager Meelis Kompus said on Monday morning.

Kompus said the fault was discovered in the engine room, but it is not yet possible to say exactly what caused it or how long repairs will take.

Passengers have been informed, and freight customers will receive further information during the day.

Megastar and Victoria I ferries are running as normal on the Tallinn-Helsinki route.

World.title: Shale oil to replace gas for winter heating, but bills still may not fall
World.content:
Heat producers may turn to shale oil in severe winter cold if gas is scarce or too expensive, but the cheaper fuel may not mean major savings for household consumers.

The Environmental Board has granted temporary exemptions to two heat producers — Enefit Power in Narva and Utilitas in Tallinn — allowing them to replace natural gas with shale oil from November 1 this year to April 30, 2027. Shale oil is cheaper, but consumers will also bear the costs of procurement, transportation and handling.

Winter district heating prices are forecast to stay high, with natural gas prices elevated on the global market and other fuels such as wood chips also having risen in price.

Estonia wants to keep its oil-shale sector alive, but the EU's emissions trading rules are set to cut free allowances and hike the cost of polluting.

Narva was last heated with shale oil four years ago, when gas prices were extremely high. Enefit Power was then allowed to use it for the whole heating season. Producers want to ensure continuity of district heating and reduce the risk of gas supply disruption. Shale oil is cheaper than gas but causes more air pollution, and the permit does not necessarily mean it will be burned. The board is attaching conditions because the exemptions must be precisely regulated.

Enefit may burn 23,000 tons of shale oil over the winter; Utilitas 20,000 tons. Erik Kosenkranius, the board's deputy director general for environmental use, said the board assesses the technology while the Ministry of Climate assesses the gas market. Producers must monitor quantities and operating hours, notify the board when they start and stop, and carry out additional checks and sampling. "We want to know very precisely how emissions change," he said. "They must comply with existing limit values for air quality outside the production site."

In October the Competition Authority approved maximum district heating prices of €84/MWh in Tallinn and €137.69/MWh in Narva. Shale oil could reduce prices, but compliance costs, production, procurement, transport, handling and environmental charges could cancel the savings. Enefit board chairman Raine Pajo said the cogeneration plant offers cheaper heat — "€74/MWh plus VAT" — and would be used when prices are higher, reducing oil volumes. "When prices are low, the unit cannot be started, cogeneration is not possible and we cannot use oil shale and wood chips. In that case, there must be a backup plan that provides consumers with heat at a reasonable price."

Utilitas board chairman Robert Kitt said gas prices have doubled in a year, creating both price risk and supply risk. "The permit is very recent, and we are still clarifying the details with the Environmental Board, including what quantities must be nominated in advance," he said. "We will use it as little as possible, but as much as necessary." Shale oil and gas cannot be burned together, and three of Utilitas's four Mustamäe boilers are covered by the permit, two of which may not run simultaneously.

VKG has proposed a permanent right to switch to shale oil when gas is expensive. Technical director Raivo Attikas said it is strange that domestic fuel is available but producers must apply for a permit each time prices rise. "Currently, we sell five percent of our oil on the domestic market, while 95 percent is exported, where it is used mainly as marine fuel," he said. "Because our shale oil has a low sulfur content, it is a highly valued product."

Prices of almost all heating types are rising this winter. Natural gas has more than doubled in a year, wood chips are dearer, and costs at the Iru power station just outside Tallinn are up. Utilitas is pinning hopes on a Paljassaare heat pump plant and shale oil to curb further increases.

District heating involves hot water piped in to apartment blocks in larger settlements, for heating purposes only. Heating season is taken to run October to March inclusive.

World.title: Houthis attack Saudi Arabia before high-stakes talks in Tehran
World.content:
Riyadh – Yemen’s Houthis have kept up their attacks on Saudi Arabia as senior officials from the kingdom, Turkey and Pakistan are due to hold high-stakes talks with Iran in Tehran on Monday, following warnings of a return to war.

Fresh explosions rattled Riyadh overnight, along with a text message warning to residents, after the Iran-allied Houthis claimed a new attack on the Saudi capital’s international airport on Sunday.

Saudi Arabia, the world’s top oil exporter, has become deeply embroiled in the eight-month war since hostilities in its long-running conflict with the Iran-allied Houthis resumed in July.

Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman is among the delegations travelling to Tehran, made up of officials from the three countries that signed a defence alliance in Mecca in August.

Their visit follows warnings by the United States, Iran and Israel that hostilities could resume.

Tensions have increased ahead of Israel’s pivotal election on Tuesday and next week’s US mid-terms, where US President Donald Trump’s Republicans are battling to keep control of both chambers of the US Congress.

Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei will take part in Monday’s meeting with Prince Khalid, Pakistani army chief General Asim Munir and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin, the deputy secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, Ali Bagheri Kani, told state TV.

“This historic meeting in Tehran may be the last chance before escalation spirals out of control, an attempt to impose a path of de-escalation before it’s too late,” Hesham Alghannam, a Saudi security analyst and researcher, posted on X.

“The presence of military and security figures at this level together means that the remaining time is extremely limited.”

– ‘Serious tensions’ –

On Sunday, as blasts rang out over Riyadh and authorities sent texts warning residents of a “hostile aerial threat”, the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said it struck missile launchers and storage facilities in Yemen.

The Houthis said they had attacked Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport once again. The repeatedly targeted facility has been largely closed since 13 people were killed and more than 300 wounded in a major attack this month.

Mediation efforts between the US and Iran have been led by Qatar and Pakistan. A Qatari delegation visited Tehran on Sunday, Iran’s foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said.

“Our region is in the grip of serious tensions, and neighbouring countries are striving to convey a message and put forward initiatives,” Baqaei said on Monday.

Andreas Krieg of London-based risk consultancy MENA analytica said Prince Khalid’s presence in Tehran was “hugely significant”, calling him the “strategic mastermind of Saudi Arabia”.

Prince Khalid, brother of Saudi de facto ruler Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, has emerged as one of Saudi Arabia’s key diplomatic interlocutors, dispatched on sensitive regional missions.

“For him to go to Iran directly in this very sensitive time is a very, very strong signal that the kingdom is not just… sitting and waiting for things, events to unfold,” Krieg told AFP.

“There’s a clear effort by the Mecca alliance to signal to Iran that they’re ready to work together to defend the kingdom and defend the kingdom’s borders,” he added.

“And so should Iran think to escalate, which they will likely do if Israel and the US strikes, and they will most likely strike Saudi Arabia, Iran will have to bear the consequences.”

– ‘Don’t test us’ –

Comments by senior officials have raised speculation about renewed hostilities.

Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Sunday “there has been talk of a new war” but that Tehran’s policies remain unchanged.

Trump said on Friday that Washington “may do another little Epic Fury”, referring to the US-Israeli campaign against Iran that began on February 28.

On Sunday, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu warned that Iran may try to disrupt the Israeli elections, where he is in a close-fought race to stay in power.

“We have intelligence signs that our enemies, Iran and its proxies, could challenge us with attacks in order to disrupt the elections,” Netanyahu said.

“Don’t test us. You will suffer disproportionate blows,” added Netanyahu, who has campaigned heavily on his security credentials.

The remarks came as Israel’s Channel 12, citing unnamed sources, reported a confrontation between Netanyahu and army chief Eyal Zamir over an unspecified new directive in the war with Iran, which the premier denied.

World.title: France’s Macron to visit Marseille after protest violence
World.content:
Marseille – The French government sought to draw a line Monday under weeks of protests that have been marred by violence, with President Emmanuel Macron headed to Marseille and the prime minister to meet with students demanding better school conditions.

France has been rocked by widespread anger over the rising cost of living, with nationwide demonstrations on October 17 degenerating into some of the country’s worst rioting in years.

The demonstrations have come at a critical moment for France, six months ahead of a presidential election to replace centrist Macron.

The frontrunner — far-right leader Marine le Pen — held an election rally in Orleans Sunday, a day after yet more demonstrations also saw some violent clashes on the sidelines.

She vowed to “restore the rule of law” if elected next year. Polls show the protests and ensuing disorder have boosted her support, as the government and Macron faced sharp criticism over the unrest.

Authorities have admitted to security and intelligence failures that paved the way for the clashes, large-scale looting and vandalism of public property that erupted on October 17, and had stepped up security for Saturday’s protests.

While Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said the outcome of Saturday’s rallies was more “positive” than a week ago, street violence still erupted in the French capital and a number of other cities including Marseille.

The Elysee said Macron would visit the city hall in Marseille, France’s second-largest city, on Monday, after it was damaged in the protest violence on October 17.

He was also due to meet shopkeepers who had fallen victim to looting and vandalism, the Elysee said.

“He will also pay tribute to and thank the internal security forces that helped restore republican order,” the presidency said.

After this weekend’s protests, many shopfronts in the city centre were still boarded up early Monday, just hours before Macron’s arrival.

Macron’s visit was intended to demonstrate that “the state is present, standing firm and fulfilling its mission to protect,” an aide said.

– ‘High level of violence’ –

A total of 1,435 people were arrested on the sidelines of the most recent weekend protests, Nunez said on Monday.

“The day was brought under control and there were no serious incidents,” he told broadcaster BFMTV.

“Nevertheless, we saw a very high level of violence directed at the internal security forces,” Nunez added.

He said that 267 police officers and gendarmes were injured, along with 150 protesters, including three who were seriously hurt in Toulouse, Reims and Clermont-Ferrand.

The unrest followed weeks of demonstrations by students campaigning for better learning conditions.

Several teenage protesters have been seriously injured and thousands arrested.

The police response to their demonstrations, which included blockades of schools, has been criticised as heavy-handed and sparked a broader movement against the cost of living and police violence.

In Paris on Monday, Lecornu was to meet student leaders, with National Education Minister Edouard Geffray and Higher Education Minister Philippe Baptiste joining him for the talks. Following that meeting, Geffray and Baptiste will hold a news conference.

Macron already met representatives of secondary school pupils last Friday, but they emerged from the talks urging students to keep protesting until the government put forward concrete proposals to address their demands.

On top of the protests, the country was last week shaken by a shooting that killed one person and wounded five, including a 12-year-old girl, outside Paris.

Macron has branded the shooting a “racist terrorist attack”, as most of the victims were from foreign backgrounds.

World.title: Russia says open to mini Ukraine ceasefires, but no let up in war
World.content:
Moscow – Russia said Monday that it would not slow down its offensive on Ukraine despite upcoming US-brokered talks on ending the conflict but that it could agree local “humanitarian” ceasefires.

The Kremlin said that it was open to short-term “humanitarian” ceasefires along the front line, ahead of a truce in the ravaged Russian-occupied city of Oleshky.

A ceasefire is to start in the southern Ukrainian city early Tuesday, brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump after months of reports that residents faced dire food, water and medicine shortages.

Asked whether Russia would consider more local truces, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters: “For humanitarian purposes, absolutely.”

But Moscow vowed not to let up in the overall pace of the war, even as the sides prepare to restart stalled talks under US mediation next month.

“The decision to resume trilateral talks does not imply any restrictions on combat operations,” Peskov said.

“Our armed forces continue to carry out massive strikes on Ukraine’s military-industrial complex,” he added.

Russia has intensified drone and missile attacks on Ukraine in recent weeks, hitting energy sites around major cities in what Kyiv says is a bid to plunge the country into cold and darkness throughout the winter.

Strikes last year left millions without heating or electricity with temperatures as low as -20C.

The two sides are to meet next month with US envoys to discuss ways to end Europe’s worst conflict since World War II.

Several previous rounds have failed to move the sides closer to a deal. Russia demands more territory in eastern Ukraine and sweeping military and political restrictions on Kyiv.

Ukraine and its allies say the demands are tantamount to a capitulation that would leave the country exposed to a future Russian attack.

World.title: Anthropic’s AI model accessed US voter data: Axios
World.content:
Washington – Anthropic’s Claude AI model bypassed a paywall and accessed publicly available voter data in the US state of Georgia without human authorization, Axios reported on Sunday.

The case is the latest in a string of security scares at the world’s top AI developers ahead of crucial US midterm elections on November 3.

Claude accessed aggregate voter counts in Georgia, where more than one million voters have already cast early ballots, Axios reported, citing an Anthropic spokesperson.

According to the spokesperson, the model, which was being trained as part of an internal statistics project, accessed the information behind a paywall by bypassing the system “without being asked to.”

It did not access the state’s voter registration system or change or download any voting records, the spokesperson said, adding that the company has since taken measures to prevent these kinds of actions.

The disclosure adds to mounting unease over how well leading labs can control increasingly autonomous systems.

In July, a group of OpenAI agents broke out of their test environments and launched a cyberattack on AI firm Hugging Face, causing international alarm. Other companies have since reported similar incidents.

The incidents have fueled calls in the United States and abroad for tighter oversight of AI development.

American tech executives signed in September what President Donald Trump described as a “morally binding” commitment to build adequate safeguards around AI models.

World.title: Iraq prepares to receive advanced air defense systems and long-range radars
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is preparing to receive advanced air defense systems, long-range surveillance radars, and anti-missile and counter-drone batteries to bolster its defense capabilities and protect sovereign airspace and critical infrastructure, announced Major General Sabah Al-Numan, spokesperson for the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces.

Speaking to the official gazette, Al-Numan stated that deploying the incoming systems marks a strategic shift in building Iraq’s sovereign military capabilities, equipping the armed forces to enforce airspace integrity and intercept aerial breaches and external threats.

He emphasized that the initiative aims to safeguard vital economic and oil infrastructure, enhance operational self-reliance, reduce dependence on external security guarantees, and prevent Iraqi airspace from being used as a battleground in regional conflicts.

Meanwhile, Khalid Sido, a member of the Parliamentary Security and Defense Committee, stressed the need to review budgetary allocations for the Ministry of Defense to reflect modern warfare realities.

Sido noted that upgrading national air defense networks requires dedicated legislative scrutiny, warning that current spending allocations remain insufficient to meet the technical demands of acquiring advanced counter-drone systems and ballistic missile interceptors.

World.title: US dollar edges down to 167,000 range across major Iraqi exchanges
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar posted a modest decline across parallel market counters on Monday, October 26, 2026, pulling wholesale and retail rates toward the 167,000 dinar range across major commercial hubs after touching near 170,000 dinars per $100 last week.

The downward trajectory follows recent statements delivered on Friday, October 23, by Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi, who stated that Washington will dispatch $1 billion in physical cash consignments to Iraq and assured the public that parallel market rates are slated to drop toward 155,000 dinars per $100 in the coming period.

According to market rate data, cash counters in Baghdad registered retail selling prices at 168,500 dinars against buying bids of 167,500 dinars per $100.

In Erbil, trading bureaus posted selling rates at 168,000 dinars alongside purchase offers of 167,850 dinars.

Across the southern commercial center of Basra, foreign exchange desks listed selling prices at 168,000 dinars and purchase bids at 167,500 dinars per $100.

Despite the recent downward movement, street rates retain a significant spread above the Central Bank of Iraq’s official statutory cash peg, which remains set at 152,000 dinars per $100 (1,520 dinars per dollar), reflecting persistent parallel cash demand beyond the official electronic trade financing platform.

World.title: Iraq U-15 cruises past Saint Kitts 5–0 ahead of decisive Egypt clash
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s U-15 national football team extended their commanding run at the inaugural FIFA U-15 World Cup & Festival 2026 in Baku, Azerbaijan, securing an emphatic 5–0 victory over Saint Kitts and Nevis on Monday morning.

The young Lions of Mesopotamia established control from kickoff, entering the halftime break with a commanding 4–0 advantage courtesy of strikes from Sajjad Fayez, Ayman Hameed, Mohammed Qassim, and Mahdi Saleh. Karrar Meethaq added a fifth goal in the second half to seal an emphatic win.

The result marks the fourth consecutive victory for head coach Safwan Abdul-Ghani’s squad in Baku, following previous group-stage triumphs against the Cayman Islands, Trinidad and Tobago, and Macau.

Iraq now prepares for a decisive group showdown later today, Monday, October 26, 2026, against Egypt at 2:45 PM. The encounter will determine the winner of Group S and award direct qualification to Tier A (Level A) for the tournament knockout rounds.

World.title: Jetour and Harlem Group sign deal to build auto plant in Zakho
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Chinese automotive manufacturer Jetour, in partnership with Harlem Group, signed a contract on Sunday, October 25, 2026, to establish the first and largest local automobile assembly and manufacturing plant in the northern region of Iraq.

The facility will be constructed across an area exceeding 1,000 dunams (approx. 250 hectares) in the Zakho Autonomous Administration.

The official signing ceremony took place in Zakho in the presence of Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) Prime Minister Masrour Barzani, Chairman of the Kurdistan Board of Investment Mohammed Shukri, Supervisor of the Zakho Autonomous Administration Guhdar Shekho, and Chinese Consul General Zhang Jianxin, according to a corporate statement issued by Jetour Iraq.

The investment agreement was signed by Alan Noor, board member of Harlem Group, and Jin Kai, Middle East Regional Director for Jetour International. The initiative aims to shift operations from domestic retail distribution to local vehicle manufacturing under global standards.

The project is designed to advance advanced automotive engineering transfer, generate localized manufacturing jobs, and foster technical industrial expertise under the banner “Made in Iraq, Kurdistan.”

World.title: Congress to hold ‘Vote Bachao' rally at Ramlila Maidan on Nov 1; Amit Shah to lead padayatra in T'gana on Nov 2
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Congress will hold a

âVote Bachao, Desh Bachaoâ

mega rally at Ramlila Maidan in New Delhi on November 1, party president Mallikarjun Kharge said on Monday. The protest comes over the alleged vote theft, demanding the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and an immediate halt of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).

Meanwhile, Union home minister Amit Shah is also set to attend a BJP foot march in Telangana a day later, on November 2, to counter what the party calls the Congress's âfalse narrativeâ against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

Telangana BJP president N Ramchander Rao announced Shah's participation in the November 2

âLoktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hataoâ (save democracy, remove anarchy)

padayatra on Monday.

The announcement comes amid a political row over the SIR exercise, with the Congress accusing the Election Commission of large-scale electoral irregularities.

âThey (Congress) are trying to create anarchy in the state and country. That's why we are going to organise a padayatra with the theme

'Loktantra Bachao - Arajakta Hatao' (save democracy - remove anarchy)

. Amit Shah ji will attend the padayatra on 2nd (of November),â news agency PTI reported, quoting Rao.





Kharge announces mega rally at Ramleela Maidan

Kharge announced the November 1 rally in a video shared on X, alleging that the constitutional right to vote of millions of Indians was under threat.

âThe constitutional right of the Indian people to cast their votes is under threat. CEC Gyanesh Kumar is solely responsible for this; he has acted entirely at the behest of the Prime Minister and the Home Minister,â Kharge said.

Kharge also criticised the government over inflation.

In his video address, he said, âGreetings, friends. It is the festive season, yet you are currently grappling with back-breaking inflation. The government, however, is completely unconcernedâall they know how to do is steal votes. Large-scale vote theft has taken place, and it continues even now.â

Announcing the rally, he said, âIn this regard, a 'Save the Vote, Save the Nation' (Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao) mega-rally will be held on November 1st at the historic Ramlila Maidan in New Delhi.â

âI appeal to you to participate actively in this rally to protect our Constitution and democracy, and to help make this campaign a success. Long live the Constitution! Jai Hind!â he added.

BJP challenges Congress over SIR claims

Rao accused the Congress of spreading misinformation about the electoral roll revision and challenged Telangana chief minister A Revanth Reddy to identify voters whose names had been wrongly deleted.

Observing that Congress was spreading lies over the SIR exercise, Rao said he was ready to visit the chief minister's native village, Kondareddypalle, to check how many voters' names had been removed from the rolls.

He said genuine voters whose names were deleted had the option of getting them included again. Rao also asked Congress ministers in Telangana to identify at least 10 voters whose names had been deleted and explain the reasons for their removal.

Responding to allegations that 13 crore voters had been removed during the SIR exercise, Rao claimed that they fell into the categories of 'Absent, Shifted, Dead and Duplicate' (ASDD).

Of these, he claimed, 2.8 crore were dead, three crore were absent or untraceable when booth-level officers visited them, 6.3 crore had permanently shifted and nearly one crore names were registered at multiple locations. He cited the example of a man in Hyderabad who had admitted to having voter registrations at three places.

Rao targets Kharge, Congress over rally

Rao also criticised Kharge over his remarks against Prime Minister Narendra Modi, alleging that Congress was unable to accept that a 'chaiwala' had become the country's Prime Minister.

He said the party was desperate to return to power after losing elections since 2014.

The Telangana BJP president asked party workers to burn Congress effigies at district headquarters on Monday in protest against Kharge's remarks.

He also took exception to Congress leaders from Telangana travelling to Delhi for the November 1 rally, citing water shortages in the state. Rao claimed that more than 300 of Telangana's over 600 mandals were facing drought-like conditions due to a rainfall deficit.

Pointing to the impact of El Nino on water availability in Hyderabad, he said around 8,000 water tankers were being booked daily in the city. He urged Revanth Reddy to focus on addressing the water crisis instead.

On the chief minister's recent pitch for Rahul Gandhi to become Prime Minister, Rao said the BJP's graph had risen since Gandhi began occupying leadership positions in the Congress.

Taking a swipe at the Congress leader, Rao said, "you cannot market a failed product".

World.title: DMK’s ‘maternal uncle’s gift’ jibe at CM Vijay over women’s safety in Tamil Nadu
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (

NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh chief electoral officer Navdeep Rinwa on Monday responded to allegations of caste bias over an erroneous voter slip, saying that computers and software are not casteist.This comes after AAP Rajya Sabha member Sanjay Singh questioned Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over an erroneous entry in a voter slip where "Ramhit Yadav" became "Ram ne Yadav ko Maara".In a post on X in Hindi, Singh said, "Gyanesh Kumar ji, why did Ram hit only a Yadav? Why did Ram not hit any Singh, Pathak, Asthana, Sharma, Rai or Bisht? Is your computer casteist? Are you running the agenda of any political party?"In a sarcastic reply to Singh, Rinwa said that had the entry read Ram hit a minority (alpasankhyak), the authorities would have been accused of communalism too."A strange name, 'Ram ne Sharma ko Maara', is also present in the voter list of the recent legislative council elections. Computers/software are not casteist," the UP CEO said."We accept that an error was made, but fortunately, even while making the error, no caste discrimination took place. Thank God that Ram did not hit a minority. Otherwise, besides being accused of casteism, we would have also faced allegations of communalism," he added.The CEO's office also shared a voter slip from the recently held graduate constituency legislative council elections. The slip listed the voter's name as Ravi Sharma, while his father's name appeared as "Ram ne Sharma ko Maara".The exchange comes days after instances of erroneous entries in electoral records were flagged, raising questions over the computer software used to prepare voter lists.Later, Rinwa, in a post on X, said some "bizarre-looking names" had appeared in the voter list during the recently held legislative council elections."The reasons behind such mistakes are being looked into and appropriate action is being taken to prevent recurrence," the CEO said.He said "some forged voter slips" had gone viral on social media and were being displayed or circulated by several established media outlets and prominent individuals. "The person responsible for the forgery will be dealt with as per law," Rinwa added.Last week, Rinwa had explained that the software was designed to transliterate names entered in English into Hindi.However, in some cases, instead of transliterating names, it translated the words, resulting in incorrect entries. For instance, if "Ramhit Yadav" was mistakenly typed as "Ram Hit Yadav", the software translated it into Hindi as "Ram ne Yadav ko Maara" (Ram hit Yadav).He said the errors could have been corrected using the editing feature, but some remained in the final list.Another instance, in which "B.Com" was entered in place of the father's name in the electoral roll for the legislative council polls, appeared to be a case of human error or negligence, the CEO had said.Polling for 11 seats in the Uttar Pradesh legislative council was held on October 23, and counting of votes will take place on October 27.

World.title: BJP protests across states over Kharge's 'baap' remark at PM Modi; demands apology
World.content:
NEW DELHI: BJP workers on Monday staged protests in Bihar, Jammu and Bengaluru against Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's controversial 'baap' remark against Prime Minister Narendra Modi, demanding an apology from the Congress chief.

The protests came a day after Kharge, speaking at an event in Patna, responded to a person from the audience who said that PM Modi would not go anywhere. "Modi ka baap bhi jayega (Even Modi's father will have to go)," Kharge said, triggering criticism from BJP leaders.

The remark was made during a programme marking the 139th birth anniversary of Bihar's first chief minister, Shrikrishna Singh.

BJP leaders detained during Bengaluru protest

In Bengaluru, BJP leaders and workers staged a demonstration at Freedom Park, demanding an unconditional apology from Kharge over his remarks.

Police detained several BJP leaders, including Karnataka assembly leader of opposition R Ashoka and former minister CN Ashwath Narayan, during the protest.

BJP leaders accused the Congress president of making offensive remarks against the Prime Minister and his family.

BJP workers burn Kharge's effigy in Patna

In Patna, BJP workers took out a 'Jan Akrosh March' under the leadership of Bihar BJP president Sanjay Saraogi.

The protesters marched from the party headquarters towards Income Tax Golambar, raising slogans against Kharge and the Congress.





They also burnt an effigy of the Congress president.

"Yesterday, all limits were crossed when the platform to celebrate the birth anniversary of Shrikrishna Singh, the architect of modern Bihar, was used to make abusive remarks about the late father of the Prime Minister," Saraogi said.

He accused the Congress of making personal attacks against Modi out of political frustration and demanded an apology from Kharge and Rahul Gandhi.

"The Congress, Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi must apologise to the people of the country," he said.

Protests in Jammu, other districts

In Jammu, BJP leaders and workers staged a protest at Dogra Chowk, raising slogans against Kharge and the Congress. Led by BJP MLA Shagun Parihar and Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha's Jammu and Kashmir president Arun Prabhat, the protesters marched through Dogra Chowk, burnt posters of Kharge and Rahul Gandhi, and staged a brief sit-in on the road.

Parihar condemned the remarks, saying they were disrespectful not only to the Prime Minister's late father but also to elderly people who had passed away.

"If they do not respect the prime minister's father, how will they respect the father of an ordinary citizen?" she asked. Protests were also reported from Samba, Kathua, Poonch, Udhampur, Rajouri, Doda, Kishtwar and Reasi districts. Similar demonstrations were held in Delhi and Lucknow as part of the BJP's nationwide protest against Kharge's remarks.

Congress defends Kharge's remarks

Meanwhile, the Congress defended its president, claiming that a BJP supporter had first insulted Kharge's father during the Patna event. Congress leader Pawan Khera said Kharge was referring to the RSS as PM Modi's "ideological father", rather than his biological father. RJD leader Bhai Virendra also defended Kharge, describing his remarks as a "slip of the tongue" and saying he did not need to apologise.

World.title: Rahi @100: Man of wit, words and verse
World.content:
It is said that a person never truly dies as long as they live on in someoneâs memories. This measure of life and legacy assumes an extraordinary significance in the case of celebrated author, poet and screenwriter

.

Decades after his death, his words continue to draw readers, scholars and admirers into his world. On Saturday, many of them gathered in his native city of Ghazipur as part of a year-long celebration marking his birth centenary.

Milestones of Rahi's journey.

Sharing anecdotes from Razaâs life and times with TOI on the sidelines of the programme, they brought to life the many hues of his persona.

Nephew and filmmaker Asif Jah recalled that in everyday life, Rahi preferred saafgoi over pleasantries and pretence.

âOnce I wrote a poem and asked him to take a look at it. He remained silentâ¦ Eventually I asked him â Kaisi Lagi? And he bluntly repliedâ¦ wahiyat (absurd)â¦ disheartened I said â¦ âtheek hai phirâ¦ likhna chord deta hoonâ¦ he instantly deterred me and asked how I will improve if I quit so easily,â said Jah.

He also called Rahi as a man who followed his heart. âWhen Mamu came in touch with Nayyar Jahan, she was already married. Rahi was advised by friends and well-wishers to stay away from her and the controversy, but he did not budge and got married in 1966.





The hullaballoo contributed to his leaving Aligarh Muslim University, where he was working as a lecturer,â he said adding that he moved to Bombay thereafter.

A former student Nadeem Adhami loved his teacherâs wit. âUnka andaz bada dostana tha,â he said adding, âhe would crack jokes on himself which takes a big heart and an open mind.â

Rahi's student, Dr Nadeem Adhami

Citing a memory Adhami said: âRahi used to limp because of the polio inflicted legâ¦ but instead of being touchy about it, he saidâ¦ Kaun Kehta hai ki rahi langda hai; jo Marris Road (where Aligarh Muslim University Womenâs College is located) tak daud jaye wo langda ho hi nahi sakta.â

Urdu enthusiast and former chief secretary Anis Ansari remembered how students were mesmerised by his handsome personality. âPeople felt that khuda ne unko fursat se banaya thaâ¦ He was hard to ignore in a room filled with 40-50 people,â he said.

Verse to prose.

Razaâs persona followed him to the Bollywood. Writer and film maker Amit Khanna admitted that in his early years, he was not fully aware of Rahiâs literary contributions to Hindi and Urdu but deeply felt his intellectual streak.

âUrdu poet Majrooh Sultanpuri told me about his about Raza saabâs importance in literary circlesâ¦ But there was something scholarly in his bearing and Tehzeeb dripped from his words,â he said.

Not just in work, Raza left a lasting impression on people he met.

âA true literary maestro, Rahi Chacha was in a league of his own in both Urdu and Hindustani. He did not merely play with words; he had an extraordinary understanding of human expression and emotion that gave dialogues a soul,â said actor turned politician Raj Babbar who often turned to him for clearing doubts and followed his advice even when they did not make sense to him.

Real to reel

Film maker Subhash Ghai also swears that he can never forget Dr Rahi. âA witty man, he was like family to meâ¦ So, he had to push his pen to write the dialogues of my first film production Karz. But all his work was better than Karz,â Ghai wrote.

Calling Rahi his âManas Pitaâ and his visit to Ghazipur a pilgrimage, voice artist Harish Bhimani said: âlike a father he envisioned the birth of Samay (the narrator in Mahabharat) and shaped him in every episode like a mother.â

He also recalled how Rahiâs teaching never let success get into his head. âOnce he told me apni avaz se nahi andaz se logon ko apna banaoâ¦ and I follow this principle till date,â Bhimani said.

1959

To his niece Samar Rizwi, Raza is a jewel in her crown. âSome children are known by their family names while others became their family name. He is a jewel not just in the crown of our family but also that of Indian society who continues to sparkle,â she said.

âRahiâs writing combined Indianness with revolutionary thought and an uncompromising fight against casteism and communalism. He was deeply secular, and his command over Hindu mythology was remarkable,â said noted anthropologist Prof Nadeem Hasnain and close relative.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The love for Raza continues to linger, believes actor and producer, Rahul Mitra. âThe most striking thing about him is that he called himself the son of three mothers â Nafisa Begum (his biological mother), AMU his alma mater and Ganga the great river along which he lived,â he said.

Asif Azmi, convenor Maati Foundation.

The programme concluded with attendees lighting earthen lamps in Razaâs memory, reaffirming their commitment to keeping his literary legacy alive. âIdeas donât die when writers like Raza give them a life beyond their own,â said Asif Azmi, convenor of Maati Trust, which is organising 100 programmes to mark the occasion.

Calling those who draw inspiration from Rahiâs work his âintellectual heirsâ, Azmi said they had a responsibility to introduce his writing and ideas to the next generation.

World.title: Australia expands biometric requirements for visa applicants in India from October 26

World.title: SC rejects plea for CBI probe into ‘horse-trading’ post TN Assembly polls
World.content:
The Supreme Court on Monday (October 26, 2026) dismissed a petition seeking a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into allegations of “horse-trading” involving Tamil Nadu Minister and Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) general secretary N. Anand and four former AIADMK MLAs who shifted political allegiance to the ruling party after the State Assembly elections in May 2026.

A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant rejected the petition filed by Tamil Nadu resident M. Srinivasan, who alleged Mr. Anand and the four former AIADMK MLAs — K. Maragatham Kumaravel, S. Jayakumar, P. Sathyabama, and E. Subaya — had indulged in “horse-trading” to secure a majority in the Tamil Nadu Assembly.

Mr. Srinivasan, represented by advocate Achintya Tiwari, had sought directions for an investigation and the filing of a final report in a time-bound manner.

The petition had also sought the court to invoke its extraordinary powers under Article 142 of the Constitution to frame specific and stringent “rules” to prevent MLAs who have either been disqualified or have resigned from the Assembly without any “valid, material and justifiable” reason from contesting subsequent bypolls in the same constituencies.

The plea further sought directions to the Union government, the Election Commission of India and the State of Tamil Nadu to recover from the resigned MLAs the expenditure incurred for conducting the Assembly elections in their respective constituencies.

The petition also urged the court to direct the four former AIADMK MLAs to deposit the entire costs for the upcoming byelections in their respective constituencies.

TVK formed the government in the State with the help of the Indian National Congress, the Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi, the Indian Union Muslim League, the Communist Party of India and the Communist Party of India (Marxist).

During the ensuing floor test, 25 MLAs, including the four arraigned as respondents in the petition, had defied the party whip to support the TVK government.

World.title: Odisha’s contempt petition in Supreme Court over Kotia panchayat election | Explained
World.content:
The story so far: The Andhra Pradesh State Election Commission issued a notification on October 19, 2026, for elections to the Mandal Parishad Territorial Constituencies (MPTCs) and Zilla Parishad Territorial Constituencies (ZPTCs), scheduled for November 3.

The decision to hold the elections in the Kotia group of villages, whose jurisdiction has been disputed by Andhra Pradesh and Odisha since Independence, triggered protests across the political spectrum in Odisha.

The Biju Janata Dal (BJD), Congress, and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) accused Andhra Pradesh of undermining Odisha’s territorial integrity. The Odisha government said on October 23, 2026, that it had filed a contempt of court petition against the Andhra Pradesh government in the Supreme Court challenging the notification for the forthcoming election in Kotia.

Why Kotia is disputed?

As many as 21 villages in the Kotia group, under Pottangi Tahasil of Odisha’s Koraput district, have been at the centre of a territorial dispute with Andhra Pradesh since 1955.

According to an Odisha government brief on the dispute, Odisha exercised administrative control over these villages from 1936. The dispute surfaced in 1955, two years after the formation of Andhra Province, when Andhra Pradesh officials attempted to collect land revenue from the villages. Odisha protested through its Chief Secretary, but Andhra Pradesh countered that it had been collecting revenue there since 1947 and that residents had participated in the State’s 1954 elections.

In 1959, Andhra Pradesh cited a 1942 boundary demarcation by M. Gilby, Assistant Director of Survey, Madras Province, claiming it had been carried out with Odisha’s consent. Odisha rejected the claim, arguing that Gilby had wrongly assumed his demarcation conformed to the Government of India (Constitution of Orissa) Order, 1936. Both States held general elections in the disputed area in 1967.

Amid the impasse, the then Union Home Minister convened a conciliatory meeting on September 12, 1968. It failed to resolve the dispute, with the Minister reportedly observing that Odisha’s claim would be difficult to sustain in view of the acceptance of Gilby’s report.

The legal recourse

Odisha moved the Supreme Court under Article 131 of the Constitution on November 14, 1968. Talks between the two Chief Ministers in 1978 also proved inconclusive.

On March 30, 2006, the Supreme Court disposed of the original suit, holding that it lacked jurisdiction to adjudicate the dispute because of the proviso to Article 131. It directed that the status quo should be maintained until the dispute was taken up by an appropriate authority in accordance with law. According to legal experts, issues under Article 131 of the Constitution are resolved only by Parliament. Odisha’s review petition in 2006 and curative petition in 2007 were also dismissed, effectively closing the door to further judicial scrutiny through those proceedings.

The dispute resurfaced in 2021 when Andhra Pradesh, on February 13, 2021, notified a Gram Panchayat election in Phatusineri (Pattuchennuru). Odisha approached the Supreme Court with a contempt petition, alleging a violation of the status quo order. Andhra Pradesh subsequently notified elections to MPTC and ZPTC seats in Kotia, scheduled for April 8, 2021, prompting another contempt petition by Odisha seeking an injunction against the neighbouring State and its officials.

The two Chief Ministers met again in 2021 amid renewed tensions, but the talks skirted the contentious jurisdictional issue and ended with a general assurance of cooperation.

In 2023, Odisha again approached the Supreme Court seeking adjudication of the Kotia dispute. In the latest proceedings, Odisha has filed its response to objections raised by Andhra Pradesh.

Present contempt petition

Fabi Rasheed, Koraput Sub-Collector, said the District Collector filed a fresh contempt petition in the Supreme Court, alleging Andhra Pradesh violated the 2006 status quo order.

Meanwhile, a BJD delegation visited Kotia and criticised the Mohan Charan Majhi government, alleging that the Kotia issue had been completely mishandled by the administration. A Congress delegation led by its state president, Bhakta Charan Das, is scheduled to visit Kotia on Tuesday (October 27, 2026).

In order to win over the people of Kotia, both the Odisha and Andhra Pradesh governments are spending heavily. While the Odisha government is emphasising creating infrastructures such as opening educational institutes, laying roads and bridges and creating other government institutions, Andhra Pradesh is focusing on getting children of Kotia admitted in schools situated in its jurisdiction and distributing pensionary benefits.

World.title: Left leaders hail Lula’s fourth win in Brazil, say it offers hope to workers’ movements
